title: Emeka Egbuka has cleared concussion protocol, but will miss Sunday's game with a foot injury
summary: The Buccaneers will play without wide receiver Emeka Egbuka again this weekend.
full_text: The Buccaneers will play without wide receiver Emeka Egbuka again this weekend. Head coach Todd Bowles announced on Friday that Egbuka has been ruled out for their home matchup with the Falcons. Bowles said that Egbuka has cleared concussion protocol, but a foot injury will keep him from playing against their NFC South rivals. Egbuka did not play in last Sunday's win over the Panthers either. He has 28 catches for 240 yards and two touchdowns so far this season. Bowles provided a better update on safety Antoine Winfield. Winfield has missed the last three games with a rib injury, but he was a full participant in practice this week and is set to return to the lineup against Atlanta. Right tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) returned to practice and Bowles said he has a chance to play this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ja'Marr Chase set to play vs. Titans
summary: It looked like things were trending in the right direction for Ja'Marr Chase to play this weekend, and now that is officially the case.
full_text: It looked like things were trending in the right direction for Ja'Marr Chase to play this weekend, and now that is officially the case. Via multiple reporters, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said on Friday that Chase is good to go and will play against Tennessee on Sunday. Chase has been dealing with an ankle injury. He did not practice on Wednesday, but his designation also noted that he didn't practice for rest, implying that he'd likely be able to play. Chase has caught 32 passes for 351 yards with five touchdowns this season. But safety Kyle Dugger (quad) has been ruled out. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is questionable for the game.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Saquon Barkley is at Eagles practice Friday
summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's chances of playing against the Commanders on Sunday night are looking better on Friday.
full_text: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's chances of playing against the Commanders on Sunday night are looking better on Friday. Reporters at the open portion of Friday's practice said that Barkley was dressed and participating in the team's final workout of the week. Barkley did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. Barkley missed two games with a hamstring injury, but returned to action against the Cowboys in Week 7. He only played 10 snaps with a back injury given as the reason for his limited workload and the back issue was also part of this week's injury report. The Eagles will release injury designations for the Commanders game later on Friday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Acrisure Stadium will have a quick turnaround this weekend
summary: When Heinz Field opened in 2001, the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Pitt Panthers became roommates.
full_text: When Heinz Field opened in 2001, the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Pitt Panthers became roommates. Or, more accurately, partners in a timeshare. The Panthers use it several times a year. The Steelers use it several times a year. Sometimes, they use it on back-to-back days. More rarely, the turnaround is very quick. On Saturday night at 7:30 p.m. ET, Pitt hosts Georgia Tech. On Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET, the Steelers host the Browns. It will be plenty of work to convert the venue now known as Acrisure Stadium from its Pitt configuration to being Steelers-ready. It will put extra stress on the playing surface. Last year, there were constant concerns about the quality of the grass; Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers at one point called it " borderline unplayable ." A change in the construction of the field has caused those worries to subside in 2026. Still, this weekend's schedule cuts it as close as it ever will be cut. The Pitt game could have started earlier, obviously. The Steelers game potentially could have been moved later, but the league decided (after considering flexing the game between the 5-2 Browns and 5-2 Steelers to prime-time in place of the game between the 2-5 Eagles and 1-4-1 Commanders) to keep the game at 1:00 p.m. ET. Situations like this will be unavoidable whenever a college team and a pro team play their home games in the same building. Last year, former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger said Pitt should move out . That's how it was from 1970 through 2000, when the Steelers played at Three Rivers Stadium and Pitt played at Pitt Stadium. (Before Three Rivers opened, the Steelers split time between Pitt Stadium and Forbes Field.) Steelers owner Art Rooney II hasn’t ruled out ditching grass altogether for artificial turf, if the current experiment doesn't work. This weekend, the new field will be put to its biggest test yet.
author: Mike Florio

title: Osi Umenyiora on the journey that led to NFL Africa
summary: Osi Umenyiora reflects on the unlikely path that inspired NFL Africa.
full_text: Umenyiora on how Nigerian culture has shaped life Osi Umenyiora joins By Way of Africa to discuss growing up in Nigeria, how Nigerian culture and values have shaped him, and the importance of giving back. Born in London and spending his formative years in Nigeria, Osi Umenyiora had never even heard of American football until he moved to the U.S. as a teenager. After moving to Auburn, Alabama, he took up the sport in high school and eventually earned an opportunity at Troy University. He was drafted by the New York Giants in 2003 and went on to win Super Bowls XLII and XLVI. Umenyiora spent ten years with the Giants and two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons before retiring in 2015. The rest, as they say, is history. Yet Umenyiora's story was far from over. "My whole story has just been one of pure fortune, and so I looked at it like, 'Okay, I've been given this opportunity, and now I'm working with the NFL. How can I now give this opportunity to more people?'" That's where an e-mail to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell snowballed into NFL Africa, the league's initiative to grow the game on the continent and perhaps Umenyiora's most impactful chapter yet. In the conversation below, part of NBC Sports' By Way of Africa series , Umenyiora reflects on his childhood in Nigeria, the story behind NFL Africa's creation, and what the initiative's growth means to him. *This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Mary Omatiga: Osi, you were born in London, but I read that you lived in Nigeria from age 7 to 14. What memories come to mind when you think of your childhood there? Osi Umenyiora: Nigeria to me is a very special place. It's a place that I hope to one day return to and live. Growing up there meant so much to me. My family being there, coming back there. Because of the way we were raised — and we were raised in a very Nigerian way — when I got there, the only difference really was the climate. Other than that, it was basically the same things going on. But overall, it was just a really, really great experience and time in my life. It's something that I'll never forget and something that I cherish. Courtesy of Osi Umenyiora How did that time there shape you into who you are today? Umenyiora: In a multitude of ways. The environment there teaches you how to survive first and foremost. It instills toughness. There are so many things that you see there that, whenever you leave that environment, the ability to thrive in those situations, you can carry them with you pretty much anywhere. I know they say that if you can make it in New York, you can make it anywhere, but really, it's if you can make it in Lagos, Nigeria, you can pretty much make it anywhere. Courtesy of Osi Umenyiora Names can carry so much weight in African culture. What’s your full Nigerian name and what does it translate to? Umenyiora: Ogemdi Ositadinma Iloabuchi Umenyiora . My father would actually name us after periods in his life. So Ogemdi means 'My time is now'. Ositadinma means, 'From today, things will be good', and Iloabuchi basically means, 'The heart of who is God'. So it's three different names. Then one of [my dad's] friends went to him and was like, 'You have four sons at this point, and none of them are named after you. Why don't you name one of your sons after you?' So he just started calling me Osi randomly when I was two years old and that's how I got the name. But my first name is actually Ogemdi. How do you think the meaning of your name has played out in your life? Umenyiora: First and foremost, just understanding that my father would name all his children — and he had ten of them — after different periods of his life. I think it was a very special and sentimental thing for us because a lot of times you don't really know the meaning of your names, or people just randomly call their children whatever. But the fact that my father took the time to think about each one of his children and specifically name us after something that happened translates, and it just gives your name that much more pride and that much more meaning. Also, the thing about Nigerian names is you can tell where somebody's from within Nigeria just by hearing their name, which is kind of unique to a lot of people. So I can hear somebody's name, and I'll be like, 'Okay, this guy is Fulani, or he's Hausa, Yoruba, or Igbo, simply by hearing their name. The name really is an identifier. It's a marker of who you are, where you come from, and a lot of times it actually carries your whole family history with you. Courtesy of Osi Umenyiora You are Igbo. Can you talk about the values and traditions that come from your culture that have led to your success on and off the field? Umenyiora: Being from the Igbo tribe, we're very, very proud people. Obviously, there was a situation back in the '60s and '70s where Nigeria fought a war. Biafra was trying to secede from Nigeria. It didn't work out well, but the Igbo people were the main people who were in that. So, just being a part of that tribe, I would say I find it interesting how I don't really consider myself Igbo until I get to Nigeria. Because outside of Nigeria, you're just Nigerian. Everybody is cool. They're family. You're just one. But the minute you go back into Nigeria, that's when you become either Igbo, Hausa, Yoruba, Fulani, Ijaw, Efik, Ibibio — one of those tribes. To be honest, I wish that we would take more of the approach that we have outside of Nigeria into Nigeria, so we can be more cohesive and really move as one within the country. Because outside of the country, my best friends are Yoruba, Hausa, it doesn't really matter until you go back in. I wish we would stop that. You are a two-time Super Bowl champion, a New York Giants legend. So much of your journey was shaped by hard work and values, but your journey is also a testament to the power of having someone believe in you and take a chance on you. How has that inspired this chapter of your life as the lead for NFL Africa? Umenyiora: Oh, massively! A lot of times, people can look at things that they do and things that they accomplish and think that they're the ones who did it. For me, I've never thought that way. I always knew that I was very fortunate. I was lucky to have the parents that I did who were able to send me to America. I was lucky to be able to start playing the game of football, which gave me the opportunity to get a scholarship and then go on to the NFL. My whole story has just been one of pure fortune, and so I looked at it like, 'Okay, I've been given this opportunity, and now I'm working with the NFL. How can I now give this opportunity to more people?' Because there are so many people, especially when I was growing up, who were more talented than me, had much more ability than me, but they just didn't have the parents, or they didn't have the [opportunities]. So now that I'm in a position to help, why would I not try to put those people in the exact same position that I'm in? As opposed to just going back there and doing the regular things. 'Oh, we're going to do a charity here. We're going to do this and that.' Cool. I get all that, but for me, it was about this: There are tremendous athletes there. There are people there with real ability, and all they need is just a pathway. All they need is just somebody to hold the door open for them, so they can come and make the best of their abilities. For me, the idea that I had this opportunity to do something like that, given the fact that I was given that exact same opportunity, was monumental, and it's something that I knew that I had to do. It's been brewing for 20 years. I know people see what's going on now, but this is something that has been a long journey, a long process, and is just now starting to come to fruition. NFL Tell me about the e-mail you sent to Roger Goodell that started that long process. Umenyiora: Roger is my guy. We spent quite a bit of time together, and so, just the understanding of the NFL trying…
author: Mary Omatiga

title: NFLPA names Eagles S Michael Carter their Community MVP for Week 8
summary: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Eagles safety Michael Carter has been named their Community MVP for Week 8.
full_text: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Eagles safety Michael Carter has been named their Community MVP for Week 8. Carter is being honored after he and his foundation hosted a Baby Shower on the Block event. The event welcomed 40 expectant and new mothers as well as their families for educational panels focused on mental health, prenatal care, maternal care and fatherhood. The attendees also received supplies to help care for their children. “Being named the NFLPA Community MVP means everything to me,” Carter said. “Maternal health is not talked about enough, especially in communities where families are already navigating so much. Baby Shower on the Block was about meeting moms where they are — with real resources, real information and real support. This recognition belongs to every family who showed up and every partner who made it possible." The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to Carter's foundation. He will also join the other weekly MVPs in being eligible for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ryan Poles: "F them picks" is really not what we're about
summary: The Bears completed a blockbuster midseason trade, bringing in defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons for a package that included two first-round picks.
full_text: The Bears completed a blockbuster midseason trade, bringing in defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons for a package that included two first-round picks. General Manager Ryan Poles told reporters in a Friday press conference that given what Simmons meant to the Titans, he didn’t necessarily think the franchise would part with him. But the club believes the defensive tackle can help Chicago now and into the future, given that he’s already under contract through 2030. But Poles also wanted to make it clear that the franchise is being measured with its approach to utilizing picks to acquire premium players. “One thing I want to hit, I know it’s kind of a joke that goes around, but, ‘F them picks’ is like a big thing — that’s really not what we’re about ,” Poles said. “I know it took a lot to get this done, but we absolutely believe that the draft and bringing [in] young talent is the way you sustain success around here. “I’m challenging myself and our crew, for the picks that we do have, we have to hit. We have to be great with our undrafted free agent process. And whatever tier of free agency we’re working in, which we’ll have constraints, we have to hit there, too.” But Simmons is expected to make the Bears better on and off the field, with Poles expressing a belief in how the veteran defender can positively impact the club’s culture. “His intensity that he brings to the football field, he has a certain standard of how you play this game,” Poles said. “He lives that. He models that behavior. I think that when you don’t live that, he’s a guy that makes it a little bit uncomfortable for you, too, which is important. I don’t know that we have that right now, and we do with him, adding him. “When your phone blows up, and you have coaches, players, people that have been with him that talk about what he means to a football team, to the culture, you know exactly what he’s going to do.” Simmons recorded a career-high 11.0 sacks last season — the first time he’d reached double-digit sacks in his career. He has tallied 4.0 sacks, six tackles for loss, and nine QB hits in seven games so far in 2026. Poles noted that he's assuming Simmons will play in Monday night's matchup with the Seahawks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Titans sign DT Timmy Horne to 53-man roster
summary: The Titans filled the opening on their 53-man roster that was created by Thursday's trade of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears.
full_text: The Titans filled the opening on their 53-man roster that was created by Thursday's trade of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears. They announced that they have signed defensive tackle Timmy Horne off of the practice squad. Horne was released when the Titans claimed defensive tackle Jonah Laulu off of waivers and he returned to the practice squad the next day. Horne had five tackles in two appearances for the team this month. He previously played in 21 games for the Falcons and Giants and had 31 tackles in those appearances. The Titans also announced that they have signed linebacker Dominique Hampton to their practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills' Spencer Brown "took enough drugs to sedate a small elephant" to play with back injury
summary: Bills right tackle Spencer Brown says he needed to be heavily medicated to play in Week 6 against the Raiders after suffering a back injury in Week 5 against the Rams.
full_text: Bills right tackle Spencer Brown says he needed to be heavily medicated to play in Week 6 against the Raiders after suffering a back injury in Week 5 against the Rams. Asked about his presence on the injury report, Brown says it stemmed from his back but wouldn't keep him off the field. "Just lingering stuff from what's happened to me the last couple weeks here. And what happened in that LA game just kind of got nicked up and then I took enough drugs to sedate a small elephant when I was in LA," Brown said. Reporters chuckled at that description, but Brown said it's just a part of life for an NFL player. "Everybody's laughing. It's protocol. NFL signed off on it, so it's OK," Brown said. "But yeah, just took care of the body the best way I knew how and got through the Vegas game and played pretty well and got on the bye week and kind of bit me in the butt a little bit. So, just taking it easy and smart." Brown said if he's physically capable of getting on the field, he'll always play and make no excuses. "I do pride myself on being ready every single day," Brown said. "When I'm out there, I'm out there. There's not going to be any, 'He's nicked up, he's got this going on, that's why he's not playing very well.' That's not me at all. If I'm out there in between the lines, I'm good enough to go." No one can question Brown's toughness, but it's fair to question whether it's a good idea for the NFL to allow players to play when they're injured badly enough that they need that kind of medication. The league is facing renewed scrutiny in recent weeks for issues including Jalen Hurts' blood clot and Christian Watson returning to Thursday night's game after going to the hospital with a broken rib. Perhaps players on enough drugs to sedate a small elephant should be given the day off.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Xavier McKinney says he was fined for criticizing officials after Packers-Lions game
summary: After Sunday's loss to the Lions, Packers safety Xavier McKinney had some things to say about the officiating.
full_text: After Sunday's loss to the Lions, Packers safety Xavier McKinney had some things to say about the officiating. And he knew he was inviting a fine. After Thursday night's win over the Panthers, McKinney confirmed that he was fined. Via Rob Demovsky of ESPN, McKinney didn't disclose the specific amount. He did say it wasn't less than the minimum of $25,000. " I make enough money so I’ll be OK ," McKinney said. McKinney said it was worth it to support the team. Meanwhile, it's unknown whether Raiders minority owner Tom Brady was fined for his criticism of the officials during that same game. Through it all, the NFL essentially has conceded that referee Alex Moore's crew didn't meet the standard, by flexing Moore's crew out of Sunday night's game between the Eagles and Commanders.
author: Mike Florio

title: David Bailey doubtful, Breece Hall questionable for Sunday vs. Raiders
summary: The Jets are unlikely to have one of their top young defensive players when they host the Raiders on Sunday.
full_text: The Jets are unlikely to have one of their top young defensive players when they host the Raiders on Sunday. Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters in his Friday press conference that edge rusher David Bailey will not practice on Friday and is doubtful for the game. Bailey is dealing with a groin injury and has not practiced this week. The No. 2 overall pick of this year’s draft, Bailey has registered 5.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, and nine QB hits so far this season. He also has three forced fumbles. Running back Breece Hall (quad) will once again be limited in practice on Friday and is questionable for Sunday’s game. He has been limited in practice all week. Offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee) will also be questionable. Defensive lineman T’Vondre Sweat (knee) has been ruled out.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Panthers fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero
summary: At 3-4, Carolina shakes up the defensive side of the ball.
full_text: Panthers owner David Tepper had big expectations for his team in 2026. With a 3-4 record after seven games, the team is making some big changes. The Panthers have announced the terminations of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. Moving forward, defensive line coach Todd Wash will serve as defensive coordinator and call the defensive plays. Outside linebackers coach/run game specialist AC Carter will also coach the defensive line, and secondary coach Renaldo Hill will continue to oversee the defensive backs. Evero, 45, had worked for the Panthers since 2023, arriving as a member of Frank Reich's staff. Evero remained in place after the hiring of Dave Canales in 2024. In 2022, Evero was the defensive coordinator of the Broncos. His first job as an NFL position coach came in 2017, when Rams coach Sean McVay hired Evero to serve as safeties coach on McVay's initial staff. Evero was secondary coach and passing game coordinator for the Rams in 2021, which resulted in a Super Bowl win. Through it all, the Panthers remain tied for first place with the Falcons in the NFC South.
author: Mike Florio

title: Christian Watson cleared, on his way back to Lambeau from hospital
summary: The Packers wide receiver was injured in the second quarter.
full_text: Packers wide receiver Christian Watson was cleared at a local hospital and is on his way back to Lambeau Field, Kaylee Hartung of Amazon Prime reports. The Packers still list Watson as questionable to return. Watson was injured on a 53-yard reception with 9:11 remaining in the first half. He appeared on land on the ball as Panthers cornerback Will Lee landed on him. Watson was sent in an ambulance to a hospital for further evaluation, with the sternoclavicular joint as a possible concern. The Packers initially listed Watson as questionable to return with a chest injury. He has six catches for 100 yards tonight, giving him a career-high 695 receiving yards for the season. The Panthers have ruled out Lee with a hamstring injury. He was injured on the same play as Watson. The Packers have ruled out tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Packers running back Josh Jacobs scored on a 4-yard reception from Jordan Love with 7:30 remaining in the third quarter to take a 27-10 lead. UPDATE 10:25 P.M. ET : Watson has returned to the game.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jared Verse returns to practice, Tytus Howard remains sidelined
summary: Jared Verse was back on the practice field for the Browns on Thursday as they continue to prepare for Sunday's matchup with the Steelers.
full_text: Jared Verse was back on the practice field for the Browns on Thursday as they continue to prepare for Sunday's matchup with the Steelers. Verse (knee) was a limited participant in the session after he was sidelined on Wednesday. Verse has registered 17 total tackles, four tackles for loss, and five QB hits so far in 2026. Center Elgton Jenkins (knee) also returned to practice in a limited capacity. Right tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) did not practice for the second consecutive day. Running back Dylan Sampson (knee) was upgraded from limited to full. The rest of Cleveland’s injury report remained the same as Wednesday. Safety Grant Delpit (neck), defensive tackle Mason Graham (ankle), defensive tackle Mike Hall (ankle), cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring), safety Daniel Thomas (ankle), and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) were all limited.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Ben Johnson is going for it on fourth down even more than Dan Campbell
summary: Lions head coach Dan Campbell has earned a reputation as one of the NFL's most aggressive coaches on fourth downs, a reputation that he bolstered on Sunday with a surprising fourth down attempt at his own 24-yard line late in the fourth quarter against the Packers.
full_text: Lions head coach Dan Campbell has earned a reputation as one of the NFL’s most aggressive coaches on fourth downs , a reputation that he bolstered on Sunday with a surprising fourth down attempt at his own 24-yard line late in the fourth quarter against the Packers. But it's one of Campbell's former assistants who is going for it on fourth down more than any other coach in the NFL. Bears head coach Ben Johnson has had his team go for it on fourth down 17 times this season, the most in the NFL. Campbell's Lions, on the other hand, have gone for it on fourth down 13 times, tied for the sixth-most in the NFL. The Lions have punted twice more than the Bears have, while the Bears have attempted five more field goals than the Lions have. The two teams are similar in all three categories of decisions a coach can make on fourth down, but it's noteworthy that it's Johnson who has gone for it the most in the league so far this season. Before Campbell's surprising decision on Sunday against the Packers, the most controversial fourth down decision of this NFL season may have been the first fourth down decision Johnson made this season, when the Bears went for it on fourth-and-1 from their own 21-yard line against the Panthers in Week 1. Caleb Williams was stopped for no gain, but the Bears still won the game, and afterward Johnson said the call was part of his overall aggressive approach to trying to field the highest-scoring offense in the NFL. Confidence in their offense is one thing Campbell and Johnson have in common. They'd rather have the game in the hands of their playmakers than on the feet of their kickers.
author: Michael David Smith

title: New report paints fuller picture of the Troy Aikman, Joe Buck rift
summary: The inevitable Saturday Night Live skit should be very entertaining.
full_text: ' The inevitable Saturday Night Live skit should be very entertaining. But maybe not as entertaining as the reality. With the dysfunction between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck continuing to simmer, Andrew Marchand of The Athletic has provided the clearest and most comprehensive details yet as to what happened, in a lengthy article that delves into the nooks and crannies of a 25-year relationship gone sour. There's a lot there, and it's worth reading the whole thing. For these purposes, here are the facts that seemed to be the most significant. First, Marchand reports that, before the Week 5 Monday night game in L.A. between the Bills and the Rams, ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro "had a tense one-hour chat" with Aikman. Per the report, Aikman and Pitaro "discussed the rupture" between Aikman and Buck, "and whether there is a future for the duo." “Could you still work with Joe?” Pitaro asked Aikman. Aikman said he could. But then came the verbal altercation between Buck and Aikman, with Buck saying to Aikman (per Marchand), "You are not going to fucking talk to me?” Marchand reports that Aikman believed Buck was hoping to bait Aikman into a backlash that would leave Buck looking like "the good guy." During their back-and-forth, Buck reportedly said to Aikman, “I’m not the reason you don’t have a contract.” Aikman reportedly suggested that Buck manipulated the constant turnover in the ranks of Monday Night Football producers and directors, telling Buck, "I never thought you'd do it to me." (At some point, Aikman reportedly said more pointedly to Buck, per Dylan Byers of Puck , " You fucked me over! ") Said Buck of the now-former producers and directors, “They got rid of them because you were screaming at them.” The hard feelings, per Marchand, came from Aikman's perception that Buck and ESPN secretly worked out a new contract "in the early spring" while Aikman was left to wait. That said, Marchand points out that Aikman agreed to leave Fox for ESPN at a time when it wasn't clear whether Buck would be able to follow him to Monday night. It's unclear when Buck and ESPN specifically did their deal. In mid-April, Buck spoke as if he didn’t have a new contract . An August report from Front Office Sports created the clear impression that neither Buck nor Aikman had a new contract, and that their mutual agency (CAA) possibly would approach the negotiations as a package deal . And while, as John Ourand of Puck has reported, Aikman's camp at one point sought an increase from $18 million per year to $30 million (thanks to Tom Brady's top-of-market $37.5 million annual pay), Marchand reports that Aikman eventually was willing to take the same 18-percent increase Buck received. ESPN passed. As Marchand explains it, ESPN has now chosen not to negotiate with Aikman because: (1) it doesn't want to further invest in a relationship gone sour; (2) the network is generally in cost-cutting mode (except when it isn't); and (3) ESPN believes "there is depth in the NFL game-analyst market." Aikman's side role with the Dolphins, per Marchand, isn't a factor in ESPN's reluctance to proceed. However, Aikman reportedly concedes that he should have told Pitaro about his plan to work for the Dolphins before embarking on the creation of an obvious conflict of interest. From ESPN's perspective, the negotiations are simply "paused." Marchand reports that ESPN does not have a plan in place for a post-Aikman Monday night booth. Given that ESPN believes "there is depth in the NFL game-analyst market," does it need one? ESPN likely realizes that, if it makes a decision after Super Bowl LXI to move on from Aikman, his seat will be easily filled. Through it all, Buck and Aikman share close quarters for three hours or more every Monday night. Plenty of people are studying all words uttered and every glimpse of facial expressions and body language in search of evidence of a potential on-air fracas to come. For now, Aikman sees the handwriting on the wall. He said this week there's a " 50-50 chance " he won't be working in TV next year. His public comments about possibly working for the Cowboys (which he now says he regrets ) make it clear that he's available and willing to explore a full-time football role with one of the various 32 NFL franchises. However it plays out, it's unprecedented to have a prime-time network broadcast team in the throes of such public acrimony. On one hand, it tarnishes ESPN's first-ever Super Bowl season. On the other hand, it adds another layer of reality show to the ultimate reality show that is the NFL.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Bears are close to a deal to stay in Illinois
summary: So much for Hammond, Indiana.
full_text: The Bears can finally drop the Hammond facade. After months of claiming that they’re solely focused on building a new stadium in Indiana, the bluff has worked. Via Greg Hinz of Crain's Chicago Business , the Bears are " close to a deal that would keep them in Illinois ." A vote in the Illinois legislature could come as soon as November. The new venue would "most likely" be built in Arlington Heights, not Chicago. But Illinois is still Illinois. And it's not Indiana. The new law would allow any municipality (including Chicago) to form an authority that would own and operate the stadium, with no property taxes being paid. Taxpayers would be responsible only for new roads and other infrastructure. Hinz also reports that recent progress has been fueled by the involvement of Bears minority owner Pat Ryan. Commissioner Roger Goodell also has gotten involved, with majority owner George McCaskey and president/CEO Kevin Warren — who said in August that Hammond, Indiana was the team's " sole focus " — taking a backseat. It's still not done, but it's the biggest indication yet that the Bears won't be leaving Illinois. Even after repeatedly saying they would.
author: Mike Florio

title: Robert Saleh: Titans aren't shopping anyone, but when you're 1-6 teams call you
summary: Titans head coach Robert Saleh says his team will not hold a fire sale ahead of the trade deadline.
full_text: Titans head coach Robert Saleh says his team will not hold a fire sale ahead of the trade deadline. But the offer they got from the Bears for defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons was too good to pass up. The Bears traded their next two first-round draft picks to the Titans for Simmons, and Saleh said that a team in the Titans' position couldn't realistically have passed that up. "No one's shopping any of our guys, but like I told our guys, when you don't close out games, and you're standing here at 1-6, teams are going to start fishing," Saleh said. "And eventually a team threw a hook big enough that I don't think any of us could've said no to." Saleh said he considers Simmons "by far" the best defensive tackle in the NFL and hates to see him go. "It's tough. Jeff is an elite football player and he's an even better person," Saleh said. "He's an elite leader. I've been outspoken on that. It sucks. Everything about it sucks. Unfortunately, necessary." Saleh declined to answer when asked what he said to Simmons before he left the Titans' facility for the last time. "I'll keep that between me and him," Saleh said. "Very, very, very tough conversation." It was a tough decision for the Titans, but in the long run it may prove to be the correct decision. Those two first-round picks may help the Titans build a winning team, something they don't have now.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Colts sign OT Charlie Heck to 53-man roster
summary: The Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks this week and they filled the opening that move created on their roster on Thursday.
full_text: The Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks this week and they filled the opening that move created on their roster on Thursday. They announced that they have signed free agent offensive tackle Charlie Heck to their 53-man roster. Heck was a 2020 fourth-round pick by the Texans and he spent four years in Houston before moving on to stints with the Cardinals, 49ers and Buccaneers. He went to camp with the Dolphins this summer, but failed to make the team. Heck made 21 starts with the Texans and has started 29 of the 67 games he's played in over the course of his career.
author: Josh Alper

title: Christian Watson spat up blood, broke a rib, went to the hospital and returned to the game
summary: Watson left Lambeau Field in an ambulance, spent an hour getting checked at the hospital, and then rode in an ambulance back to the stadium and played again.
full_text: Packers wide receiver Christian Watson left Lambeau Field in an ambulance on Thursday night after breaking a rib and spitting up blood, but he later returned to the field and said after the game that he never doubted whether he should play through it. "I was spitting up some blood or something like that, so the doctor said I had to go get a CT," Watson said. "I was trying to beg him to not make me do that. I got a rib, that's all, but the other stuff was good. No internal bleeding, nothing like that." Watson said he would always play through pain if he possibly could. "Before I even left I wanted to get back out there," Watson said. "This means everything to me, to be out there on the football field. I've had injuries I was not able to go on the field for, and I've missed significant time due to injuries, so any chance I get to go out there on the football field, I'm going to be out there on the football field." Watson finished the game with eight catches for 113 yards: Six catches for 100 yards before going to the hospital, and two catches for 13 yards after returning from the hospital. Watson said his philosophy is simple: "If you can get up, you've got to get up."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Josh Jacobs denies he was mimicking himself in handcuffs in touchdown celebration
summary: After scoring a touchdown on Thursday night, Packers running back Josh Jacobs put his hands behind his back, which many observers interpreted as mimicking himself in handcuffs.
full_text: '' After scoring a touchdown on Thursday night, Packers running back Josh Jacobs put his hands behind his back, which many observers interpreted as mimicking himself in handcuffs. Which would be in poor taste, given that Jacobs is playing only his second game of the season after he was put on paid leave following a no contest plea in connection with a domestic violence accusation brought by his girlfriend. Jacobs denied that's what he was doing. Jacobs said the broadcast of Thursday night's game didn't show his full touchdown celebration, which he and teammate Savion Williams planned, and which was inspired by a gospel song. "They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said. "Shit, it was fuckin' one second that they just showed me. But anyways, me and Savion came up with the celebration, if they would have seen the whole celebration. Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was gonna thank God, that's what I did last week. Second was going to be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was gonna be the next celebration. It's a correlation. The media is gonna run with it. They're gonna make it something that it wasn't. But it is what it is." Although Jacobs' paid leave is over, he remains subject to a potential unpaid suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bryce Young says knee is "fine" after loss to Packers
summary: Panthers quarterback Bryce Young has been on the injury report since hurting his left knee during the team's Week 3 loss to the Browns and he was asked if it was bothering him after Thursday night's game in Green Bay.
full_text: Panthers quarterback Bryce Young has been on the injury report since hurting his left knee during the team's Week 3 loss to the Browns and he was asked if it was bothering him after Thursday night's game in Green Bay. Young was sacked six times, hit nine times, had passes batted down at the line and threw an interception while being pressured regularly in 27-19 loss to the Packers. The questions came because Young had little luck evading pressure which head coach Dave Canales said "maybe" was related to the knee issue, but Young waved that off when he spoke to reporters. "Yeah, I’m fine ," Young said, via the team's website. "Everyone's dealing with something at this point in the year. It's football. Nothing like that is an excuse; go out there and play the game. I'm blessed to be able to do that. That's all that matters." The quarterback wasn't helped by the fact that the Panthers were forced to do more shuffling on the offensive line. Right tackle Taylor Moton went on injured reserve this week and left guard Damien Lewis was inactive, which led to Monroe Freeling and Corey Bullock starting up front. Bullock had to leave the game with a quad injury and Jake Curhan entered as the Panthers continued to patch things together on the fly in front of Young. It didn't work on Thursday and the Panthers will try and come up with something better when they try to snap their losing streak at home against the Broncos in Week 9.
author: Josh Alper

title: Thursday Night Football: Packers hold on for 27-19 win over Panthers
summary: The Packers improved to 5-3 despite a sluggish fourth quarter.
full_text: The Milwaukee Brewers celebrated their World Series with a trip to Lambeau Field. The Packers joined in the celebration with a 27-19 victory over the Panthers. It was closer than it should have been. Trey Smack missed an extra point; the Packers turned it over three times, including a fumbled kickoff; and Green Bay let Carolina climb back into it after leading 27-10 midway through the third quarter. It's the same problems the Packers have faced over the past two seasons — poor special teams play and choking big leads. The Panthers outgained the Packers 109 to 32 in the fourth quarter. The Packers didn't blow this one, though, moving to 5-3. The Panthers fell to 3-4. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw incomplete on fourth-and-5 at midfield with 2:41 left in their best chance for a comeback. Packers wide receiver Christian Watson left in an ambulance for a local hospital with 9:11 remaining in the first half. He had his chest injury examined there, and doctors cleared him to return. Watson returned to Lambeau Field in the passenger seat of the ambulance and had a clutch 7-yard reception on third-and-2 with 2:33 left. It allowed the Packers to run down the clock, with Carolina getting the ball back with only 22 seconds left. Young was sacked six times, including by rookie Dani Dennis-Sutton with four seconds remaining. Young, who was hit nine times, was 23-of-41 for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Chuba Hubbard had 22 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown and seven catches for 38 yards. Tetairoa McMillan had six catches for 58 yards. Ryan Fitzgerald made field goals of 39 and 50 yards. The Packers outgained the Panthers 354 to 258. Love finished 30-of-41 for 288 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. His touchdowns covered 12 yards to Tucker Kraft, 24 yards to Matthew Golden and 4 yards to Josh Jacobs. Jacobs also scored on a 1-yard run. Jacobs rushed for 39 yards on 21 carries and caught six passes for 13 yards. Watson had eight catches for 113 yards and Golden seven for 79. Packers wide receiver Coleman Owen fumbled the opening kickoff, and Watson lost a fumble in the first half. The Panthers, though, got only a field goal out of the three takeaways.
author: Charean Williams

title: Grey Zabel: Move to right guard will be "such a growing experience"
summary: The Seahawks hope their trade for Quenton Nelson will have an impact on their entire offense over the rest of the season and it will have an immediate impact on two of his new teammates.
full_text: '' The Seahawks hope their trade for Quenton Nelson will have an impact on their entire offense over the rest of the season and it will have an immediate impact on two of his new teammates. Anthony Bradford is heading to the bench because the team is moving Grey Zabel from left guard to right guard to allow Nelson to remain in the position he's played for his entire NFL career. On Thursday, Zabel admitted to "a lot of emotions" about the change but said that the prevailing one is that it will allow him to grow as a player. "At the end of the day, I'll do whatever's best for the team ," Zabel said, via the team's website. "Get to learn from an unbelievable player, person, leader, as Q is. And at the end of the day, it's going to be such a growing experience for me, kind of move positions as well as be able to learn from a guy like that. And at the end of the day, just become a better football player." Picking up the nuances of a different position in a couple of days isn't the easiest of asks, but Zabel will have to do it and he could be there for a while. Nelson's in the final year of his contract and a new deal with the Seahawks will leave the right side as Zabel's domain for quite some time.
author: Josh Alper

author: Michael David Smith

title: Jeffery Simmons, Quenton Nelson will renew their rivalry at Bears-Seahawks Monday night
summary: Nelson vs. Simmons will be the most-watched offensive lineman vs. defensive lineman battle of this NFL season, as two All-Pros go at it again on new teams.
full_text: '' Quenton Nelson knows how hard it is to block Jeffery Simmons. When Nelson was a guard for the Colts and Simmons was a defensive tackle for the Titans, the two played against each other 13 times. And when Nelson got traded to the Seahawks on Tuesday, he thought he was going to get a break from facing Simmons. That didn't happen. Shortly after Nelson got traded to the Seahawks, Simmons got traded to the Bears. Who play the Seahawks on Monday night, in the first game for both players on their new teams. Nelson said he considers Simmons one of the best opponents he's faced, and he's ready for a big challenge when the Bears visit Seattle on Monday night. "He's an amazing football player and competitor. I was like, Man, can't get away from this guy. It'll be another battle against him this week," Nelson said. Nelson vs. Simmons will be the most-watched offensive lineman vs. defensive lineman battle of this NFL season, as two All-Pros go at it again, now on new teams with Super Bowl aspirations.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Aaron Donald isn't bothered by not having a sack since he returned to the Rams
summary: In five games played since he emerged from a two-year retirement, Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has yet to record a sack.
full_text: In five games played since he emerged from a two-year retirement, Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has yet to record a sack. During his weekly press conference on Thursday, Donald was asked whether that bothers him. “No. I didn't come back for individual stats," Donald told reporters. "I would love to have some stats, but I'm here to just play the game. When the plays present themselves, take advantage of it, try to get my plays, but my main focus is trying to find ways to help this team win. That's the goal. I didn't come back to try to earn individual accolades or anything. I did that, accomplished that. It doesn't excite me. The only thing that excites me is winning so I’m just playing a football game, trying to do what I can to help this team. As long as we win, I can build off everything else and get myself better off that.” The Rams have won only three of seven games, and Donald has yet to play with Myles Garrett. Even though it was the trade that brought Garrett to the Rams that lit the fuse to get Donald to return. Against the Raiders in Week 7, Donald was on the field for 74 percent of the Rams' defensive snaps. It was his highest rate of the season, and the more he's on the field, the more likely he'll be to get some of those stats he'd love to have — even if winning continues to be the focus. The Rams should get their fourth win of the season on Sunday, against the 0-6 Chargers. If they don't, the Rams will be 3-5 through eight games and dangerously close to having too many losses to play beyond Week 18.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers close to within 27-19 of Packers
summary: The Packers led 27-10 midway through the third quarter.
full_text: The Packers led 27-10 midway through the third quarter. They lead only 27-19 with 5:37 left. Carolina got a 50-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald with 4:07 left in the third quarter. Two drives later, the Panthers were within one score. Jalen Coker caught a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young on fourth-and-3. They also converted two third downs during the 12-play, 70-yard drive. The 2-point try failed as Bryce Young's pass was deflected. Young is 21-of-37 for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception.
author: Charean Williams

title: Troy Aikman says it was "unfair" for him to back Jerry Jones "into a corner"
summary: ESPN's Troy Aikman has had plenty to say recently about his uncertain professional future.
full_text: ' ESPN's Troy Aikman has had plenty to say recently about his uncertain professional future. On Thursday, he acknowledged that he may have said too much. Via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing , Aikman expressed some regret during a Thursday appearance on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas regarding comments about potentially working for the Cowboys. “The last thing that I want is — I was answering a question, and I think it’s really unfair to Jerry that he then has to answer these questions,” Aikman said. “As far as, ‘Hey, would you bring Troy back, or would you have a role for him?’ I mean there’s no real good answer that he can give.” Aikman said he raised the issue with Jones in Philadelphia on Monday night, where Aikman called the game between the Eagles and the Cowboys. “We briefly touched on it just because I felt that maybe I backed him into a corner that he didn’t deserve to be backed into," Aikman said. "He didn’t ask for it. And so, we’re clear on that. He totally understood, and yet, he was very complimentary if something like that were to ever take place with the idea that we’re not having those conversations at this time.” Aikman is in an awkward spot of his own. He senses that ESPN doesn't want to bring him back next year. He pegs his chances of having a job in TV next year at " 50-50 ." Part of his own personal coping mechanism seems to be talking about the fact that he feels his 25-year broadcasting career slipping through his fingers. Aikman now realizes that, in recently talking about possibly working for the Cowboys , he has created a scenario in which Jones will be asked about Aikman possibly working for the Cowboys. Which happened on Tuesday , given that Jones does two radio spots of his own every week on 105.3 The Fan. Still, Aikman's latest comments are all part of the dance aimed at potentially laying the foundation for Aikman, who was and by all indications still is working for the Dolphins, potentially joining forces with Jerry in an effort to finally put together a team that can possibly get back to the NFC Championship, for the first time since 1995.
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Packers lead Panthers 20-10 at halftime
summary: The Packers have outgained the Panthers 227 to 87.
full_text: The Packers have two turnovers and a missed extra point. They lead the Panthers 20-10 at halftime. Green Bay outgained Carolina 227 to 87 in the first half, with Jordan Love going 18-of-24 for 189 yards and two touchdowns. He threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to tight end Tucker Kraft and a 24-yard touchdown to wide receiver Matthew Golden. Packers wide receiver Christian Watson, who had six catches for 100 yards, was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation of a chest injury. He was injured on a 53-yard reception, with Panthers cornerback Will Lee injuring his hamstring on the same play. Lee needed a cart to get into the X-ray room. Josh Jacobs scored on a 1-yard touchdown run. The Packers would lead by more if Trey Smack hadn't missed his first PAT try off the left upright, his eighth missed kick of the season. Green Bay also lost two fumbles. Packers wide receiver Coleman Owen fumbled the opening kickoff, and linebacker Nick Hampton recovered for the Panthers. Carolina gained only 8 yards in the drive before Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 39-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. Watson fumbled on an 8-yard reception, a fumble forced by safety Nick Scott and recovered by Bobby Okereke. The Panthers, though, didn't take advantage of their second takeaway. Bryce Young has taken only two sacks, but the Packers have constantly pressured him and linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper intercepted Young. Young is 10-of-19 for 65 yards. Chuba Hubbard has 11 carries for 37 yards and a touchdown and five catches for 21 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bryce Young and the Panthers' passing game are running into familiar problems, can they be fixed?
summary: Young struggled again as Carolina lost to the Packers and fell below .500
full_text:
The last time the Carolina Panthers appeared in primetime, Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns in a 32-26 win over the Lions . Young was both efficient and impressive, hitting on all the new, creative solutions offensive coordinator Brad Idzik had installed and making some big-time throws needed. An 18-yard sideline dart to Tetairoa McMillan on a third and 14 late in the game epitomized everything that was going right for the Panthers' passing offense, led by a massive step by Young.
By the end of the night, Young was leading the NFL in passing yards.
But that was then, and this is now. After a 27-19 loss to the Packers , the Panthers are 3-4 and have produced back-to-back offensive stinkers. Just four days earlier, they were blown out 43-13 by the Buccaneers , a game in which Young threw two interceptions and took five sacks. Thursday, Young took six sacks and threw a pick.
Teams have bad games and even bad stretches. But this stretch has been particularly worrisome for the Panthers for a bevy of reasons: Young's play, yes, but also a crumbling offensive line and opponents figuring out some of Idzik's and Young's tendencies. Given Young's rocky career path thus far, there are big questions arising, the same big questions that have followed him his entire career. Do the Panthers have answers?
Young's biggest strength has always been his mind. He is terrific at dissecting defenses both pre- and post-snap. This week was always going to be a challenge. Short weeks on the road leave far less time to prepare, and it often becomes a "players, not plays" scenario when it comes to determining a winner; physical skill wins out.
Young, because of some of his physical limitations, has a thin margin for error. And when the Panthers trot out an offensive line like this, especially against a blitz-heavy, disguise-heavy Packers defense, that margin for error completely disappears.
Ekwonu is injured (torn patellar tendon)
Moton is injured (broken leg/ankle)
This group doesn't cut it. Walker was particularly brutal, allowing four pressures and a sack and committing two penalties. Fortner and Freeling allowed three pressures, and Hunt allowed two. In fact, the only players who didn't allow a pressure, according to PFF, were Bullock (who left early with an injury) and Jake Curhan , who was called up from the practice squad.
Injuries have completely destroyed this unit. The Panthers knew they'd be without Ekwonu for most of, if not all of, this season. Walker was supposed to be a suitable replacement. He had been an established starter for the Packers. Instead, his 30 pressures allowed are the most in the NFL.
At the other tackle spot, Moton has been a steady presence for years. But he missed the start of the year with blood clots and then broke his leg and suffered ankle ligament damage that ended his season after two games . Freeling, a first-round pick who was viewed as a project and is coming off a knee injury, has played a ton. He currently ranks 65th out of 71 tackles in PFF's grades (Walker is tied for 58th).
On Thursday, Amazon Prime commentators Kirk Herbstreit and Al Michaels discussed the Panthers trying to "protect" their tackles. But really, there was nowhere to hide and, for Young, nowhere to escape. What is he supposed to do when three offensive linemen -- including both tackles -- get beat immediately?
SWARMED 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/CT4vF4IaUk
Or when Freeling gets beat so easily it's like he was hardly there?
Barryn Sorrell gets the fifth sack of the night for the Packers! CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0MBS9KVmSV
The tackles are far from the only problem. Fortner has given up 18 pressures, six more than any other center. The left guard spot currently belongs to Bullock, who only joined Carolina after not surviving the Ravens ' final cuts.
As such, Young has faced the ...
That's impossible to survive. While he isn't faultless for his sack problems, PFF says the offensive line has been at least partially responsible on 83% of the pressures he's faced, the 10th-highest rate in the NFL.
Perhaps the play most illustrative of this problem was actually one of Young's better plays Thursday. On an RPO throw, Young nearly ripped it to Tetairoa McMillan immediately. The problem? Packers linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper was standing right there. He knew what was coming. Young double-clutched, McMillan worked his way into a tiny sliver of space, and Young fired for a first down.
Still, it showed that one of the solutions Idzik implemented this offseason, these quick-hitting passes, are getting more challenging and less effective.
Bryce Young -- Passes under 2.5 seconds
When you're trying to protect your offensive line, quick throws make sense. But an over-reliance on them makes them too easy to defend. Young threw 20 passes that came out in 2.5 seconds or faster Thursday, the most of the season, and his 40% success rate on these throws was his worst of the season.
Smart opponents are basically saying, "Want to beat us over the top? Prove it." Two of Young's worst games this year have been against the Browns and the Packers, who rank first and third, respectively, in press coverage snaps. The other was against the Buccaneers, who knew they didn't need to press or blitz because they were constantly wreaking havoc up front (42% pressure rate) even without doing so.
There's a game plan here to compress everything in front of Young and see if he can win deep, which he can't under current conditions. Thursday, Young went 1 for 6 on passes 10+ yards downfield and only attempted one pass 20+ yards downfield.
Completions 10+ yards downfield
Using net yards per attempt, Young is on par with Daniel Jones and Jalon Daniels in those three bad games and on par with Drake Maye and Trevor Lawrence in every other game.
The problem? Teams are starting to pick up on the weaknesses.
Young was ninth in net yards per attempt through six weeks (7.4). He's averaging 4.5 net yards per attempt over the past two weeks.
Another problem? Young isn't 100%. He's been on the injury report with a knee issue the past several weeks, and though he hasn't missed any practice time, coach Dave Canales thinks it's impacting him.
"I would say that he certainly doesn't look like he's got that quick, make you miss type of deal, but he was able to create some space for himself," Canales said, per the team's transcript.
Young's sack rate and sack-to-pressure rate are way up, indicators of a lack of protection and a lack of escapability. Opponents will attack each and every weakness relentlessly, and right now, both Young and Carolina have many.
The short answer is yes, but the ceiling is low.
If it feels like every week is a referendum on Young, it's because he walks such a fine line between success and failure. He is not going to overcome suboptimal surroundings consistently. He is very smart and accurate in tight spaces when not under pressure, but he is rarely going to win deep, and his arm-strength issues prevent him from accessing all areas of the field. That's why it feels like defenses are closing in so much. They are challenging Young to win in places he doesn't usually win.
The line has to get better for Young to have any chance. Canales is confident it will.
"I just think it comes down to a protection plan deal for us, because when we give Bryce time he's shown his ability to be able to spread the ball around, distribute it, find accurate throws in traffic and all those things, and I'm confident if we shore that thing up, which we will -- when we shore that part up -- Bryce will be back in his rhythm making the throws that he can."
Idzik will come up with some solutions, too, and a mini-bye here should help. But we've seen throughout Young's career that the ceiling is relatively low. Even at his best, he's a middle-of-the-league quarterback, and those "at his best" stretches are fragile. That much is clearly and obviously on display right now.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Cam Skattebo says he feared amputation after gruesome injury that ended his 2025 season
summary: In a new documentary about his recovery, he also said he had a pregame premonition about his injury
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is coming off his best game of the season, having rushed 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown against the Houston Texans last week. Skattebo had been unceremoniously benched in the previous game, taking just six snaps and recording zero carries following a costly fumble the week before, so it was good to see him get back to form.
Early in the season, Skattebo was running extremely inefficiently and averaged just 3.6 yards per carry over the Giants' first five games. That was perhaps unsurprising when you consider that his 2025 season ended with a right ankle dislocation, an open tibia fracture and a ruptured deltoid ligament. That's a scary injury, and one that can obviously affect a running back's performance, given how important cutting and changing direction are to succeeding at the position.
Skattebo said earlier this year that he had considered retirement in the wake of the injury, and this week he and the Giants released an hour-long documentary detailing his recovery. He revealed more about his situation, including that he was afraid his foot would have to be amputated and that he had a premonition about a potential injury before the game.
"Before the game, I actually had an out-of-body experience," Skattebo said, via GiantsWire . "We were all praying in the showers. I was holding both my teammates' hands. It almost felt like, when we were praying, my body was lifted out of my own body. It was weird. I didn't feel like I was in the present me. I didn't feel like myself."
Once he saw what the injury looked like, he feared doctors would have to amputate his foot.
"When I first got hurt, like I'm asking the doctors, like, they're going to have to cut my foot off," he said, via The New York Post .
"As soon as the doctor touched my foot, I felt pain. He snapped (my ankle) back into place, and it was like, 'A sigh of relief.' Once I got in the X-Ray room, they cut my shoe off, they cut my sock off, I was a half-second from passing out because I had dislocated it so far that the skin ripped."
Skattebo obviously did not get his foot amputated and did not retire, and is now back on the field and looks like the lead back for the Giants — especially after the team cut Najee Harris and placed Tyrone Tracy Jr . on injured reserve. He will need to maintain the improved efficiency he showed against the Texans, but just being back on the field and playing at all is pretty impressive considering the extent of the injury he sustained.

title: NFL Week 8 schedule: Why you should watch these three underrated games
summary: Here are three games you should watch that people may not be talking about
full_text:
It's Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season, and this is just about the time when the window for teams' playoff possibilities starts to close. We saw some significant results last week, both good and bad.
The Texans losing another and falling to 2-5 raises questions about whether their season is done for. The Seahawks had a very redeeming win, handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season in a blowout. Staying in that division, the Rams made things interesting in the standings by getting a check in the win column as well. The Falcons also kept their season hopes trending positive by handing the 49ers their first loss of the season.
This all just proves that even if a team isn't on the top of the playoff picture, their games may end up being the most interesting ones of the week.
Which brings us to why we are here: it's time for the weekly edition of underrated NFL games . Here are three games you should keep on your radar:
Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)
It's the battle of the Los Angeles teams this week, and it always adds an interesting layer when squads who share a stadium face each other. While they both call SoFi home, one team does have to be dubbed the home team and this time it's the Rams, meaning the Chargers will have the visiting locker room in their own stadium.
The Chargers are basically playing for the No. 1 seed at this point. No NFL team has ever started the season 0-6 and made the playoffs. The worst start for a team that ended up in the postseason was by the 1992 San Diego Chargers, who went 0-4 and finished 11-5.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh is on the hot seat and needs to get his team looking somewhat better if he wants to keep his job, and 0-7 doesn't look great to front offices.
The Rams are also not off to the best start, though it seems amazing compared to their Week 8 opponent. There are many 3-4 teams in the league that are in the playoffs, and Super Bowl chances seem slim, but that's not the case for the Rams.
Despite their wildly underwhelming start, they still have the fifth-best odds of winning the Super Bowl (+1100), per DraftKings Sportsbook. If they fall to the no-win Chargers, however, those odds may plummet. This is a big game for both teams, as one looks to avoid going 0-7 and the other fights to reach .500.
Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming on Paramount+
We know how much I love divisional games, because they are the most unpredictable, have the most history and carry the most weight. The Dolphins are 1-5, so this likely won't affect the final divisional standings between these two teams, but it could have a significant impact elsewhere.
The Patriots could still win the AFC East, though they are behind the Bills , they did win their first head-to-head against Buffalo. New England retook their AFC East throne last year, after a few years of the Bills getting that hat and t-shirt feeling when Tom Brady left. If the records are close down the line, these divisional games will mean a lot, and right now the Patriots need that boost.
The other interesting thing about this game is that, even though the Patriots are on paper a better team in every category, they historically struggle in Miami. The Patriots have lost five of their last six games in Miami. Will the Patriots lose to the Dolphins? Most likely not, but it could get closer than people think; divisional games tend to do that.
The Patriots are looking to bounce back from a 30-24 loss against the Chicago Bears . They beat themselves in the game numerous times and an easier opponent will be a good test of whether they can correct those mistakes and look dominant enough to be a threat in the AFC.
Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free)
The NFC South includes the 3-3 Panthers, 3-4 Atlanta Falcons, 2-5 Buccaneers and 2-5 Saints.
This game will likely have significant implications for the divisional rankings. This is also a matchup between two teams who struggled in the beginning of the year and have found a resurgence. The similarities don't end there; both teams had quarterbacks sidelined for multiple weeks, with the Falcons' Michael Penix Jr . sidelined while recovering from an ACL injury and the Bucs' Baker Mayfield sidelined due to a thumb injury.
The Falcons are coming off a huge win against the San Francisco 49ers, handing them their first win. The Bucs are coming off a win against the Panthers. I think these teams will have a lot of fight in them this week and it will make for a very competitive game.

title: Panthers fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, make other defensive changes after Packers loss
summary: Evero has had the league's No. 30 scoring defense (26.3 points per game) after four years in Carolina
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers made a rare, in-season coaching change Friday morning by firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. Carolina also let go of defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley, and defensive line coach Todd Wash will serve as interim DC and call the team's defensive plays.
The Panthers' 27-19 road defeat on "Thursday Night Football" to the Green Bay Packers proved to be the last straw for Evero. In Week 7, Carolina lost by 30 points to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , marking the third-most points allowed in a home game in franchise history. The Panthers also allowed a whopping 59 points in their 2026 opener, a 59-37 defeat against the Chicago Bears . Those 59 points allowed are the most surrendered in a single game in Panthers franchise history.
Despite facing a Packers team with the NFL's worst rushing offense, the Panthers failed to contain Packers quarterback Jordan Love, who had to throw the ball all over the yard for Green Bay to win on Thursday. He threw for 288 yards, three touchdowns and an interception on 30-of-41 passing.

Evero's unit struggled almost across the board in his four seasons running the Panthers defense. The lone bright spot was Carolina's pass defense, where they allowed the fourth-fewest passing yards per game (201.1) since 2023.

Evero wasn't anywhere close to having his ideal secondary in the Thursday night loss at Lambeau Field. Cornerbacks Jaycee Horn (quad), Mike Jackson (groin) and Akayleb Evans (knee/triceps) were all on injured reserve in Week 8.
Carolina hopes this defensive shakeup will be enough to repeat as NFC South champions in 2026. One of the coolest things about the modern NFL is the amount of trades we get, with legitimate stars changing teams in the offseason and now during the season pretty darn regularly. title: Cowboys already won 2026 NFL trade deadline with Joey Porter Jr. trade
summary: In Porter Jr.'s three games with Dallas, he profiles as the league's best cornerback
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The 2026 NFL trade deadline isn't until Nov. 10, but the Dallas Cowboys can already claim to be one of the league's victors thanks to their acquisition of cornerback Joey Porter Jr .
Dallas traded a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers in the middle of the night between Sept. 30 and Oct. 1 after contract talks fell apart between the 26-year-old cornerback and Pittsburgh. The Cowboys knew they had to do something after a 1-2 start to their 2026, and the trade for Porter Jr. has gone exactly how owner and general manager Jerry Jones could have hoped for.
Porter Jr. profiles as the NFL's No. 1 cornerback in his three games with Dallas this season. Entering Week 8, Porter Jr. ranks first in the NFL in completion percentage allowed (18.2%), passing yards allowed (10) and pass yards per attempt allowed (0.9) among the 254 players with at least 10 passes thrown their way.
The Houston Texans didn't throw toward him once on his 19 coverage snaps in the Cowboys' 34-30 road win. He then missed "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a game Dallas lost 24-16, because of a stomach bug . Porter Jr. returned to face the Green Bay Packers on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6, and he didn't allow a catch on the five times Jordan Love threw his way on his 25 coverage snaps in a 23-13 defeat. On "Monday Night Football" against the Philadelphia Eagles , he allowed his first two catches of the year for a total of 10 yards on the six times quarterback Tanner McKee threw Porter Jr.'s way on his 30 coverage snaps.
"I love it man. I love it when we have a player like that who you can just throw on anybody's top guy, and then just say 'if you're going to beat us, beat us with that guy on him.' Lately, he's done a great job," Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb said after practice on Thursday. "I don't think he's had a completion on him yet. I don't know the facts behind that, but just off what I've seen, when the ball is thrown his way, it somehow ends up on the ground. Soon enough it's going to be in his hands."
Porter Jr. knows exactly how many completions he has surrendered this season: two. Both of them were against the Eagles in Week 7. The first was a five-yard gain to Philadelphia tight end Dallas Goedert for five yards on a third-and-6, and the second one was a five-yard gain to Eagles first-round rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon on a second-and-20. He is still seething about both of those completions even though it's past the "24-hour rule" NFL players will cite as the amount of time they have to process the previous week's game before moving on to prepare for the upcoming week's game.
"Two little 5-yard outs or whatever. I was pissed about it. … As a DB, you never want to give up anything," Porter Jr. said after practice on Wednesday . "I really hold myself to a high standard when I'm on the field. I definitely don't want to give up any passes to anybody I don't think I should be giving up passes to."
Completion percentage allowed
Pass yards per attempt allowed
Passer rating against as primary defender
Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker knows he'll soon be talking to Porter Jr. about teams simply deciding to avoid throwing his way for the vast majority of Dallas' games. It's a talk he's had to have with the likes of All-Pro corners he has coached in previous stops like Denver Broncos 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Pat Surtain II and Philadelphia Eagles 2025 first-team All-Pro Quinyon Mitchell .
"I've coached guys where it gets to that point, but then you're going to play certain teams who have a receiver where they don't care if Deion [Sanders] came out of retirement to go cover him," Parker said on Thursday. ... "So he knows that because as soon as you're playing in that way, and you think that you're not getting those targets, you're getting those targets. And so you have to stay aggressive, you have to stay dominant, your technique has to be perfect every play. Corner is one of those positions where you could have 99 perfect snaps, and that one could cost us. So that focus level and that intensity has to remain, and he's [Porter Jr.] done a good job of maintaining that."
Whether it's erasing a top-flight wide receiver from the game through teams deciding not to throw at him or having a flurry of action come his way, Porter Jr. has fun because he knows his opponent isn't. He had chances to defend Packers wide receiver Christian Watson , who ranks seventh in the NFL with 595 receiving yards, and Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden , who ranks 10th in the NFL with 512 receiving yards, and he didn't allow a catch on five targets. That's the most fun he's had this season.
"That's my whole job. I get any type of satisfaction when I get the opponent upset or whatever they're going through," Porter Jr. said. ... "It's both. I enjoy when I get games where they try me like the Packers game. I had fun because I got a lot of targets. I don't really get that often. So when you're in the kitchen and in the fire like that, it's kind of fun to show off your talents."
Hearing Porter Jr. talk like that and seeing him trash talk opponents' top receivers on the field is quite the juxtaposition from his off-field persona. In the locker room, Porter Jr. maintains a low profile while opening up to his new teammates. Joey Porter, Porter Jr.'s father, who was a four-time Pro Bowl linebacker and member of the 2000s All-Decade team, was known for his fiery on-field demeanor. Porter Jr. channels his dad on the field but enjoys relaxing off of it.
"Ever since I was a kid, it's been that comparison. I'm like my mom on the outside, but when I get on the field, I'm kind of like my dad," Porter Jr. said. "I'm cool, calm and collected for the most part, but when I'm on the field, I turn it on a little bit to try to be an energizer and be there for teammates as much as possible."
The Cowboys are already enjoying Porter Jr.'s desire to "run to the smoke" on the field while bolstering what has been an up-and-down pass defense in 2026.
"I think you watch him from afar. I think his personality, he's a real laid-back dude, but on the field when he crosses those white lines, he runs to the smoke," Parker said. "So that's what we value with him is he has an energy about himself. He affects others with his energy and his play. Then off the field, he's very kind of low-key, but when he steps on the field, he turns into a different person."
Dallas four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams has already noticed a dramatic uptick in his performance since Porter Jr's in-season arrival. Williams leads all NFL defensive tackles in tackles for loss with nine in 2026, and seven of the nine have come since Porter Jr's Cowboys debut in Week 4. The Cowboys have also allowed under 24 points in three straight games, something they didn't do in either of the two prior seasons.
"He's a baller. I joke with him and tell him all the time 'I've been playing better since he got here, so he's the reason I've been playing better,'" Williams said after practice on Thursday. "He's a baller man. He brought energy. He brought swag. Just the confidence he has when he is on an island by himself is unbelievable man. The player that he is is great to have on our team."
The scariest part of the NFC East and the rest of the Cowboys' opponents is that Porter Jr. produced like the league's top cornerback while still learning both Dallas' playbook and his teammates. Now, his new-team adjustment period is over from a schematic perspective, meaning Porter Jr. could be even better going forward. For the cost of what's essentially a third-round pick (the sixth-round pick in 2027 and the second-round pick in 2028), Jones gave his team an All-Pro-caliber, No. 1 cornerback. That makes the Cowboys the 2026 NFL trade deadline's undisputed winner with a couple of weeks to go.
"I wouldn't say I'm going through the growing pains…
