title: Steelers legend Kordell Stewart changes narrative on his NFL career in new HBO documentary
summary: Stewart wants his career to be remembered for what happened on the field
full_text:
For NFL fans of a certain age, Kordell Stewart is remembered as an exciting player who starred as "Slash" before becoming a Pro Bowl quarterback, leading the Pittsburgh Steelers to two AFC Championship game appearances in the late '90s and early '00s. That's how Stewart wants to be remembered.
He doesn't, however, want his career to be defined by a rumor that nearly derailed his career and now takes center stage in HBO's new documentary, "Kordell Stewart/Slash & Burn."
"I just wanted people to appreciate my experience of being a Steeler in Pittsburgh," Stewart recently told CBS Sports. "Not appreciate it from the standpoint of liking, disliking, but just identify it for what it really was. I thought that, truth be told, it was arguably one of the best runs that I can think of where I was able to do so much on the football field that was different than most.
"I had my ups, you know. I had my downs. I never complained. I never blamed. All I did was just work. ... I would like to say I had a lot of success in Pittsburgh, and we had some failures. You know, I'm a glass half full guy. I'm always about being objective and transparent, but also real."
For Stewart, what was real was an exciting, two-year stint playing quarterback/receiver/running back/punter (yes, even punter) and six seasons as Pittsburgh's starting quarterback. The fiction, however, included an unfounded rumor that Stewart had been caught engaging in lewd activity with another male in a city park.
The rumor, started by a local police officer, came out just two days after an ugly loss during the 1998 season, a loss that ended with a fan calling Stewart a racial slur and throwing beer at him as he was walking off the field.
While there was no merit to the rumor, it lingered over Stewart and the Steelers, who staggered through a 7-9 season.
Things got worse before they got better. Stewart was benched in 1999 and briefly returned to his role as Slash. After starting the 2000 season on the bench, Stewart was returned to the starting lineup with the Steelers sitting at 0-3. With Stewart at the helm, Pittsburgh went 9-4 that season. He was the last quarterback that season to defeat the Ravens and their historically dominant defense.
Stewart and Co. carried that momentum into the 2001 season. That year, Stewart piloted Pittsburgh to a 13-3 record, the team's best record since 1978. He set a single-season franchise record for completion percentage, was named to the Pro Bowl and finished fourth in league MVP voting. He was also named the Steelers' MVP.
The Steelers dethroned the Ravens in the AFC divisional round, but they were defeated at home by the eventual Super Bowl champion Patriots (who were later punished for stealing opponents' signals, including Pittsburgh's ) in the AFC Championship game. The loss hurt, but that season was nonetheless validation for Stewart after all he had been through the previous four years.
"Oh, it was the greatest," Stewart said of that '01 season. "You know how bad I wanted to go to the Super Bowl that year? Because of all that I had to go through with that rumor and just people doubting me, telling me what I couldn't do and telling me what I should do and not appreciating what I was doing. ... And we came so close."
Both of Stewart's best seasons (1997 and 2001) ended in AFC Championship games. In both games, the Steelers lost close games to the eventual Super Bowl champions led by iconic quarterbacks in John Elway and Tom Brady .
"Looking back on it, I'm not going to say I accept it," Stewart said. "But hey, if those are the two guys [I lost to], I don't think that's too bad."
Those losses are part of Stewart's story in Pittsburgh, but they aren't the story. In Stewart's case, the destination was truly the journey.
You'd be hard-pressed to find a more exciting season than the Steelers' 1997 campaign, Stewart's first as Pittsburgh's starting quarterback. That season, the Steelers overcame deficits of 21-0 (in Baltimore), 21-7 (against Denver) and were 3-0 in overtime games. That was also the season when then-Steelers coach Bill Cowher nearly tackled a Jaguars player on "Monday Night Football."
Individually, it was an historic season for the then-25-year-old Stewart. He became the first player in NFL history to throw 20 touchdowns and run for 10 scores in the same season. Stewart also became the first player to throw three touchdowns and run for two scores in multiple games.
Stewart was part of Pittsburgh's prolific offensive trio that also included Jerome Bettis and Yancey Thigpen. That season, Bettis ran for 1,665 yards, the second-highest single-season total in Steelers history. Thigpen set a then-single-season franchise record for receiving yards (1,398).
The Steelers' most memorable game that season came in Week 16, a late afternoon game in New England. Against the defending AFC champions, Pittsburgh overcame 14-0 and 21-13 deficits to pull off a stunning, 24-21 win in overtime. Pittsburgh forced overtime after Stewart led a drive that included a fourth-and-7 completion, a touchdown pass on third-and-goal and a successful two-point conversion.
In overtime, Stewart, under duress, completed a 41-yard pass that set up the game-winning field goal.
"In the pros, there was not a better moment in my career," Stewart said.
OTD 1997 #Steelers #Patriots @KSlash10 leads Pittsburgh down the field for a touchdown late and gets the 2 point conversion to send the game to OT. Johnson would kick the winning FG giving the #Steelers their 3rd OT win of the season. 24-21 #HereWeGo pic.twitter.com/iSD13ZV5ui
Moments like that, Stewart said, are what he hopes Steelers fans remember when they think about his career, one that he believes will eventually be immortalized in the Steelers Hall of Honor.
"For me, playing ball in that city and the things that I had to go through, I think that would really vindicate and cap off a successful run in Pittsburgh," he said. "I think it will do a lot of people proud once that day actually comes. But it's gonna happen, and I'm gonna be here to see it."
HBO's new original documentary "Kordell Stewart/ Slash & Burn" is now streaming on HBO Max. It tackles Stewart's career and the devastating rumor that has followed him for decades.

title: Josh Jacobs explains controversial touchdown celebration vs. Panthers that seemed to mimic arrest
summary: Jacobs says the celebration was a reference to a gospel song titled "Break Every Chain"
full_text:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was recently reinstated from the commissioner's exempt list after serving a six-game stint on the list. He was there in the wake of disturbing domestic violence allegations stemming from an offseason incident, but has been back on the field for the last two games.
On Thursday night, Jacobs scored a short rushing touchdown against the Carolina Panthers and, during his celebration, appeared to put his hands behind his back as though he were being arrested and handcuffed. At least, that's how many observers saw it.
TOUCHDOWN PACKERS 📺: Prime Video pic.twitter.com/JGV2fIEObP
He was asked about it following the game, and Jacobs said the celebration was not a reference to his being arrested, but instead to a gospel song titled "Break Every Chain."
"They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said, referring to the Amazon Prime broadcast. "It was one second that they just saw me. Anyways, me and (wide receiver Savion Williams ), we came up with the celebration, if they would've seen the whole celebration.
"Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was gonna thank God. That's what I did last week. Second one was gonna be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was gonna be the next celebration. It's just a correlation. But like I said, the media's gonna run with it. They're gonna make it something that it wasn't. But it is what it is."
A longer video of the celebration shows Williams running over to Jacobs and seemingly unlocking the chains on Jacobs' wrists, after which Jacobs breaks free.
The full TD celebration in question: https://t.co/jUhME09rjn pic.twitter.com/xMu1702t1f
Jacobs' explanation seems reasonable, if you see the full video and know the context and content of the gospel song in question. But it's also reasonable that people would assume, based on what they saw on Prime, that the gesture was a reference to his arrest. (It wouldn't be the first time a player has celebrated a touchdown that way, after all.) The confusion is understandable, and probably not entirely a media creation.
Jacobs was charged with two misdemeanors, battery and damage to property, from an arrest in May after police responded to his home following a domestic violence incident. He later pleaded no contest to the charges in September, resolving the court case. He also filed an action seeking to prevent the public release of evidence related to the case, including alleged video of the incident.

title: Deshaun Watson vs. Steelers' suffocating secondary: How pivotal AFC North duel will be won
summary: How Watson attacks Pittsburgh's zone coverage will be crucial
full_text:
First place in the AFC North is on the line in Week 8 between a team used to these stakes, the reigning division champion Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2), and a newcomer to these types of games, the Cleveland Browns (5-2).
It's been a long time since this matchup meant this much. The Steelers' and Browns' Week 8 game this season possesses the third-best combined record (10-4, .714 winning percentage) entering a matchup this late into the season in the last 50 years. After Cleveland defeated Pittsburgh 27-24 on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 4, it now has a chance to sweep the Steelers in the regular season for the first time since 1988. That's the longest regular-season sweep drought (34 seasons) for any divisional matchup since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
So, where could this matchup between two hard-hitting defenses and battle-seasoned quarterbacks in Pittsburgh's Aaron Rodgers and Cleveland's Deshaun Watson be won? Let's take a closer look.
After struggling on and off the field for the vast majority of his five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million contract, Watson has begun to give the Browns some value. He is just the third quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of a season, along with Troy Aikman (1990) and Matthew Stafford (2016). Watson produced at least three completions and 30 yards on all five of his game-winning drives this season.
In Cleveland's latest comeback, a 27-24 win against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7, the Browns trailed 14-0 in the first quarter, marking the team's largest comeback win since 2023. Watson had his most prolific game yet as a Brown with 308 yards passing, his most since Week 17 of the 2020 season, and he snapped a streak of 25 consecutive starts without 300 yards through the air.
So how will the Steelers slow down a reinvigorated Watson? Well, they entered Week 8 with the league's No. 5 scoring defense (19.7 points per game allowed) and the league's No. 6 total defense (303.7). The matchup that will decide this showdown will be how Watson pilots the Browns' passing game against the Steelers' zone coverage.
Pittsburgh runs zone at the fourth-highest rate in the NFL , 82.2% of the time, per TruMedia, and it is allowing the ninth-lowest success rate in the league (42.2%) when running zone coverage, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. When the Steelers specifically utilize their Cover 3 zone, their success rate allowed decreases to 37.2%, the sixth lowest in the NFL. Of Pittsburgh's seven interceptions in 2026, four have occurred in Cover 3, tied for the league lead.
However, Watson's 49.4% passing success rate against zone coverage is tied for the fourth-best among qualified quarterbacks this season. The good news for Pittsburgh is that success hasn't typically come from big plays, as his 10.6% explosive play rate vs. Cover 3 is the sixth-lowest in the NFL. That means the Steelers can allow a few papercuts, but they should be able to keep everything in front of them when facing a physically diminished version of the three-time Pro Bowler, thanks to the litany of injuries he has suffered in his Browns career.
Whoever wins the battle of Watson vs. the Steelers' zone coverage unit will likely dictate which team will sit atop the AFC North standings entering Week 9.

title: NFL's 'scariest' good, bad teams: Why Seahawks strike fear, Titans fans should be terrified
summary: With Halloween arriving, these teams sure are spooky
full_text:
It's the last week of October, which means spooky season is in full effect. Whether you're dressing up, partying, handing out candy, watching scary movies and visiting haunted houses, or partaking in none of the Halloween festivities on Saturday, the NFL season will continue rolling Sunday — a great way to enjoy all that leftover candy.
With the season nearly halfway done, we know which teams are trending toward the postseason and which ones aren't. But which teams are truly scary in a good way — no opponent wants to see them — or scary bad to the point their own fans want to hide their eyes?
We break down the nine scariest teams, six scary good, three scary bad, this season.
Yes, the reigning Super Bowl champions still belong here, even if they're "only" 4-3, and a 20-3 domination of the Chiefs should be all the reason you need. Even their defense is called the "Dark Side," and any unit that combines Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy up front with safety/weapon Nick Emmanwori and star cornerback Devon Witherspoon should strike fear in opponents. Sam Darnold has had some turnovers that make Seahawks fans hide their eyes, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba is scary enough to keep any defensive coordinator up at night. Overlook last year's champs at your own peril.
The offense may not strike fear in many opponents' hearts, but that defense? Downright terrifying, especially for quarterbacks. Brian Flores' unit blitzes on 71% of opponents' dropbacks, which is 27 percentage points higher than the second-highest rate. The Vikings also own the best sack rate in the NFL (10.6%). Only one team has scored more than 16 points on this defense, which might as well be the Purple People Eaters 2.0. And just when you think you have the offense under control, Justin Jefferson can produce a big play anytime, anywhere. If Kyler Murray can settle in, this team will be frighteningly good, and with blitzes that will give even the most poised quarterbacks a jump scare or two.
Could we really get another installment of the Reign of Terror from Kansas City? Looking for his fourth Lombardi Trophy already, Patrick Mahomes has been impressive early this season after returning from a torn ACL. Kenneth Walker III has been the best offseason addition by any team, able to seemingly disappear in a pile of would-be tacklers and reappear down the field. His seven carries of 20+ yards are tied for most in the NFL. Steve Spagnuolo's defense may be young, but his cornerback tandem of Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams can make opponents feel like they can't escape anywhere. The Chiefs need more firepower in the passing attack, but everyone knows by now that Mahomes is the scariest of sights come the postseason.
The 49ers ' injury report makes it look like the team survived a month full of terror, but after the bye week, Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel, and a host of other standouts could be on their way back. And no one will want to see this offense in full gear. Brock Purdy and mad scientist play caller Kyle Shanahan can expose any defense's weakness, and no one wants to mess with George Kittle or Trent Williams in the trenches. On defense, newly acquired game-wrecking defensive lineman DeForest Buckner makes San Francisco a lot scarier, too.
Simply put, we have evidence that Josh Allen is an alien who's come to take over planet Earth.
How did Josh Allen make this TD pass to Keon Coleman? BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CNLw6KW2tC
If you cannot stop the run game, the Bears will hammer you over and over again, with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai proving to be double trouble. But what gets really scary is when Caleb Williams starts doing his thing. Always capable of using dark arts to finagle his way out of trouble and making a big play, Williams has gotten terrifyingly accurate this year, too. Oh, and there aren't many scarier sights along the defensive line than newly acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who will have opposing offensive linemen quaking in their cleats.
The Chargers won 11 games in back-to-back years, but this team is a perfect example of how scary expectations can be. Mike McDaniel was a highly anticipated addition as offensive coordinator, but Justin Herbert's play has been hard to watch. Add in injuries along one of the NFL's worst offensive lines and struggling pass catchers all over the place, and Herbert is doomed. The echoes of Jim Harbaugh saying, "Who's got it better than us?" haunt the nightmares of any Bolts fan this season. In the midst of a brutal stretch of the schedule, it might get worse before it gets better.
The Titans hoped a new coach, a new offensive coordinator and new weapons would help Cam Ward , but here they are with a 1-6 record and Ward having thrown for over 200 yards just once this season. Tennessee might have a bright future, in part thanks to the two first-round picks they acquired for Simmons, but without its best defensive player, this team could continue to spiral for the rest of the season. Can Ward help them escape the nightmarish run of quarterbacks they've been on? Nashville's known for country music, but this has been a sad-song franchise for quite a while.
The Colts are in the scariest situation of them all. Just a year ago, the Colts traded two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner . Now, they're selling at the trade deadline and tanking ... without their 2027 first-round pick. If the season ended today, Indianapolis would have the seventh pick ... and send it to the Jets . Horrifying. The Colts just fired GM Chris Ballard, Daniel Jones keeps turning the ball over in truly disgusting ways, and there's no telling who will still be on this team come Nov. 11, when the trade deadline has passed. The Colts have dug themselves a deep, deep hole, and who knows how long it will take for them to escape?

title: NFL Week 8 bold predictions: Jared Goff tears up Vikings D and Justin Herbert plays a clean game?
summary: Plus, an AFC South running back has a huge game, and Jets WR Garrett Wilson reconnects with Geno Smith a week after sideline shouting match
full_text:
Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 8 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea.
With the Green Bay Packers ' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers , they prevailed to 5-3 despite having under 500 rushing yards as a team (485) this season. Green Bay is the first team ever to have a winning record through eight games while also rushing for under 500 yards. They are also the third team since 1950 with no individual players with 50-plus rushing yards in a game through that span. The Packers' ability to continue to win without any semblance of offensive balance is simply unprecedented.
What other astounding things can happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 8 slate on Halloween weekend? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
The Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's last undefeated team, but it's not because of their offense. They have scored the fewest touchdowns (10) during a 6-0 start since the 1934 Detroit Lions . Minnesota is 6-0 because defensive coordinator Brian Flores' unit is a horror movie for opposing offenses.
The Vikings defense leads the NFL in the following statistics:
However, Lions five-time Pro Bowl quarterback Jared Goff will overcome his struggles against the Vikings to light Minnesota up for 250-plus passing yards and three-plus touchdowns while being sacked no more than once. In each of his last two games against the Vikings, Goff was sacked five times each.
This time will be different because Goff is on an all-time heater to start the 2026 season. He enters Week 8 leading the NFL in passing yards per game (298.0), touchdown-to-interception ratio (14-0) and passer rating (112.5). Goff's 223 throws without an interception are the most through the first six games of a season in NFL history. His 14 touchdowns without an interception are also tied for the most in NFL history in that span, along with Russell Wilson in the 2019 season. Goff has never played better, and he'll stay locked in to shred the Vikings and hand them their first loss of the season.
Entering Week 7, it looked like Tennessee Titans Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard was washed up at the age of 29. He was averaging just 58.2 rushing yards per game and 4.0 yards per carry with just one rushing touchdown. But against the Cleveland Browns , Pollard turned back the clock to run for 129 yards and a career-high three rushing touchdowns.
On Sunday, at the Cincinnati Bengals , Pollard will do it again, rushing for over 120 yards and multiple scores. Yes, the Bengals are a much-improved defense after completely remaking their defensive line with the additions of three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence , two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jonathan Allen , Super Bowl champion edge rusher Boye Mafe, and rookie second-round pick edge rusher Cashius Howell .
In 2025, Cincinnati ranked as the league's No. 30 scoring defense (28.9 points per game) and the NFL's worst rushing defense (147.1 rushing yards per game). This season, the Bengals are the league's No. 8 scoring defense (20.3 points per game) and the NFL's No. 19 rushing defense (116.3 rushing yards per game). Despite that dramatic improvement, Pollard will remain in the zone and go berserk, despite a non-threatening passing game led by 2025 first overall pick quarterback Cam Ward .
Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is having a career year. His 855 yards from scrimmage stood as the fourth most in the league through Week 7, and his 705 since Week 3 are the most in the entire NFL in that span. Warren's 6.8 yards per touch this season would be the most in a season on 15-plus touches per game (he's had 18 touches per game this season) since C.J. Spiller's 6.8 yards per touch back in 2012 with the Buffalo Bills .
Facing a Browns squad that surrendered 129 yards rushing and three rushing touchdowns to Pollard in Week 7, Warren will go off for a career-high 200 yards from scrimmage to even the season series against the Browns at one win apiece.
In most years, this prediction of multiple touchdown passes and no turnovers for the Los Angeles Chargers' two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert wouldn't be considered bold, but he is struggling mightily. He is tied for the league lead in both interceptions (8) and turnovers (10) this season. Herbert is also the first quarterback in NFL history to start 0-6 with an interception and multiple sacks taken in each of his team's first six games.
Against his SoFi Stadium neighbors, the Los Angeles Rams , Herbert will have a clean game. Three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald looks every bit of a 35-year-old who took two seasons off as he is sackless in five consecutive games, the longest streak of his career. Los Angeles will ride former first-round running back Omarion Hampton , control the clock and allow Herbert to play a much more relaxed style of football. That will lead to a big day for the struggling Herbert.
Week 7 couldn't have been uglier for the New York Jets . They allowed the previously-winless Miami Dolphins to tally their first victory of the season, and No. 1 wide receiver Garrett Wilson shared an animated conversation with quarterback Geno Smith and passing game coordinator Seth Ryan. It made sense: Wilson registered season lows in targets (3), catches (2), receiving yards (26) and no touchdowns.
The great news is that Week 8 provides Smith with a revenge game against the slumping Las Vegas Raiders . After their 3-0 start, the Raiders have now lost four in a row because their defense is crumbling. They have allowed 35.8 points per game and 11 passing touchdowns during the four-game losing streak. Smith will light up his old defense, and Wilson will produce over four times his receiving yards total from Week 7 on Sunday with over 100 yards receiving and a touchdown.

However, Deshaun Watson and Co. scored 17 unanswered points, and then Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 28 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter to set up a game-winning field goal. Seriously, it looked like we were headed to overtime, but Robert Saleh's defense forgot there was time on the clock.
I've liked backing Tennessee against the spread in spots against "beatable" teams this year, but the Bengals are not a beatable team, in my opinion. They dropped 35 points on the Ravens in the second half last week, because Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase are unstoppable. The dynamic duo combined for 210 yards receiving and two touchdowns in Week 7. I don't think the Titans' cornerbacks can keep up with them. In fact, their top cornerback, Alontae Taylor , who signed a three-year, $58 million deal in free agency this offseason, hasn't played a single snap in two games now.
This is a massive number, but I have zero faith in Cam Ward . Tennessee averages 157.4 passing yards per game, and just traded away the heart and soul of their team, locker room and community in Jeffery Simmons .

title: Packers' Christian Watson returns against Panthers after chest injury, hospital visit
summary: The Packers wide receiver was injured on a 53-yard reception in the first half
full_text:
Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson returned to the Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Carolina Panthers in the third quarter after departing in the first half with a chest injury. Watson was transported to a hospital near Lambeau Field for precautionary tests and returned to the stadium shortly after halftime. The team initially deemed him questionable to play, and upon his clearance, he reentered the contest.
Watson arrived back at Lambeau Field in an ambulance and ran into the locker room, where he spent about three minutes preparing for a return to action. He emerged onto the sideline with additional padding around his ribs and pointed to the lower right side of his chest when teammates inquired about the injury, according to Prime Video's Kaylee Hartung.
"It was tough," Watson said to Hartung during the postgame show. "I never wanted to go. I was hoping they would let me off. I said I was feeling better once I kind of caught my breath. They said there was a couple of signs that made them have to take me over there. It is what it is. I was just praying that it was good enough to where I could come back out here. Thankfully it was, and I was able to get back out. I'm trying to be on the football field. That's first and foremost for me."
Watson said that he spit up blood upon sustaining the injury, which was a trigger for the Packers' medical staff to take him to the hospital. Tests ruled out internal bleeding, which opened the door for him to play. He said that he monitored the game from his hospital room and watched the play-by-play feed while waiting for the results of his tests.
The injury occurred on the biggest play of the first half: A 53-yard reception that set up the Packers' second touchdown of the night. Watson collided with Panthers cornerback Will Lee III , who was also injured on the play. Carolina ruled Lee doubtful to return with a hamstring injury.
Jordan Love ➡️ Christian Watson for a 53-yard gain! CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tNglqbJ3ZI
Watson was in the midst of a massive performance when he departed from the contest. He led all receivers in the first half with six catches for 100 yards. His ability to separate from the maligned Panthers defense was instrumental in quarterback Jordan Love completing 17 of his first 20 passes on the night.
The Packers dialed up a pass in Watson's direction on his first play back from the hospital, and while he did not come up with the catch, he did add a pair of receptions in the fourth quarter. The second of those two grabs nearly iced the game, as it converted a third down and allowed the Packers to drain valuable time off the clock and limit the Panthers to mere seconds on their final possession.
Matthew Golden stepped up in Watson's absence as the No. 1 option in Green Bay's receiving unit. He caught a touchdown pass on the Packers' first possession without Watson and redeemed himself for dropping a would-be scoring pass on the previous play. Tucker Kraft also played an increased role downfield and was responsible for the Packers' first touchdown on Thursday.
Injuries, unfortunately, have been a defining element of Watson's NFL career. He has an extensive history that includes a separate chest injury, three hamstring strains, an ankle sprain, three knee bruises and an ACL tear. He also sustained a concussion during his rookie season in 2022. In all, Watson has missed 20 games and is yet to play a full season across five years in the league.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Prisco's Week 8 NFL picks: Lions hand Vikings their first loss, Chiefs over Broncos
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game
full_text:
Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night.
I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1.
So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use.
One game at a time. One week at a time.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it.
The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk.
Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10
The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week.
Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21
The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it.
Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13
Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it.
This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it.
Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20
This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it.
The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London.
Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16
The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close.
Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20
The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush.
Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14
The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it.
Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14
This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it.
Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16
The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it.
Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17
These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going.
Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24

title: Jonathan Taylor says he hasn't requested trade as Colts' deadline selloff continues
summary: Trade speculation continues to swirl around the star running back as Indianapolis shifts toward a rebuild ahead of the NFL trade deadline
full_text:
The trade deadline fire sale is on for the Indianapolis Colts , who made two of the NFL's biggest in-season moves of the year this week when they shipped Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers . With those two stars off the roster, the attention is squarely on running back Jonathan Taylor and whether he will be the next standout Colt to leave town.
If Taylor has any say in the matter, he might remain in Indianapolis. He played each of his first six and a half professional seasons with the Colts and on Thursday said that he wants to stay with the team that drafted him in the second round in 2020.
Taylor said that despite the losses of two critical players and the clear downward trajectory of a franchise that seems committed to a rebuild, he has not requested a trade.
"I haven't heard anything," Taylor said . "I can't control that. Obviously, like you guys know, I'm always proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here. Similar to Quenton and Buck. They were proud to wear the horseshoe. They were proud to be here. But obviously, circumstances may cause otherwise. Hopefully that day may not come, but I can't control that."
The potential of a trade is clearly weighing heavily on the Taylor household. Taylor's wife, Ayanna, spoke out about the trade buzz in a social media post, saying her "mind is spiraling."
Taylor himself has to balance the uncertainty surrounding the trade deadline with his duties as the Colts' biggest star. He and the rest of his squad are gearing up for Sunday's divisional battle with the Jacksonville Jaguars . They enter Week 8 as sizable underdogs in the wake of the two blockbuster trades and are in danger of slipping further into the NFL's basement with additional losses tacked onto their already poor 2-5 record.
As it becomes increasingly clear that the Colts are slipping out of contention for the playoffs, and with the franchise firing general manager Chris Ballard in the middle of the season, the biggest question is which additional players, if any, are on the trade block.
"Obviously, it was all speculation until stuff started happening," Taylor said. "Quenton, Buck, those guys are the gold standard of the NFL. Obviously the business side of things, that's where it sucks at. I wish some way, somehow, I could have done more. I wanted to win for those guys. We wanted to get it done here with those guys. Especially Q. He's part of the guys who laid the groundwork. They're definitely gonna be missed."
Among the plethora of candidates to be dealt at the NFL trade deadline, Taylor might be the most impactful . He has twice led the league in rushing touchdowns (including as recently as last season) and paced the NFL in rushing yards in 2021 when he earned a first-team All-Pro selection. He is on pace this season to threaten his career high of 18 touchdowns, given that he already has eight on his ledger through seven games.
The Colts will undoubtedly receive a high volume of calls about their star running back, if they have not already. The Minnesota Vikings may be the best fit of any potential suitor given their offensive needs and the urgency to capitalize on an elite defense, but numerous other teams could also be in the market for a running back upgrade before the Nov. 10 deadline.

title: Packers vs. Panthers prediction: Green Bay, Carolina both look to get back into win column on 'TNF'
summary: How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses
full_text:
In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games.
The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways.
Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five.
Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late.
The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents.
Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field.
Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush.
In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines.
The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league.
The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise.
So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit.
So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love .
Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks.
He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina.
Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game.
It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17

title: Chiefs stand by Harrison Butker despite struggles, Justin Tucker waiting in wings
summary: Tucker's perfect tryout turned heads, but Kansas City views the veteran as both insurance and a resource
full_text:
Despite the field goal issues that marred the first six games of the season and evolved into a disaster in Week 7, the Kansas City Chiefs do not intend to make a kicker change for Sunday's road game against the Denver Broncos . Coach Andy Reid said this week that Harrison Butker will "probably" retain his role as the team's kicker in Week 8, and special teams coordinator Dave Toub went a step further when he staunchly affirmed that Butker is the man for the job.
Butker missed two field goal attempts in last week's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks and is just 11-for-16 on the year. His 68.8% conversion rate is by far the worst of his otherwise stellar career.
Those costly missed kicks prompted the Chiefs to seek outside help, and after they brought three candidates into their facility during the week, they signed free agent Justin Tucker to their practice squad. The eight-time All-Pro will not handle the kicking duties against the Broncos, though.
"Butker is our kicker," Toub said . "We're trying to improve Butker. We're trying to get Butker right. That's what this whole thing is about."
Toub said that Butker went 10-for-10 on his field goal attempts at Wednesday's practice despite 28-mph wind gusts in Kansas City.
The idea behind adding Tucker to the practice squad goes further than simply having a backup option should Butker continue to falter. It is also a calculated measure to potentially help Butker rediscover his typical accuracy. Tucker regressed during his final season with the Baltimore Ravens and missed a career-high eight of his 30 attempts, and Toub detailed how it could be beneficial for Butker to receive mentorship from one of the league's greatest kickers of all time -- one who recently dealt with accuracy struggles of his own.
Tucker missed the entire 2025 season while he served a 10-game suspension following an investigation into alleged inappropriate behaviors during massage sessions. He became eligible to sign with a new team ahead of the 2026 season and received numerous calls before the Chiefs landed him.
"He's a good kicker," Toub said. "I've heard he's been out making the rounds. We talk. All the special teams coaches talk. He had four workouts before we brought him in. We were his fifth workout, tryout. The word was that he's hitting the ball great. I wanted to see it. I always thought he was a great kicker."
Toub constructed a 30-kick tryout for Tucker and the other candidates that included 10 extra points, seven field goals of over 50 yards and one 60-yarder. Tucker went 30-for-30, and 60% of his conversions landed inside a six-foot cylinder in the middle of the uprights.
"Somebody that's struggling is not able to put the ball with that kind of accuracy at 30 kicks," Toub said. "He was off-the-charts good. That's the reason why we signed him to the practice squad."
With Tucker seemingly back in the kind of form that made him a Ravens legend, he could be a viable option on game days if called upon.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Jason Kelce rants, calls out refs over unnecessary roughness penalty on Giants' Cam Skattebo
summary: The Kelce brothers did not mince words when they voiced displeasure with the NFL's officials
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo might be the most physical ballcarrier in the NFL , and sometimes that gets him in trouble. Officials in the Week 7 game against the Houston Texans called Skattebo for a controversial penalty on a first-quarter run when they deemed him guilty of a rarely enforced unnecessary roughness infraction. The penalty flag thrown on the play drew immense scrutiny, and Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce on the "New Heights" podcast joined the chorus of prominent football figures to stand up for Skattebo.
The officials penalized Skattebo for lowering his helmet against a Texans defender. It was just the fourth time this season that foul has been called and the first time it went against an offensive player on a non-special teams play.
Cam Skattebo was penalized for this run... pic.twitter.com/tEHPezmJ3F
Travis Kelce, a physical player in his own right, scoffed at the penalty and said, "That's football." Jason Kelce took an even more passionate stance against the call.
"If the running back hits the defensive player with the crown of his helmet, and you get run over, that's the defensive guy's fault," Jason Kelce said. "Hit him in the f---ing legs. What are we talking about? You're the one who tried to tackle him up top. What the f---? I think it's a dumbass penalty. I think that the runner should have the ability to lower his shoulder and gain yardage however he wants. And if his head goes down with it, that's the way it should be.
"I'm not a fan of the way this is called. I understand it's a penalty, and this is how they want it officiated. I actually think he more just lowered his shoulders. I didn't think he actually lowered his head as much as I've seen."
This might be the dumbest penalty in football pic.twitter.com/RQ2Kw1JlA1
The 15-yard penalty did not prove costly for the Giants, as they proceeded to defeat the Texans in overtime. But it did set a precedent that could impact Skattebo's future games. He said he will not change his running style and that if he continues to draw penalties or faces league-imposed fines, then so be it.
"It was more of he just ran the f---ing dude over," Jason Kelce said, "and the guy was embarrassed, and he lied there for a second, and the league was like, 'Oh, we gotta fine Cam Skattebo.' That's the f---ing dumbest G--damn thing I've ever seen. It's f---ing stupid."
While Skattebo found himself in the doghouse with coach John Harbaugh the previous week due to his early-season fumbling issues, his coach has his back in this case . Harbaugh said it would be a "physical impossibility" for a running back like Skattebo to avoid lowering his head when carrying the ball low to the ground and praised his second-year standout for good fundamentals.
Travis Kelce sees it the same way.
"How do you -- you go flat? Eyes, head up? What's the position? You have to get into a specific position? If he's just trying to lower his pads and accelerate?"
The penalty was a minor hiccup for Skattebo in what was otherwise the best performance of his career. He racked up a personal-best 124 yards and a touchdown against the Texans and set up the game-winning play in overtime when he broke loose for a 42-yard scamper.

title: Are the next two Cardinals games the last for Josh Sweat? Budda Baker?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals had hopes for a decent season this year. The prognosis was to win between six and eight games this year, then add a few more wins in the second season under new head coach Mike LaFleur. Then hopefully, by Year 3, the roster would start making waves and qualify for a playoff […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams is hit by Josh Sweat #10 of the Arizona Cardinals during the game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. The Arizona Cardinals won 18-16. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals had hopes for a decent season this year. The prognosis was to win between six and eight games this year, then add a few more wins in the second season under new head coach Mike LaFleur. Then hopefully, by Year 3, the roster would start making waves and qualify for a playoff berth. RELATED: TWO CARDINALS AMONG BEST CANDIDATES TO MOVE Of course, this was the same plan for former head coach Jonathan Gannon. But instead of a postseason berth, Gannon’s final year ended with breaking the franchise record for the most losses in a single season with 14. So, is this a teardown process for the Cardinals? It is normal for a new head coach to come in and clean house, then bring in “his” type of players. On opening day this year, there were 23 new bodies on the active roster, and several more listed on the practice squad. After the first seven games, the Cardinals find themselves at 2-5-0 and once again in last place in the NFC West Division. Their schedule this year is brutal, despite being a last-place division finisher in 2025. Coming up, they have games against the Dallas Cowboys, Kansas City Chiefs, plus divisional games against the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and the league-leading San Francisco 49ers. All of these games could be losses. They could also get beat by mediocre clubs such as the Washington Commanders and the Philadelphia Eagles. Arizona plays the Cowboys this weekend, and then the rubber game against the Seahawks. Both games are on the road in front of very hostile crowds. If they lose both, should they begin the process of starting over? Rebuilding? Part of every team’s process of a new beginning is to get rid of their highest-priced players. For the Cardinals, that short list includes DE Josh Sweat and S Budda Baker. Sweating it out EDGE Josh Sweat was the main part of the Cardinals’ pass rush last year, as he balled out in the first year of his new contract to the tune of 12 sacks, 17 QB hits, and 28 pressures, among other stats. But this year, he has lost his partner in crime, DT Calais Campbell, who wasn’t re-signed. Campbell had 6.5 sacks on his own plus 16 QB hits and 18 pressures. He was a huge disruptor in the opposing team’s backfield on passing downs. Now, in all fairness, Arizona GM Monti Ossenfort did select Campbell’s replacement in this year’s NFL draft when he took DT Kaleb Proctor out of Southeastern Louisiana. He is one of those rare defensive tackles who can provide a pass rush and isn’t just a gap plugger. And he ran a 4.71. Then, Proctor tore his meniscus during training camp and was ruled out for the entire season. The plan was for Proctor and DT Walter Nolen to dominate the middle and take pressure and double teams off of Sweat. But Nolen has been in the medical ward off and on. So, how is Sweat doing this season with the additional attention placed on Campbell? 16 total tackles, 3 tackles for loss, 4 QB hits, 0 pass defenses, 0 forced fumbles, 0 fumble recoveries, 0 interceptions, 8 pressures, 4 hurries, 2 knockdowns, and 0 missed tackles. What do these numbers say to you? Pro Bowl prospect? Marginal talent? Sweat was real good friends with former Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon, who is now the DC with the Green Bay Packers under LaFleur’s brother, Matt LaFleur. When Gannon got fired for losing 26 games in the past two seasons, it became a problem for Sweat. Now, he said it wasn’t an issue, as he stated in Sports Illustrated : “People think I only came here for one reason, and that was Jonathan Gannon, and yeah, that made the decision easier for me. But I know the guys that were here. I love the way they play. There was a lot of noise in the offseason, but I didn’t respond purposely. I just wanted to see how far people’s imagination could take it.” This has gained some steam on social media, so just to provide some clarity: #AZCardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat is not being traded. Not to the #Packers or anywhere. Carry on… pic.twitter.com/bImuZfvWLq — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) June 3, 2026 During training camp, there were rumors that because Gannon was fired, Sweat had demanded a trade. That may or may not have been the truth, but nothing more came of it. Then Sweat stayed out of all training camp, showed up the week before the first game, and has played ever since. But there is no way he is the dynamic pass rusher he was last year. Sweat is one of those EDGE rushers that has good to very good numbers every year on a consistent basis, but he isn’t going to blow the doors off of any offensive coordinator’s game plan the way a guy like Myles Garrett or Micah Parsons may generate interest. Now in his ninth NFL season, he only has a single Pro Bowl. . @1053SS on the Cowboys potentially trading for Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat: "I'm out on Josh Sweat for what it will cost, and I'm out for what he will do for this defense…" pic.twitter.com/LHpOGh0DGE — 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) October 29, 2026 For two months, all we have heard is how Sweat will be a trade deadline candidate. If Ossenfort had traded him during the offseason, Arizona just might have gotten a good haul for him. Perhaps even a first-round draft pick. But now? What? Would the team jump at the first third-round offer that is dangled? Then there is the money issue. Sweat is in the second year of a four-year $76 million deal, with $38 million guaranteed. This year he has a cap hit of $16.4 million. The final two years of the contract rise to $23.6 million. The market for defensive linemen has already begun. The Indianapolis Colts traded DE DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers. The Tennessee Titans traded star DL Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears. The only other pass rushers rumored to be traded before the November 10 deadline are Los Angeles Chargers EDGE rusher Khalil Mack and Sweat. The big question for Ossenfort: Which is better for the Cardinals this year and in following seasons? Have Josh Sweat on the roster, or have whichever rookie player that third-round draft pick creates? The Budda Man Safety Budda Baker is a fan favorite, and the desert is his only NFL team. He was a second-round selection in the 2017 NFL Draft out of Washington and has since gone to eight Pro Bowls, been named to the NFL All-Rookie Team, voted First Team All-Pro twice, Second Team All-Pro twice, and was the NFL solo tackles leader in 2019 (104). He had a career-high 164 total tackles in 2024 and has had 100+ tackles in six of his 10 seasons. So, why is Baker on this list? Anyone? Don’t ask him. He appears to be happy with the Cardinals. He told ESPN Arizona : “My approach is I’m here. I’m here. I want to win. I want to be here. And I’m just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I’ll still be here. If not, I mean, it’s a business. I understand at the end of the day, and that’s it.” Perhaps it is the fact that he is a senior member of the roster. Or maybe it is the amount of money the Cardinals are paying him. He is in the final year of a three-year, $54 million deal in which his cap hit this year is $19.2 million. Ossenfort will have to sign Baker to another extension or trade him. But in fairness, it seems like every year, when the media begins to write articles about the impending NFL trade deadline, Baker’s name seems to leak out as a possible candidate. Baker has noticed: “My name has been attached to trade rumors for like five, six years now. So, at the end of the day, I’m here, be where your feet are. I’m happy to be a Cardinal and just focus on getting a “W” this week versus the Cowboys.” The NFL is in the entertainment profession. It is also a business with so many moving…

Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With the NFL trade deadline just under two weeks away, November 10th, the Arizona Cardinals have some decisions to make. They are clearly in a transition with their team and roster, and that could mean moving on from high priced veterans that are at the end of their football time. ESPN came out with their “ Ranking the top 25 candidates to move, plus team fits ” article and the Arizona Cardinals had two players listed at candidates to be moved. From ESPN: 3. Josh Sweat, Edge, Arizona Cardinals What Fowler is hearing: Rival teams could see him getting moved. “Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense to me,” an NFC exec said. “That’s a profile fit.” Rumblings persist that Sweat would want a new contract — he’s in the second year of a four-year, $76 million deal — and that could complicate things. But many teams are looking for an edge rusher. 9. Budda Baker, S, Arizona Cardinals What Fowler is hearing: A few wins won’t camouflage Arizona’s transitional state — and it needs draft capital to finish the rebuild. Baker, who has seven consecutive Pro Bowls and has 3.5 sacks on the season, could help get the Cardinals some extra picks. Long a favorite in coaching circles, Baker would garner strong interest. He’s owed $16.2 million this year and $17.8 million next year. People I’ve talked to believe the Cardinals should try to get something for Baker. Trading Sweat at this juncture seems like a forgone conclusion, especially with him being relatively healthy through the first seven weeks of the season after an offseason of no work with the team. So, getting something for Sweat now makes sense. Baker is a tough one. He is entering the legacy phase of his time in Arizona, where his on field work for a miserable defense isn’t quite as good as it was years ago, but he is still likely their best defensive player (which is another article in itself of why this isn’t good). However, on a team that just needs safety help, he likely would be a major asset. The problem, is a late day two or even worse a day three pick worth moving on? What are your thoughts?

full_text: Jones spent time in Atlanta as both a quarterback and head coach, leaving a unique mark on the franchise’s history. The Atlanta Falcons have lost another familiar figure from their history, as former quarterback and head coach June Jones passed away on Thursday at the age of 73. Jones had a lengthy football career that took him across the NFL, college football, and beyond, but his connection to Atlanta was particularly unique. It’s not often that a player gets the opportunity to return to the same franchise as a coach, much less lead the team as its head coach. Jones was one of the rare individuals who experienced both sides of that relationship with the Falcons. Jones originally joined Atlanta as an undrafted quarterback in 1977, spending five seasons with the franchise through 1981. Primarily serving as a backup, he appeared in 17 games and threw for 923 yards and three touchdowns. His playing career wasn’t particularly memorable statistically, but his time in Atlanta would prove to be just the beginning of his relationship with the franchise. After transitioning into coaching, Jones eventually returned to Atlanta in 1991 as offensive coordinator under Jerry Glanville. When Glanville departed following the 1993 season, Jones was promoted to head coach, a position he held from 1994 through 1996. His most successful season came in 1995, when the Falcons finished 9-7 and earned their first playoff appearance since 1991. That team featured quarterback Jeff George, who threw for 4,143 yards and 24 touchdowns, along with offensive standouts like Terance Mathis, Eric Metcalf, and Craig “Ironhead” Heyward. Atlanta’s season ultimately ended with a Wild Card loss to the Green Bay Packers, but Jones had helped deliver one of the franchise’s relatively rare postseason appearances of that era. Jones finished his three seasons as Falcons head coach with a 19-29 record. While his tenure had its ups and downs, his impact on the game extended well beyond wins and losses in Atlanta. A longtime advocate of the run-and-shoot offense, Jones was known for his innovative approach to the passing game. He would later find considerable success at the University of Hawaii, where he helped transform a struggling football program into a national contender. In 2007, he guided Hawaii to an undefeated regular season and a Sugar Bowl appearance, one of the most memorable accomplishments of his coaching career. He also coached at SMU and continued working in professional football, building a career that spanned multiple leagues and several decades. For Falcons fans, Jones will be remembered as someone who experienced the franchise from perspectives few others ever have. He wore the uniform, stood on the sidelines, and helped guide Atlanta to the postseason during a period when those opportunities were far from guaranteed. His time with the Falcons was only one chapter of a remarkable football life, but it was a meaningful one nonetheless. We extend our condolences to Jones’ family, friends, and everyone who had the opportunity to know and work with him.
