summary: The trade was reported earlier this morning. The Tennessee Titans announced it in a statement and at a press conference shortly thereafter. And now the Chicago Bears have made it official. The Bears traded a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Titans for Simmons and a 2028 […]
full_text: STARKVILLE, MISSISSIPPI - SEPTEMBER 05: Tennessee Titans player Jeffery Simmons reacts during the game between the Mississippi State Bulldogs and the ULM Warhawks at Davis Wade Stadium on September 05, 2026 in Starkville, Mississippi. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The trade was reported earlier this morning. The Tennessee Titans announced it in a statement and at a press conference shortly thereafter. And now the Chicago Bears have made it official. JEFFERY SIMMONS IS A CHICAGO BEAR 🐻⬇️ — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 30, 2026 The Bears traded a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Titans for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The Bears issued a statement on their website from general manager Ryan Poles. “We are excited to welcome Jeffery Simmons and his family to Chicago. We extend our gratitude to the Tennessee Titans and Mike Borgonzi for their partnership and collaboration throughout this process. We are fortunate to have the opportunity to add a player, and a human, like Jeffery to our team, and we look forward to Jeffery’s leadership and command as we continue to work toward sustained success.” Head coach Ben Johnson also had a statement. “Jeffery is one of the most respected players in the National Football League. Jeffery has proven to be one of the most impactful run defenders and disruptive pass-rushers in the NFL, and yet, through his leadership, Jeffery will have the opportunity to create a positive impact across our entire team. We look forward to the work ahead.” Simmons is in Chicago, and presumably there will be a press conference on Friday. The Bears also have two more practices scheduled (Friday and Saturday), plus a walk-through on Sunday before flying out to Washington for their Monday Night Football game against the Seattle Seahawks. Touched down in Chi-Town 📍 pic.twitter.com/WZJyhFLHm3 — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 30, 2026 Chicago GM Ryan Poles has known Tennessee GM Mike Borgonzi since at least 2008, when Poles was a grad assistant at Boston College, and Borgonzi was an assistant recruiting coordinator. They also worked together in the Kansas City Chiefs organization from 2009 to 2021. “Jeff (Simmons) has been an elite player in this organization both on and off the field,” Borgonzi said via the Titans site . “My respect and admiration for him is probably more than any player I’ve been around. … These are tough decisions, and at no point any time since I’ve been here did we every try to trade Jeffery Simmons – we’ve gotten a lot of phone calls, but it never really crossed my mind. “I got a phone call late last night from a person I have known for a while, Ryan Poles, GM with the Bears, and he’s really the only person that came out and said: Would you accept this?” Borgonzi took Poles’ offer to controlling owner Amy Adams Strunk and head coach Robert Saleh, and they decided to accept. “We thought this was the best decision moving forward, but also, it’s a really hard decision,” Borgonzi said. Amy loves Jeff as a player, as a person. Every teammate in the locker room does. This was not easy, but we felt it was the best decision to really sustain success in the future here and to really build through the draft, and that gave us the opportunity here to really accelerate the process.” The trade made sense for the 1-6 Titans, who need to rebuild, but it also made sense for the 5-2 Bears, who need an impact defender as they push for the postseason and the Super Bowl. The most impactful defensive tackle in the game today will now don Navy and Orange. Big Jeff in the house 🏠 pic.twitter.com/DOHoR9DECB — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 30, 2026

title: The Bears now have the best DT in the NFL
summary: The Chicago Bears were the talk of the NFL world on Thursday, as they traded a package headlined by two first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. From a draft capital perspective, it’s the largest in-season trade made so far this season, and it’s the most aggressive trade that Bears […]
full_text: The Chicago Bears were the talk of the NFL world on Thursday, as they traded a package headlined by two first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. From a draft capital perspective, it’s the largest in-season trade made so far this season, and it’s the most aggressive trade that Bears general manager Ryan Poles has made for a player. With the Nov. 10 trade deadline looming near, the expectation was that the Bears would remain active in discussions to add talent on the defensive side of the ball. That part wasn’t particularly surprising, but what was surprising was the fact that Simmons got dealt, especially after the Titans signed him a massive contract extension just this offseason. As a result of that extension, the Bears have Simmons under contract until 2030, and they acquire a relatively light cap hit for the 2027 season compared to what his annual average salary is. That long-term contract security likely played a role in why Tennessee was able to get multiple first-round picks for him. Bears general manager Poles knows that the NFC is wide open this year, and he’s making an all-out push for the Bears to win the Super Bowl, particularly within the next two years. In a conference where all of the top teams are either underperforming, weak on one side of the ball, or banged up with injuries, Chicago had a legitimate chance to win before acquiring Simmons. The Bears had a major weakness at the defensive tackle position. They now have arguably the best defensive tackle in the entire NFL on their roster. Analytically, it would be hard to argue against that statement. With a 98.9 PFN DT Impact grade , Simmons has far and away the best grade of any defensive tackle in the NFL. He’s over five points higher in grading than Dexter Lawrence, who himself has been a phenomenal addition for the Cincinnati Bengals’ defense. Simmons has graded as a top-ten player by that metric in six of the last seven years, and he led the league in the metric in 2025 as a first-team All-Pro, as well. When you look at the individual statistical categories, it’s not hard to see why he grades so highly: New #Bears DT Jeffery Simmons’ rank among defensive tackles this year: • 98.9 PFN DT Impact grade (1st) • 4.0 sacks (T-1st) • 38 tackles (1st) • 17.4 disruption EPA (1st) The best DT in the entire NFL comes to Chicago. pic.twitter.com/Y9b2VdGm2T — Jacob Infante (@jacobinfante24) October 29, 2026 That’s not all. Simmons is also double-teamed at a well above-average rate, yet he still generates run stops at a well above-average rate. How often are DTs double teamed in the run game and their overall grade stopping the run pic.twitter.com/e1EIoR9BuV — Jrfortgang (@throwthedamball) October 28, 2026 Not only is Simmons a force multiplier whose sheer presence commands double-team blocks, thus creating more one-on-one opportunities for his teams, but he’s also able to shed double-team blocks much better than the average NFL defensive tackle. Elite pass-rushing defensive tackles are incredibly hard to come by, and the Bears now have one of them on their roster. This should be extremely beneficial to defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, who has dialed up a blitz-heavy approach in lieu of a lacking four-man rush from his defensive line. Having Simmons up front makes their double-mug A-gap blitz look that much more dangerous, because not only do you have to worry about determining who’s rushing the passer and who’s dropping back into coverage, but you also need to know where Simmons is on the field at all times. This is one of the biggest splashes Chicago has made in recent memory, and arguably in team history. Simmons gives them an elite player at a premier position who’s in his physical prime, and it happens to come at arguably their biggest weakness on the roster. It’s a good day to be a Bears fan.

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Jamree Kromah #59 of the Chicago Bears lines up before a play during an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In case you missed it (and if so, where the heck have you been?), the Chicago Bears have acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, along with a 2028 fifth-round pick, in exchange for Chicago’s 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-rounder. The Bears have not yet announced the deal, but today they cleared a spot on the 53-man roster by waiving defensive end Jamree Kromah. Kromah was inactive for Chicago’s first five games this season but played in the last two, recording 2 tackles and a tackle for loss in 28 defensive snaps. Simmons is expected to take his physical on Friday, and the deal will become official then. UPDATE: The Bears have officially announced the trade. The Bears also signed 29-year-old cornerback Josh Butler to the practice squad today. Butler (6’, 192) went undrafted out of Michigan State (2015–2019), and he began his professional career in the Spring League in 2021. In 2023, he played in the USFL before landing with the Dallas Cowboys from 2023-2025 (he tore his ACL in 2024), where he played in 6 games with 3 starts. He spent a couple of recent weeks on the Ottawa Redblacks’ practice roster in the Canadian Football League, but was let go on October 22. title: Ryan Poles shows Bears fans he means business with Jeffery Simmons trade
summary: Now that’s how you read the cards on the table, Ryan Poles. With the rest of the NFL world kicking off the trade deadline madness a few weeks early, the Chicago Bears general manager has been in the thick of things early on, putting feelers out for the likes of former Indianapolis Colts Quenton Nelson […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 8: Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans celebrates after making a stop during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears, at Soldier Field on September 8, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that’s how you read the cards on the table, Ryan Poles. With the rest of the NFL world kicking off the trade deadline madness a few weeks early, the Chicago Bears general manager has been in the thick of things early on, putting feelers out for the likes of former Indianapolis Colts Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner before they were traded to the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers, respectively. But we didn’t have to wait much longer for him to cash in. Poles’ massive trade for now-former Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, in exchange for their next two first-round picks and this year’s fourth-rounder (while getting a 2028 fifth-round pick in return), might be the biggest stunner of the deadline season so far. Not just because it actually happened, but because it signaled a dedication to the shift Poles has been hinting at from bargain-hunter to big-game hunter. The time to compete is over. Winning time is here. The Bears, at 5-2, are firmly in the mix with the best playoff teams out there in the NFC and have a young quarterback in Caleb Williams who has played about as well as anyone in the league the last few weeks. But the defense, while over-performing for a short stretch there, still lacked a difference-maker up front to make them a true force on the side of the ball. The 29-year-old Simmons, who is PFN’s number one defensive tackle, and who grades among the NFL’s top-15 defensive interior players according to Pro Football Focus , is without question one of the league’s most disruptive interior pass-rushers, changes that equation. It’s the sort of move that pushed teams like the New England Patriots and Seahawks, who brought in Milton Williams and DeMarcus Lawrence, respectively, last season, over the top: a disruptive force in the middle that offenses have to account for. (Getting him on the field against Nelson on Monday Night Football, for example, could be an awesome battle.) And it’s precisely what the Bears haven’t had for years. Given the price, it might be the only major move the Bears make, unless there’s someone who can be had for a future Day 3 pick. (Let’s have a moment of silence for the dream of bringing Khalil Mack back to Chicago. I was looking forward to it.) But it’s worth the price the Bears paid for it as long as Simmons remains what he is for the next few years. One thing’s for sure: Poles isn’t messing around. He knows he doesn’t have long before Williams costs an arm and a leg. He knows how few opportunities most teams get to be great and truly compete for a title. And he’s acted that way heading into this trade deadline. Poles understands the assignment. Now, it’s time to see how his designs work out.

title: Week 8 game preview: Chicago Bears vs. Seattle Seahawks
summary: Good teams play in big games and the Chicago Bears have a big game this week. They hit road to play the Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks. And they’ll do it with a brand new All-Pro defensive tackle! Jeffery Simmons is a Bear! The Bears are proving themselves to be one of the best offenses in […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates against the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good teams play in big games and the Chicago Bears have a big game this week. They hit road to play the Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks. And they’ll do it with a brand new All-Pro defensive tackle! Jeffery Simmons is a Bear! The Bears are proving themselves to be one of the best offenses in the league with one of the best rising-star quarterbacks. And their head coach and quarterback face a huge test against one of the league’s best defenses. Chicago didn’t fare so well in their first defensive test of the year, against the Minnesota Vikings. However, the weather was a factor in that game, like it or not. Plus, Caleb Williams didn’t finish the game. Excuses, maybe, but also realities. This matchup has a lot of great storylines and will be a measuring stick for the Bears to see how they compete against the league’s best. It feels like a game with playoff implications. It feels like a game worthy of the Monday Night Football spotlight. It will be the first game in November for the Bears, too. When teams really start to separate themselves. Let’s meet the Seahawks. Seattle Seahawks SB Nation site : Field Gulls Record: 4-3, second in the NFC West Last week: 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs Game day, time, TV: Monday, 7:15 p.m. CT, ESPN Spread: Seattle -3.5 Bears all-time record against: 8-12, including 2-0 postseason Historical meeting: The Bears have never beaten the Seahawks in the month of November. In the second-ever meeting between the teams, the Seahawks beat the Bears 31-29 in week 10 of 1978. The Bears fell behind 21-9 with Jim Zorn hitting Steve Largent twice for touchdowns and Sherman Smith rushing for another. But Chicago made a strong comeback. Roland Harper scored on a 20-yard pass from Mike Phipps. After another Smith touchdown, Walter Payton scored from 7 yards out, drawing the Bears within six. The Seahawks drove down the field and tacked on another field goal to go up 31-22. Phipps threw a pick but Sam McCullum intercepted Zorn right back. Phipps put together a good drive and Harper scored a 2-yard TD with 40 seconds left. The Bears managed to recover the onside kick but with 12 seconds left, from Seattle’s 46-yard line, Phipps’ pass was intercepted to end the game. Last meeting: Who could forget the awful, terrible 6-3 Thursday Night Football game? Thomas Brown was coaching the Bears. It was a defensive slugfest. Or a total offensive mess. Depends on how you remember it. The most memorable play didn’t count, as Caleb Williams rolled out and threw an off-platform pass to Rome Odunze four a touchdown. It was called back for offensive holding. (I cannot find a clip online, but I remember it was awesome). Offense: The Seahawks offense ranks 13th in points and 15th in yards. Their passing offense is 16th and their rushing offense ranks 17th. Sam Darnold (62.1 pct. cmp./1,290 yds./8 TD/8 INT) currently leads the league in interceptions, but played a lot better last week. Unless you’ve been living under a rock, you likely know about Jaxon Smith-Njigba (58 rec./867 yds./8 TD). Beyond him are AJ Barner (19/180/0), Cooper Kupp (18/199/1), deep threat Rashid Shaheed (16/163/0) and George Holani (12/88/0). Jadarian Price (28 att./119 yds./0 TD) is injured, but expected to return to practice this week along with Zach Charbonnett (no stats in 2026 yet). In their absence, it’s been Emanuel Wilson (111 att./403 yds./3 TD) and Holani (26/108/1). Defense: Seattle’s defense comes into Monday night as one the league’s best. They rank fourth in points allowed and first in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks first in passing yards and sixth in rushing. The loaded unit stars Nick Emmanwori (27 tkls/3 TFL/2 sk/1 PD/7 QB hits), DTs Leonard Williams (3 sk/7 TFL/9 QB hits/1 PD), Byron Murphy (3 sk/ 24 tkls/5 TFL/6 QB hits) Derick Hall (3 sk/19 QB hits/3 TFL/1 FF/1 FR) and Ernest Jones (3 sk/68 tkls/3 TFL/2 QB hits/1 INT/3 PD) and Devon Witherspoon (41 tkls/3 PD/3 TFL/1 QB hits) Other playmakers are Julian Love (2 INT/6 PD/24 tkls/2 TFL), Nehemiah Pritchett (13 tkls/4 PD/2 INT) and Josh Jobe (27 tkls/1 PD/1 INT/1 TFL). Key matchups: This is a top offense against a top defense. The Bears are going to have to play disciplined football. Take what their given, take shots when they can, use play-action to suck in the LBs. On defense, stop JSN. That’s no easy task. The Seahawks can find a running game if Price and/or Charbonnett are back. Anyway to get pressure on Sam Darnold is good though; we know what happens when he is pressured. Key stats The Seahawks haven’t allowed a 300-yard passer this season. The Rams are the only team with more than 300 passing yards against Seattle since week 2 of last season. Seattle has lost only three times at home going back to the beginning of last season. The 49ers are the only team to beat Seattle at home during this span Despite their strong numbers, the Seahawks have allowed opponents to score on 78.6 percent of their trips inside of the red zone. The Seahawks’ 13 offensive turnovers on the season rank fourth-most in the league. Their 12 defensive turnovers rank third-most. Seattle is allowing a league-low 144.4 passing yards per game and the second-worst passer rating of 72.6. Only the Vikings allow a worse QB rating Can the Bears hang with a team as good as the Seahawks? How will their offense and QB measure up against Seattle’s defense?

title: Chicago Bears Acquire All-Pro Jeffery Simmons
summary: Since the start of spring, we’ve tracked the Chicago Bears’ need to bolster their defensive line by any means possible. So far this regular season, after minimal moves were made beforehand, that deficiency has been magnified considerably. A team pursuing their first Super Bowl championship in decades had to make a move. Consider those deficiencies […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Jeffery Simmons #98 of the Tennessee Titans celebrates after recovering a fumble against the Indianapolis Colts during the third quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Since the start of spring, we’ve tracked the Chicago Bears’ need to bolster their defensive line by any means possible. So far this regular season, after minimal moves were made beforehand, that deficiency has been magnified considerably. A team pursuing their first Super Bowl championship in decades had to make a move. Consider those deficiencies addressed. Per Tom Pelissero , NFL Insider for the Ringer and Netflix, the Chicago Bears have agreed to a deal with the Tennessee Titans that will send 4-time Pro Bowler and 2025 1st Team All-Pro Jeffery Simmons to the Monsters of the Midway. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the trade includes two first-round picks in 2027 and 2028 plus a 2027 fourth-rounder heading to Tennessee, with Simmons and a fifth-round pick in 2027 coming back to Chicago. Never mind the fact that arguably the NFL’s biggest pass-rushing menace amongst interior defensive linemen is now under Dennis Allen’s control up front. The 29-year-old Simmons is a dominant force in all phases of the game. This includes an unbelievable 76 combined tackles registered in 2024. So far in Simmons’ 2026 campaign, he’s tallied 4.0 sacks and 13 QB pressures along with 38 combined tackles while playing in a similar 4-man front. Currently, his pass rush production ties Austin Booker for the team lead in sacks and trumps everyone in pressures. The 6-4, 305-pound tackle in Jeffery Simmons, who produced a career-high 11 sacks and 21 QB pressures in 2025, projects as the perfect fit alongside Grady Jarrett to beef up their defensive interior. The draft capital and cap space being allocated for this move could not have been used for a better deal. This is the type of rare mid-season trade Super Bowl contenders earmark and pursue to close the gap. You had best believe Ryan Poles is “all in” for 2026. LFG.

title: The Bengals’ real need at NFL trade deadline may not be in the offensive backfield
summary: It’s that time of year. The trade deadline is creeping up (Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET), the Bengals are 4-2 and coming off a 35-13 beatdown of the Ravens, and two of the biggest names at running back are reportedly on the table. Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis. Saquon Barkley in Philadelphia. If you’ve spent […]
full_text: It’s that time of year. The trade deadline is creeping up (Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET), the Bengals are 4-2 and coming off a 35-13 beatdown of the Ravens, and two of the biggest names at running back are reportedly on the table. Jonathan Taylor in Indianapolis. Saquon Barkley in Philadelphia. If you’ve spent any time on Bengals Twitter this week, you’ve seen the photoshops, debates and talking points. And I get it. Chase Brown hasn’t looked like Chase Brown this year. In Baltimore, while the offense was hanging 35 straight points in the second half, he finished with 11 carries for 39 yards. Samaje Perine has been somewhat effective in a supplemental role (4.1 yards per carry), but the longest run by either him or Brown has been 15 yards this season. That’s been the story this season—a lack of explosive run plays. But ESPN’s Dan Graziano made a case this week: the Bengals should be buyers at the deadline. Just maybe not at running back. The numbers aren’t pretty Let’s not sugarcoat it. Through six games, Brown has 82 carries for 285 yards. That’s 3.5 yards a pop with one rushing touchdown. He hasn’t topped 80 yards in a game, and he’s been held to 61 or fewer in five of six. His share of the carries has slipped too, from about 72 percent over the first four games to roughly 49 percent since, with Samaje Perine eating into the workload. Perine himself had a rough stretch in Weeks 2-4, logging eight carries for 22 yards (2.8 yards per carry), zero touchdowns, and a long run of just five yards. They’re both still catching the ball: 28 grabs for 143 yards for Brown, and seven for 61 yards on Perine’s statline. But nobody’s confusing this with last season. Why not Taylor or Barkley? Graziano’s argument comes down to three things, and they’re hard to argue with. The price. Both backs cost a lot, in salary and in what you’d have to send back. That’s a steeper hill for Cincinnati than for most teams. It’s not who the Bengals are. In Graziano’s words, “it would be very unlike Cincinnati to surrender draft capital for them.” This front office builds through the draft and pays its own. Shipping picks for a 27-plus-year-old running back on a big deal would be a total departure. While the Bengals deviated from this a bit this offseason, that was much more of an outlier than a possible trend. Brown has earned some rope. Remember last year? He started slow then too, and finished with 1,019 rushing yards, a team-record 69 catches, 1,456 scrimmage yards and 11 total touchdowns. That guy is still in there. Instead, Graziano would look at linebackers and defensive backs first. And if the Bengals want to juice the offense, he’d go after an offensive lineman or a tight end before a running back. What’s the plan going forward? Here’s the part I keep coming back to: 3.5 yards a carry is rarely a one-man problem. When a back who just ran for over 1,000 yards suddenly can’t find room, I look at the guys in front of him first. Swap in Taylor or Barkley behind the same blocking, and I’m not convinced you get the version of them you’re paying for. However, the Bengals’ offensive line has been performing pretty well this season. So, scheming up a successful run game remains an issue under Zac Taylor. And, as noted in Baltimore, Cincinnati may be reverting back to more of a shotgun/spread look in a pass-first approach. This offense goes as Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins go. Baltimore just reminded everybody of that. The run game doesn’t need to carry the team. It needs to be good enough that defenses can’t sit back in two-high shells all day. While Cincinnati invested pretty heavily at safety, both Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger have been battling injuries. Erick All Jr. is on Injured Reserve, while linebacker remains a weakness on the defensive side of the ball. A big-ticket back helps one position and costs you the picks that keep this roster stocked. And if Duke Tobin’s going to spend draft capital, it may be better served to go toward a defense that still needs a difference-maker at linebacker or in the secondary, or to get a suitable replacement for All. That’s the move that could matter in January and cost less capital, as Graziano notes. “If I were the Bengals, I’d be looking harder at potentially available linebackers or defensive backs ahead of the trade deadline than running backs,” Graziano wrote. So, if the Bengals were to attack one of the positions, who would you like to see them target? Send us your thoughts down in the comments section!

title: Bengals Film Room: Money well spent on the defense this year
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals prioritized improving their defense this offseason. After six games played, Duke Tobin and the rest of the Bengals front office deserve praise. The additions of Bryan Cook, Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, and Dexter Lawrence as veterans have completely changed the outlook of the defense. You can even toss in the selection of […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals prioritized improving their defense this offseason. After six games played, Duke Tobin and the rest of the Bengals front office deserve praise. The additions of Bryan Cook, Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, and Dexter Lawrence as veterans have completely changed the outlook of the defense. You can even toss in the selection of Cashius Howell in the second round of the draft. The defensive line has seen the biggest difference in performance. The Bengals are tied for 1st in the league with 21 sacks to begin the season. This is even more astounding when you factor in that they have already had their bye week. A big reason for that success was the addition of Boye Mafe. After playing rotational snaps last season, there were some people that thought the Bengals might have paid too much when they signed him to a 3-year $60 million contract in free agency. That deal is looking like a steal now. He is 8th overall in pressures at his position on the season. He was able to record another 1.5 sacks in Baltimore. That puts his total through six games at 4.5 sacks for the season. Boye Mafe with the sack to force a punt. We forgive you Trey. pic.twitter.com/cx9CCFXu0Y — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Dexter Lawrence was a player that the Bengals went out and traded for. They gave up premium draft capital with the 10th overall selection. A move that has paid immediate dividends for them. Lawrence notched his fourth sack of the season, is an absolute force multiplier for the entire defense, and should be in the running for defensive player of the year. The Bengals gave him a one-year extension to his current contract at $28 million dollars, theoretically tying him to the franchise for two more seasons after this one. Another move that is money well spent. Thank you, New York Giants. Dexter Lawrence vs. Baltimore Ravens Lawrence should get serious consideration for the Defensive Player of the Year Award. He is that damn good. pic.twitter.com/MLKlPq8vH0 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The Bengals first signing during free agency was Bryan Cook. Safety has been a huge issue since the loss of Jessie Bates a few years back. Guys like Nick Scott and Geno Stone had not been the answer at free safety. They went out and got the best safety on the market. They gave the former Cincinnati Bearcat a 3-year deal worth slightly over $40 million total. While that is a big contract for a safety, it was a move that they absolutely needed to make. Cook has helped to stabilize the secondary, and rarely misses tackles. He is solid in coverage, can blitz at the line, and continually gets his guys lined up in the right spots. Bryan Cook vs. Baltimore pic.twitter.com/DYtHOMdTBR — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The Bengals also gave Jonathan Allen a good sized contract in free agency. After being let go by Minnesota, the Bengals quickly prioritized what Allen good give them, both as a veteran leader, and with his play on the field. He has been well worth the two-year $25 million contract they signed him to. Allen is tied for 10th overall in pressures on the season for defensive tackles with 21 total. Every week we see him bull rush an offensive lineman back into their quarterback. He has been solid against the run along with it, consistently discarding linemen to make plays at or behind the line of scrimmage. Jonathan Allen and Barrett Carter combining for the run stop near the line of scrimmage pic.twitter.com/6DETVaKaRK — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 The Bengals added Cashius Howell during the second round of the 2026 draft. Howell is a dynamic pass rusher that has been so close to getting sacks throughout the entire season. He was finally able to break through and notch his first one of the year during the Bengals three-and-out that started the second defensively. Duke Tobin and the rest of the front office did a great job in identifying talent through free agency and the draft, specifically on the defensive side of the ball. It certainly feels like money well spent to me. Cashius Howell sack forces a three-and-out to begin the second half for the defense pic.twitter.com/cpqJQpLVav — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026

title: Bengals News: Zac Taylor has faith in Jack Endries
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have a next man up problem at the backup tight end position. It was a position they seemed to be really deep at, but now a few injuries have them looking towards the end of the depth chart a little farther than some may like. Fear not, as the next player in […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have a next man up problem at the backup tight end position. It was a position they seemed to be really deep at, but now a few injuries have them looking towards the end of the depth chart a little farther than some may like. Fear not, as the next player in line is Jack Endries. He is a rookie tight end out of Texas who was selected in the Seventh Round, but was expected to go much sooner. Now he gets an early chance to prove that everyone made a mistake when evaluating him. “They’ll have to pick up the slack, and we’ll be counting on them to do that. Attention to detail has been really important to him. Waiting for his moment, you can tell. He never knew when his number was going to be called. He’s really got to know three different positions, and so I’ve got trust just watching him operate in practice and in meetings and in training camp that if needed he was going to be ready to go. There was a time where he wasn’t needed, because we had everybody healthy, and now’s that time. So I’m not nervous at all about using him. I think he’s earned the opportunity,” Taylor said, via Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com . Endries has a real chip on his shoulder. He really projected as a possible replacement for Mike Gesicki down the line, but he will clearly need to help fill the role that Noah Fant played last year that Erick All Jr. was commanding this season. It doesn’t fit his projected skill set, but we will see how much work he has put in learning that spot during the offseason and this year. Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! And it can happen when a team starts drinking the Kool-Aid a bit too much as a seemingly lesser team comes on the schedule. It is human nature to look at it and think it should be an easy win. That is why they play the game, though. There are a ton of people in Tennessee that will be playing for their football lives the rest of the season. Bengals’ Job Sunday Just Got a Lot Easier with Titans Trading Star Defensive Tackle It may be a sigh of relief now, but we will see Sunday how the Titans come out and play. At least the odds of Joe Burrow getting sacked went down a little bit, but this is still going to be a game this team needs to show up ready to play and not try and sleepwalk through. Why Ja’Marr Chase is happy when the Bengals’ other playmakers get the ball The first thing that helps is the team is winning a majority of their games. If he had a slow start and they were 2-4 instead it’d probably be a different tune. However, this should ultimately open things up for him more as teams doing everything to take him away still aren’t slowing down this offense. NFL News Bears acquire DT Jeffery Simmons from Titans in blockbuster trade People are saying the Bengals got a bargain, and in a way they did. However, Cincinnati’s Forst Round pick was established as the No. 10 overall pick. The Bears are 5-2 and with this trade hopefully will continue their winning ways. These two firsts could easily both be in the high teens or 20’s. NFL Week 8 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game It is easy to see why the experts have the confidence in the Bengals. The Bengals have a Top 5 scoring offense where the Titans rank near dead last in most offensive categories. It still feels a bit uneasy to see every expert going with almost a rout of Tennessee. Cam Heyward chirps back at Jared Verse ahead of Browns-Steelers rematch: ‘Bring it on’ Meh, Heyward deserves respect, but he is pretty off base about his team’s offensive line. That is the same offensive line that was grabbing and lifting Dexter Lawrence’s leg several times during their matchup. It is also kind of impossible to ignore the history of the players on that team for years now. He can be hype for the game, but he can’t be serious with this “we are operating in the scope of the game” act.

title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly: Bengals 35, Ravens 13
summary: Two halves, two completely different football teams. For 30 minutes on Sunday, the Bengals looked like they were still on their bye week. For the next 30, they looked like the best team in the AFC North. The final score was 35-13. Cincinnati improved to 4-2 and finally got that first division win. But a […]
full_text: Two halves, two completely different football teams. For 30 minutes on Sunday, the Bengals looked like they were still on their bye week. For the next 30, they looked like the best team in the AFC North. The final score was 35-13. Cincinnati improved to 4-2 and finally got that first division win. But a game like this deserves a full breakdown, warts and all. Let’s get into it. The Good Second-half Joe. After halftime, Joe Burrow went 16-of-18 for 249 yards and four touchdowns, which is a perfect 158.3 passer rating. The Bengals scored on five straight possessions and put up 298 yards and 19 first downs in the second half alone. Burrow finished 22-of-30 for 292 yards and four scores. He has 15 touchdown passes through six games, his most ever at this point in a season. Tee Higgins shows up when it counts. Higgins was shut out in the first half. In the second, he caught six passes for 148 yards, including a 44-yarder and the 13-yard go-ahead touchdown. That’s his 17th career 100-yard game, and he went over 6,000 career receiving yards in the process. No. 1 talks, No. 1 delivers. Burrow credited Ja’Marr Chase for lighting a fire at halftime. Chase then put the exclamation point on it with a 2-yard touchdown in the fourth, his 10th career score against Baltimore. The defense slammed the door. Baltimore didn’t score after halftime. It managed five first downs on six second-half drives and turned it over on downs on a fourth-and-2 at the Bengals’ 12 while trailing by a point. The Bengals scored on the very next drive. For the day, Huntley was sacked four times, with Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence II and rookie Cashius Howell (his first career sack) all getting home. Demetrius Knight Jr. added an interception. Derrick Henry, bottled up. Henry ran 17 times for 45 yards, a 2.6 average, and the Ravens averaged 3.1 yards a carry as a team. When you hold King Henry under 50 yards, you’re doing something right up front. Tight ends and the punter. Mike Gesicki (6-yard touchdown, his fourth straight game with a score) and Drew Sample (16-yard touchdown) each found the end zone. Ryan Rehkow dropped all four of his punts inside the 20. The Bad The run game is still stuck in neutral. Chase Brown had 11 carries for 39 yards, and the backs combined for 61 yards on 18 carries. Samaje Perine did punch in a touchdown. The passing game carried this one, but you can’t count on Burrow throwing for four touchdowns in a half every week. This offense needs to be able to run the ball when it has to. Huntley had a career day. A backup quarterback, with Lamar Jackson out for a third straight game, threw for a career-high 298 yards against this defense. Zay Flowers caught eight passes for 137 yards, including a 48-yard screen for a touchdown on Baltimore’s first drive. The second half was great. But the secondary gave up too many explosive plays early, and a better quarterback makes them pay. Baltimore let them off the hook. Baltimore had two red-zone trips in the first half that ended in field goals instead of touchdowns, and the Ravens committed 10 penalties for 57 yards. They also were in chip-shot field-goal range to begin the fourth quarter but opted to go for it on fourth down and failed. If they cash in on even one of those trips, this is a much tighter game. The Ugly That first half. There’s no way to dress this up. At halftime: Burrow was 6-of-12 for 43 yards. The Bengals had two first downs and crossed midfield once. Baltimore outgained them 258 to 59. The Ravens ran 39 plays to Cincinnati’s 19 and held the ball for 22:20 of the first 30 minutes. Baltimore converted 8 of 11 third downs, its most in a first half since 2018. Higgins didn’t have a catch. FOX19’s Jeremy Rauch called it “arguably the most incompetent half in the Joe Burrow era,” and I’m not going to argue with him. The defense couldn’t get off the field, and the offense couldn’t stay on it. That’s how you end up down 13-0 to a team starting its backup quarterback. The Bengals got away with it this time. They won’t against Buffalo, Kansas City, or anybody else they might see in January. The comeback deserves the headlines, but the coaching staff needs to spend this week figuring out why this team keeps coming out flat. Injuries and Erick All Jr. on I.R.: The safety position got banged up in this one, with Bryan Cook, Kyle Dugger, and Jordan Battle all getting dinged up in one form or another. Cook and Battle returned, but Dugger has a lingering injury. All landed on Injured Reserve this week, with the fear being that he yet again tore the ACL in the knee he did so twice before. It’s a sad end to his season, after coming back ahead of schedule this offseason and integrating himself well into the offense.

title: Bengals on pace for greatest differential of sacks allowed vs. defensive sacks in franchise history
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals had a real problem with both the pass rush and protecting Joe Burrow. Then they added Amarius Mims, Dylan Fairchild, and Dalton Risner to the line in 2024 and 2025. And then this past offseason, they went out and got Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe, and Cashius Howell. The result is […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 25: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals scrambles with the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the first quarter at M&T Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals had a real problem with both the pass rush and protecting Joe Burrow. Then they added Amarius Mims, Dylan Fairchild, and Dalton Risner to the line in 2024 and 2025. And then this past offseason, they went out and got Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe, and Cashius Howell. The result is a stunning turnaround. As of right now, they are on pace for the greatest differential between sacks allowed and defensive sacks since sacks were first tracked in 1982. The @Bengals are on track for their largest net differential between sacks allowed and defensive sacks in franchise history since sacks began being formally being tracked in 1982. #NFL #bengals Source: https://t.co/MXVQCl2PMv team stats pic.twitter.com/hVUpKzbRN4 — Logan Marshall NFL (@Logan1398) October 28, 2026 Currently, the Bengals have a +11 differential (Burrow has been sacked 10 times, while the defense has made 21 sacks), which puts them on pace to be +31 by season’s end. To put into perspective how far they’ve come, in 2020, the year Burrow was drafted, the Bengals were -31 . You read that right. That’s the second-worst year recorded for the franchise, after 2008, when they were -34. They’ve been negative every year they’ve had Burrow, but started to improve last year, when they were only -1. You can see the gradual progress by looking at their ranking of sacks allowed and defensive sacks per year in the Burrow era: 2020 – 28th and 32nd 2021 – 30th and 12th 2022 – 22nd and 29th 2023 – 25th and 18th 2024 – 22nd and 26th 2025 – 14th and 23rd 2026 – 5th and 1st

title: Trade for QB Justin Herbert? Browns fans split; have strong reaction to the idea
summary: When it comes to surprises so far in the 2026 NFL season, the Cleveland Browns 5-2 record, sitting atop the AFC North, is among the biggest. There are others, including the Minnesota Vikings being the lone undefeated team and the Los Angeles Chargers being the lone winless squad, but the Browns success in Year 1 […]
full_text: When it comes to surprises so far in the 2026 NFL season, the Cleveland Browns 5-2 record, sitting atop the AFC North , is among the biggest. There are others, including the Minnesota Vikings being the lone undefeated team and the Los Angeles Chargers being the lone winless squad, but the Browns success in Year 1 under HC Todd Monken has been fun for Cleveland fans and an interesting storyline for the NFL as a whole. A win in Week 8 would change things greatly for the Browns chances of turning “surprise” into “NFL playoff participants.” Cleveland’s success has come with five come-from-behind wins, with QB Deshaun Watson regaining a version of his elite past late in both halves of games . The rest of the time, the Browns have seen inconsistent play at the quarterback position. That, along with Watson heading into free agency after the season, leaves questions about the future of the position. Enter QB Justin Herbert and the winless Chargers: 🚨This is a serious question. It is not for content or memes. I am legitimately interested in the public opinion.🚨 Justin Herbert is 28 years old. He's got four years left on his deal (+ no trade clause) worth $24M, $36M, $52M, $50.5M. What would you offer in trade for him? — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 12, 2026 So, we asked Browns fans the same question and, so far, they are split almost right down the middle: A quick look at Herbert’s season shows why the idea of trading him is even being discussed publicly at all: 59% completion percentage 5 touchdowns 8 interceptions – Which leads the NFL Career-worst yards per attempt and significantly worst adjusted yards gained per pass attempt (2 strong QB metrics) Passer rating of 68.8 and QBR of 29.3 – By far his career worsts Chargers are 0-6 So, a lot of reasons for Los Angeles to potentially look to trade what was assumed to be their franchise quarterback and lots of reasons for Cleveland fans to be hesitant (or stronger words) about trading for him: As seen in the poll, not everyone was against the idea: A couple of our loyal readers brought up interesting points. First, dawngregry brought some straight facts followed by some opinions on where a trade might land: Then, Spidey mentioned a big variable: Would the Browns be gunshy to pull the trigger on another big QB deal after the Watson failed deal? In the end, a Herbert trade seems highly unlikely for a variety of reasons, including his no-trade clause. Cleveland also seems unlikely to upset the apple cart as they’ll head into the NFL trade deadline with a winning record, at worst, and potentially a commanding lead in the AFC North. Most likely, if Herbert were to be traded, the 2027 NFL offseason would be the earliest, when the Chargers could figure out what their future holds. For now, Browns fans are almost exactly split on the idea of trading for the struggling superstar, but the poll still has a little bit of time to change drastically. title: NFL predictions: Browns-Steelers square off in meaningful midseason match-up for once
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (5-2) take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. It’s Been 23 Years If I could put the meme from the Titanic here, I would, with respect to it having […]
full_text: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (5-2) take on the Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. It’s Been 23 Years If I could put the meme from the Titanic here, I would, with respect to it having been 23 years (which is a 22-game losing streak) since the Cleveland Browns have won a road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the regular season. We’ll always have that playoff victory over them, but we’re trying to keep focused on the unfathomable statistic of losing 22 in a row somewhere. Of course, the reason for that has largely been that the Browns have been a bad football team, while Pittsburgh has generally been good. But, it’s not like Cleveland hasn’t been able to beat Pittsburgh during that stretch at all. In fact, at home since 2003, the Browns are 10-13-1, including winning 7 of their last 8 games there. On the road, they are 1-22, with 22 straight losses. That 2003 match-up was one featuring Tim Couch as the Browns’ starting quarterback, as he went 20-of-25 for 208 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT, and 1 rushing TD in a 33-13 victory. Cleveland still have the classic quartet of Kevin Johnson , Quincy Morgan , Andre’ Davis , and Dennis Northcutt as their receivers, with Steve Heiden as their primary tight end. William Green ran 33 times for 115 yards. Pittsburgh was led by Tommy Maddox at quarterback, with Amos Zereoue and Jerome Bettis running and Hines Ward , Plaxico Burress , and Antwaan Randle El as their receivers. Phil Dawson was putting kicks through the uprights for the Browns. I was 14 years old back then, just starting high school. I’m 37 now, having been through college, had a full-time job for awhile, and started a family. It’s time we turned the corner for the Browns, isn’t it? Home-away records sometimes seem less valuable these days. I could go into context and say that Cleveland’s 2-2 road record this year was the team just not being prepared in Week 1, and also because of sloppy rain conditions against the Jets, and not because ‘they weren’t at home.’ But when you just look at the records straight up, the Browns are 3-0 at home. Also 3-0 at home this year? The Pittsburgh Steelers, with wins over the Falcons, Bengals, and Colts. They, like Cleveland, have had a relatively soft schedule this year, but it’s let them build some confidence and work out some things too. This game won’t be easy, but I’m excited for it. Those Darn Slow Starts Last week, I harped on the Browns needing to get their offense rocking, especially with KC Concepcion , and also needed the defense to stop allowing opening-drive scores. Cleveland accomplished half of that with the offense taking off, but the defense found themselves in a 14-0 hole before getting things back on track. Thinking back to the first Steelers game, Pittsburgh began the game with a 17-play, 73-yard drive that took up 9:48 of game clock. Then, until the fourth quarter, their drives were: interception, punt, missed field goal, field goal, punt, punt, and punt. It’s always been a known factor in the NFL that some teams can have greater success on their first drive with well-scripted sequences. But it’s a bit mind-blowing that this defense can play so well the rest of the game — which I’ve attributed to Mike Rutenburg’s ability to make adjustments — but they can’t get that stop, even out of dumb luck, on the first drive. I know Rutenburg would say that it doesn’t matter if that touchdown drive comes on the opening drive, or the fifth drive, they want to stop it. But setting the tone early will be a factor as some of these games get more serious. The last time these teams played, Cleveland erupted for 21 straight points in the second quarter. That isn’t going to happen every week (even though they erupted for 17 points in a row just last week, after being in a hole…) Here are some other notes: The running game was encouraging last week. I like some of the little things we’re seeing improve with team blocking, and I also like the adjustment to go under center more. I think Cleveland, in their efforts to make Deshaun Watson comfortable, have often gone from Shotgun, which can hurt the running game at times. Watson has been much more unphased this year, and I think we’re seeing how being under center can add some things to the ground game, quick passing game, and even springing someone like KC Concepcion open off of playaction. Speaking of Concepcion, the usage of him last week was picture perfect. Keep doing it — he is the one guy who can really propel this offense to the next level, and help open things up for other guys too. The number of crossing routes that Cleveland has started taking advantage of is perfect too. Jaylen Warren is the guy who the Browns need to stop. He’s averaging 5.5 yards per carry on the season, and with the return of Rico Dowdle last week, the duo has been very effective on the ground. I still fear Darnell Washington to a degree. The big tight end had a touchdown catch against the Browns, and has a touchdown catch in each of the past two games. I’d be tempted to put Emmanuel McNeil-Warren on him at times to see what happens. The big X-Factor this week that could throw a wrench in Cleveland’s chances is the fact that Tytus Howard might be out with a concussion. That would put Dawand Jones in as the starting right tackle. We all remember back in 2023, when Jones — in limited action — ‘shut down’ T.J. Watt , which got everyone excited about Jones’ future. It’s been a bit rough since then, and with injuries and lesser playing time, Jones hasn’t looked very sharp during fill-in duty. And then what happens if Jones goes down with an injury? I’m assuming that KT Leveston will be a gameday elevation from the practice squad, but remember, he was outright cut after being a contender for the starting right guard job in camp. Cleveland drafted Austin Barber to be a reserve offensive tackle, but he’s flourished at right guard. I suppose the they could shift Barber to right tackle, Elgton Jenkins to right guard, and then put Luke Wypler at center. On paper, that works for me. However, with the continuity these guys have built up, would they want to switch three linemen as opposed to just one? Fingers crossed that Jones not only stays healthy, but plays has a solid outing. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 3.5 point underdogs against the Steelers. The over/under is 39.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about if the running game so a breakthrough this past week, but he just appreciated the collective effort and improvements on first and second down: “Yeah, I mean, I think a lot of the things, we have been seeing improvement over the last couple weeks, so it was great to see the production that we had on Sunday. As far as breakthrough, I don’t know. I don’t know that any of our guys really look at it that way. I think that the things that we’ve been emphasizing to improve, we’ve been. We were a lot better on first and second down, which allowed us to get more runs called. You know, the more you’re on schedule, the more you’ll be able to run the ball. So, as far as breakthrough, I don’t know. I mean, we were certainly really happy to see the production that we did, and we’ll continue to try to improve.” Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg wouldn’t really give an answer to the slow start of the defense each week, other than they treat every drive the same as far as diagnosing what went wrong behind closed doors: In everything we do, when it is to our collective standard, we are constantly trying to get it better. So, whether it’s the first drive, something else, something we’re doing really well, it’s a constant under construction through the week of why, tell the truth, try and figure it out together and fight our a—- off really to fix it. And it’s a really cool process, collectively, as a staff and players.” Special teams coordinator…

title: Browns playoff odds: Big shift with Week 8 victory or loss to Steelers
summary: Few would have thought that the Cleveland Browns fans would be talking about realistic NFL playoff hopes heading into November. Instead, most thought the only focus would be on the 2027 NFL draft order, fans making other plans for the bye week and Thanksgiving, and wondering who the Browns might be trading away at the […]
full_text: Few would have thought that the Cleveland Browns fans would be talking about realistic NFL playoff hopes heading into November. Instead, most thought the only focus would be on the 2027 NFL draft order , fans making other plans for the bye week and Thanksgiving , and wondering who the Browns might be trading away at the NFL trade deadline. Instead, Week 8 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers will decide the top of the AFC North, Cleveland is linked to a number of rumored names at the deadline , and the focus on the NFL draft is tertiary, but still big given the Los Angeles Rams’ struggles . The playoff conversation is an interesting one. The over/under betting line on FanDuel has moved quite a bit, but the Browns are still not expected to make the playoffs, with +164 odds as of this writing . According to The Athletic, Cleveland currently only has a 48% chance to make the postseason and a 17% chance to win the division, despite currently sitting in first place with the third seed in the AFC. Week 8 versus the Steelers changes the odds quite a bit, according to The Athletic. A win in Pittsburgh jumps the visitor’s playoff odds to 67% and their division odds to 29%. A loss changes those numbers drastically: 38% for the postseason, 9% of winning the AFC North. For the Steelers, the numbers are similar: Current odds: Playoffs – 58%, Division – 21% With a Week 8 win: Playoffs – 67%, Division – 28% With a Week 8 loss: Playoffs – 40%, Division – 9% For fun, sweeping the AFC North (4 more victories) would run Cleveland’s playoff chances to 99% and division chances to 89%. That would also leave the Browns six other chances to get to double-digit wins. For now, that fun scenario is putting the cart before the horse. The outcome of Cleveland versus Pittsburgh in Week 8 is big enough on its own. Are you surprised how big of a swing a Week 8 game can have on playoff odds for both teams? title: Week 8 versus the Steelers shouldn’t be viewed as a litmus test for the Browns
summary: Going into the 2026 season, the expectations for the Cleveland Browns were low. A first-time head coach, Myles Garrett in Inglewood, a surplus of young offensive talent, but uncertainty at the quarterback position. A young, talented team but with valid question marks. Fast forward to late October, the Browns have a rare opportunity in front […]
full_text: Going into the 2026 season, the expectations for the Cleveland Browns were low. A first-time head coach , Myles Garrett in Inglewood , a surplus of young offensive talent, but uncertainty at the quarterback position. A young, talented team but with valid question marks. Fast forward to late October, the Browns have a rare opportunity in front of them. The team is 5-2 despite question marks on how legitimate the start is , but Sunday’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers shouldn’t be viewed as a litmus test between the two AFC North rivals. Both the Browns and the Steelers are 5-2, but Cleveland being 5-2 is more of a surprise than Pittsburgh. The last time these two teams played was a Thursday night game off the shores of Lake Erie, but the final score doesn’t indicate how close the actual game was. The Browns were the better team throughout the game, and it felt as if there was a shift in how this rivalry was going to go. The Steelers are not a bad football team; if anything, they are above average. Roster-wise, it’s essentially the same as last season but slightly better and a little older. Pittsburgh’s ceiling is a fringe playoff team, and if they were to make it, don’t expect them to win a game. However, Sunday’s game against the Steelers shouldn’t be viewed as a litmus test for the Cleveland Browns. For the Browns it’s more about proving that things are changing than how good of a team they actually are. The win over the Steelers in Week 4 was a slight shift. Yes, Cleveland has beaten Pittsburgh at home more frequently, but this season’s win felt different. The Browns, not the Steelers, were the aggressors throughout the game. Pittsburgh found a way to make it close, but Cleveland found a way to win. The Browns might not have a higher ceiling this season, but they are set up well enough for a better future than the Steelers due to their upside in terms of youth and talent. If Cleveland were to lose on Sunday, it wouldn’t matter as much because Pittsburgh shouldn’t be the standard for what the Browns want to be. If anything, it should be for what Cleveland should avoid: Being a middle-of-the-pack team with no upside is something most teams should avoid. Sunday’s game is important for both teams, but the Steelers have more pressure to win than the Browns due to what’s at stake for them. Overall, Sunday’s game is important, but it shouldn’t be viewed as a litmus test, just a vital game in the present in the AFC North. How would you describe Sunday’s Browns-Steelers matchup? title: Cleveland Browns news: A magical night in Pittsburgh
summary: The Cleveland Browns have their annual opportunity to end one of the NFL’s most egregious streaks this Sunday when they travel to Pittsburgh to face the Steelers. full_text: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have their annual opportunity to end one of the NFL’s most egregious streaks this Sunday when they travel to Pittsburgh to face the Steelers. It is bad enough that the Browns have won just three times in Pittsburgh since 1999, but it’s also been 23 years since the Browns won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh. Let that sink in for a moment. Now let’s turn back the clock and relive that October night in 2003 when the Browns took down the Steelers. Cleveland was circling the drain in head coach Butch Davis’ last full season with the team. And with quarterback Kelly Holcomb still nursing the “teeny-tiny fracture” in his leg, the Browns were back to starting Tim Couch for the nationally televised game. Couch opened the scoring by hitting André Davis with a six-yard touchdown pass for an early 7-0 lead. Cleveland pushed the margin to 13 points in the second quarter as Couch hit Kevin Johnson with a 9-yard pass. Couch added a nine-yard touchdown run just before the half to keep the lead at 13. Cleveland’s defense was energized in the second half, holding the Steelers to just three points, and putting an exclamation point on the evening when Daylon McCutcheon’s 75-yard interception return gave the Browns a comfortable 20-point lead midway through the third quarter. Phil Dawson would tack on a 22-yard field goal in the fourth quarter to make the final score 33-13. Couch finished the game 20-of-25 for 208 yards and three combined touchdowns in what turned out to be the last high point of his career. He made eight starts that season, the same as Holcomb, as the Browns followed up a playoff season by finishing 5-11. Even the most cynical of Browns fans would never have imagined that would be the last time the Browns would walk off the field in Pittsburgh on the right side of the scoreboard in a regular-season game. This year’s Browns team is better than the 2003 squad; it would be hard to argue otherwise, and Sunday presents an opportunity to back that up with a win. OK, enough of the history lesson. title: AFC North Week 8: 3 reasons the Browns should win, 3 reasons the Steelers should win
summary: The Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers have identical 5-2-0 records and are tied for the AFC North Division lead at almost the halfway point of this 2026 season. Actually, if the season were to end today, the Browns would be declared division winners based on their 27-24 win in Week 4. A win would give […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers have identical 5-2-0 records and are tied for the AFC North Division lead at almost the halfway point of this 2026 season. Actually, if the season were to end today, the Browns would be declared division winners based on their 27-24 win in Week 4. A win would give the Browns a 3-0 division record and sole possession of first place in the AFC North, which they have never won. Several Steelers Facebook fan pages are predicting Pittsburgh to run the table with their remaining games and finish 15-2-0. But it starts with the rubber match against Cleveland. RELATED: BREAKING THE THREE RIVERS JINX Sunday’s game at Pittsburgh is huge. The Cincinnati Bengals are one game behind at 4-2-0 and play the one-win Tennessee Titans. So, a loss by the Browns or Steelers, coupled with a Bengals win over a bad team, will place the entire division into disarray. And the schedule is just half over. Here are each team’s offensive and defensive rankings: Offense Passing Browns #24 Steelers #20 Rushing Browns #19 Steelers #20 i mean the aura is off the charts pic.twitter.com/uppIJfdtyW — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) October 2, 2026 Defense Passing Browns #7 Steelers #11 Rushing Browns #20 Steelers #7 What will it take to win this classic matchup? In the last 10 seasons, the Browns are 0-10 when they play at Pittsburgh in the regular season. They did win the playoff game 48-37 in 2020. The last regular-season game the Browns won was in 2003. 3 reasons the Browns should win against the Steelers Don’t let Pittsburgh get hot early The home crowd will become a huge advantage for the Steelers. The Browns’ defense must contain their offense on that first drive and not allow any momentum to happen early in the game. The defense needs to bring an extra man on passing downs since the pass rush just isn’t happening with four defensive linemen. An opening Steelers touchdown will allow the home crowd to elevate the noise level when Cleveland gets their turn, which can lead to a three-and-out, or worse, a turnover. Nothing worse than a 14-point deficit early in the game. Challenge their receivers on the line of scrimmage. Make second down more manageable The trick to getting a more manageable second down is to provide positive yardage on first-down plays. Try more short throws or swing passes to the running back. Pittsburgh is good against the run, so the short passing game can set up the few carries that the Browns attempt. By using TE Harold Fannin and RB Quinshon Judkins on short gains, this forces tackling demons such as LB Patrick Queen to have to consistently drop back into coverage instead of supporting the rushing attack. If Cleveland gets stuck in a lot of third-and-long, the outcome will not be favorable. Those Pittsburgh defensive ends, such as T.J. Watt and Keeanu Benton, live for third-and-long. Denzel Ward vs. D.K. Metcalf Ward is currently the #1-ranked cornerback in the league according to Pro Football Focus . Metcalf is ranked #27 on NFL.com in receiving yards (374) and #28 in receptions (32). This is Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers’ go-to guy in the passing game. If Ward can neutralize Metcalf, not bite on the double moves, and keep him to pedestrian numbers in this game, it will force Rodgers to rely on other receivers and his tight end, Pat Friermuth. The Steelers are hurting in the receiver room as Pittsburgh only has Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen healthy. Ben Skowronek has been ruled out. They have four receivers on their practice squad, and it is expected that veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling will be moved up for the Browns contest. Ward will have his work cut out for him as Metcalf is 6’-4” and a beefy 235 pounds. Metcalf’s signature move is an intermediate crossing pattern, and then he steps it up past the post safety when he attempts to cut it. Pittsburgh fans are expecting a huge game out of Metcalf. Ward must be at his best. 3 reasons the Steelers should win against the Browns Run defense The Browns just now got their two starting running backs to return to the field, and both Q and Dylan Sampson had an excellent showing last week against the Titans. But the Steelers’ defensive front is not Tennessee’s defensive front seven. They ranked #7 in the league for a reason. A lot is written about Watt, Benton, and Queen, but it is LB Payton Wilson who is balling out and making plays. He is ranked #10 in total tackles with 61 and leads the team almost every week. Queen has 48 total tackles and is a steady force on their defense. Both linebackers have a single sack and not much in terms of pressures and QB hits because the defense relies on its front four to get pressure on the opposing team’s quarterback. Another defender that is a beast is S Jaquan Brisker, who is used in blitz packages and is a good run stopper. Run on Pittsburgh? Guess again. Keep the run game trend going The Steelers have found their rushing attack. Last weekend, they rushed for 148 yards. That pairs nicely with the fact that Cleveland is bottom-third in rushing defense. The Browns’ defense shows a lot of aggression that may have to tone it down and stay home, especially on the edge where containment must be maintained. DE Jared Verse is known for leaving the corners open as he attacks the center of the defense. Stay home and force Pittsburgh RB Jaylen Warren to the inside. He runs a 4.55, so he is always looking to hit the edge and then kick into another gear. Warren is ranked #7 in rushing yardage (561), #14 in rushing attempts, has zero fumbles, and has scored a single touchdown. He has rushed for over 100 yards three times this year, including 101 this past weekend. Expect the Steelers to pound the rock early and often. Pressure Deshaun Watson in the pocket On passing downs, Watson is averaging 2.4 seconds on average per pocket presence . He has just three throwaway passes in seven games, which is a remarkable stat. In the game against the Titans, Watson showed what he can do if he is given enough time to survey the field to find the open man. He has an excellent on-target ratio of 70.5%, but the majority of those numbers are from the pocket. When Watson was at Clemson University and the pocket collapsed, he would take off with many huge rushing gains. But with Cleveland, after he leaves the pocket, he is still looking downfield to throw and will run if necessary. That is when Watson does the least amount of damage, as evidenced by his 36 bad throws so far. He has endured the fourth-most pressures with 67, so teams are regularly getting near him. The Steelers have the horses to put good pressure on Watson on passing downs, while Cleveland is starting two rookie offensive linemen. title: Cowboys vs. Cardinals: Matchups to watch in Week 8
summary: The Dallas Cowboys got a much needed victory over the Philadelphia Eagles last week and will be looking to extend their win streak in the Week 8 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. This is a team that beat them 27-17 last year in a surprising upset, and would probably love nothing more than to do […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys got a much needed victory over the Philadelphia Eagles last week and will be looking to extend their win streak in the Week 8 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. This is a team that beat them 27-17 last year in a surprising upset, and would probably love nothing more than to do so once again. To avoid another upset, Dallas needs to take advantage of certain matchups to sway the game in their favor, which we discuss below. RB Javonte Williams vs. Cardinals’ run defense Javonte Williams is coming off his best game of the season, and one of the best of his entire professional career, after rushing for 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries last week against the Eagles. His physicality and ability to pick up chunk yards helped balance out the Cowboys offense, which led to one of their most productive games of the season. The game plan should look much the same this week against the Cardinals who currently ranked 23 rd in the league and run defense, allowing 126.3 rushing yards per game. If the Cowboys offensive line continues to open holes like they did last week, Williams should have his second 100+ rushing yard game of the season and help sway the game in Dallas’ favor. Cowboys’ secondary vs. Cardinals’ TE Trey McBride Trey McBride is the Cardinals best, and most consistent, offensive weapon. He is coming off his best game of the year against the Broncos when he caught 10 passes for 111 yards and a touchdown, and will be looking to repeat that type of success against the Cowboys struggling secondary. Last year Dallas was able to hold him to just five catches for 55 yards and a TD and will attempt to do the same in this Week 8 matchup. McBride’s production and the outcome of the game could depend on who Christian Parker assigns to contain Arizona’s All-Pro TE. Will it be the young rookie Caleb Downs, or someone else? Whoever it is will have their hands full against one of the league’s best TEs. RT Terence Steele vs. Cardinals’ OLB Josh Sweat Opponents this week, teammates the next? Rumors continue to swirl the Cowboys could be planning on acquiring Josh Sweat via trade before the November 10 deadline. He only has two QB sacks on the year through the first seven weeks of the season, and there some concerns about his desire for a new contract, but that hasn’t stopped rumors will be playing for another team soon. A lot of eyes will be on him this week and how he performs against Terence Steele. He could sway the game in the Cardinals favor with a big game and also increase his odds of him getting dealt and potentially landing the new contract he’s seeking.

title: Dallas Cowboys offensive line needs another performance like last week
summary: The Dallas Cowboys offensive line was the best unit on the field last week against the Philadelphia Eagles. Can they repeat the performance against the Arizona Cardinals? Let’s take a look.
