full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys offensive line was the best unit on the field last week against the Philadelphia Eagles. Can they repeat the performance against the Arizona Cardinals? Let’s take a look. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 54% (9th) Run Block Win Rate – 71% (28th) Pressure rate allowed – 31% (17th) Sacks allowed – 7 (1st) Last three-week trend: Improving nicely The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Do not lose track of Budda Baker The most dangerous Arizona pass rusher so far is not actually one of its defensive linemen, it’s safety Budda Baker. He leads Arizona with 3.5 sacks, ahead of Josh Sweat and Darius Robinson, who each have two. That immediately tells Dallas something about how Arizona is creating pressure. Baker has been used selectively as a blitzer. Arizona has found ways to disguise his approach and send him through gaps where offensive linemen are already occupied. One of those plays produced an A-gap sack against Jared Goff. If Baker begins close to the line, Dallas has to decide whether he is actually coming after Prescott or simply pretending to blitz before dropping into coverage. That uncertainty is the real danger. PRESSURE POINT: Josh Sweat versus Terence Steele Arizona still has one edge defender Dallas cannot ignore. Josh Sweat has only two sacks this season, and his overall production has dropped considerably from 2025. His sacks per 100 pass-rush snaps had fallen from 3.5 last year to 1.6 this year, but he remains Arizona’s most established edge rusher. The Cardinals themselves described Sweat as their best pass rusher earlier this month, and their depth chart places him at left defensive end, that naturally creates snaps against Terence Steele. Tyler Guyton has still not surrendered a sack this season despite allowing 19 pressures, and his 84.6 PFF run-blocking grade ranks fourth among qualifying tackles this year, but Steele has been the less dependable pass protector. Arizona should therefore move Sweat toward him and see whether it can create a weakness that Philadelphia failed to find. Dallas does not need to completely remove Sweat from the game, it just cannot allow him to turn a quiet season around on Sunday. Where to attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Cardinals soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Keep feeding Javonte Williams There is no reason to complicate this after Dallas finally found its running game against Philadelphia. Now Brian Schottenheimer needs to keep using it. Arizona has surrendered 884 rushing yards through seven games at 4.6 yards per carry, that’s 126 yards per game which ranks 10th-worst. It becomes even more interesting because Arizona could again be missing defensive tackle Walter Nolen III. He missed the Denver game with an ankle injury, and head coach Mike LaFleur said that he was not expecting Nolen to practice much this week, so keep watch on his status as that removes a powerful body from the middle. That means Dallas should go straight back to Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe and Tyler Booker where Williams had huge lanes against Philadelphia. There is no reason to move away from that approach this week. Arizona defensive lineman Darius Robinson has also struggled against the run. He has a PFF grading of 42.8 against the run, 106th among qualifying interior defensive linemen. That creates another target for Smith and Booker. Double-team Robinson initially, then allow one blocker to move onto a linebacker. GREEN LIGHT: Make Arizona’s four-man rush beat you This might be Dallas’ biggest statistical advantage. Arizona’s defense has generated pressure on only 25.5% of opposing dropbacks, which ranks 26th in the NFL and sits below the league average. The Cardinals have 15 sacks, 19th in the league, so they have managed to finish some of their pressure opportunities. But they are not consistently forcing quarterbacks to move. Dallas should force Arizona to prove it can win without blitzing. If the Cardinals rush four, send everyone else into a route. Do not automatically keep Jake Ferguson beside the offensive tackle. Give Prescott five receiving options and make Arizona’s defensive line beat Dallas one-on-one, especially after seeing that Philadelphia could not do it Monday and the Eagles finished without even registering a quarterback hit. Arizona’s pressure numbers suggest Dallas should trust the offensive line again. The Chaos Report Here’s the Arizona Cardinals defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 15 (19th) Pass Rush Win Rate – 52% (14th) Run Stop Win Rate – 27% (25th) QB Pressure Rate – 25% (26th) Last three-week trend: Light pressure, run defense leaking Matchup of the week Terence Steele vs. Josh Sweat This is the individual matchup Arizona needs to win. The former Eagle has not produced at his normal level this season as Sweat has only two sacks, while Arizona’s overall pressure rate is among the lowest in the league, but Dallas knows all to well what he can do. Sweat has the speed to attack Steele’s outside shoulder and enough length to prevent the tackle from easily getting his hands into position. Steele does not have to dominate Sweat, he simply cannot allow quick losses and he needs to give Prescott time to attack. Once those wins start happening and Steele handles his assignment enough times, the Cardinals coaches will need to adjust which in turn helps Steele even more. Best Route to Success The answer here is simple, do exactly what worked in Philadelphia. Run behind Smith and Booker, and let Guyton use his run-blocking ability that currently has him ranked highly on PFF, then make Arizona react. If the Cardinals bring Baker down toward the line to stop the run, use play-action behind him. If they blitz, throw quickly. Injury Updates: Dallas currently has no new injury concerns among its five starting offensive linemen. The main Cardinals injury to monitor along the defensive line is Walter Nolen III. Darius Robinson also dealt with a back injury last week but was able to play against Denver. There is some talk of Josh Sweat hitting the trade market before the deadline, but for now expect him to play against Dallas this week.
author: Mike Poland

title: Cowboys have chance they can’t let fly away against Cardinals
summary: Halloween weekend is fast approaching, and for a Dallas Cowboys team desperate to stack wins for the first time this season, there may be no spookier, scarier sight than the Arizona Cardinals coming to town. Yeah, seriously. Even within a bad NFC East division, the Cowboys have created a small margin of error to lose […]
full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Halloween weekend is fast approaching, and for a Dallas Cowboys team desperate to stack wins for the first time this season, there may be no spookier, scarier sight than the Arizona Cardinals coming to town. Yeah, seriously. Even within a bad NFC East division, the Cowboys have created a small margin of error to lose games they’re supposed to win, having already dropped such games to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New York Giants. The Cowboys suffered their fifth loss of the 2025 season to the Cardinals in week nine at home last year, and now are looking to avoid the same amount of losses through week seven against the same opponent – one they haven’t beaten since 2017, even with three of the four meetings since that win in Arizona coming in Arlington. If not for that 28-17 Cowboys win in 2017, the Cardinals would actually have an active nine-game winning streak against the Cowboys coming into this weekend, with the last win before that one coming in 2006. The 2-5 Cardinals opened their season with what felt like an upset win at the time at the Chargers, who remain winless. In week six, they went back to SoFi Stadium and scored a legitimate upset against a division rival, beating the Rams 18-16. This snapped a four-game losing streak to the Seahawks, 49ers, Giants, and Lions, but Mike LaFleur’s team also could not stack wins as they lost last Sunday at home to the Broncos. Let’s get to our weekly look at what the Cowboys must do to finally get the monkey cardinal off their back and beat these pesky red birds, or what could throw the season back off the rails with another bad home loss. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Arizona Cardinals if… …they set the edge on defense. There was one thing the Cowboys still struggled to do for the majority of the Philadelphia Eagles game. While the offense got points early and kept the pressure on most of the night, and the defense avoided the backbreaking plays and penalties until that offense handed them a sizeable lead, and the kicking game swung the field position battle in Dallas’ favor, still, the defense had a hard time setting the edge. If ever the stage was set for a game to help prove the Cowboys are different this year, Sunday afternoon is the ultimate “do-over” game, because the defense couldn’t set an edge at all against Jacoby Brissett and these Cardinals under Matt Eberflus in 2025. A strong run game on the edge, missed tackles, and the dual-threat ability of Brissett also gave the Cowboys defense no chance to hold up in coverage, as Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride caught touchdowns – the latter making the score 24-7 in the third quarter. Christian Parker’s Cowboys defense showed new looks in the middle of the field against the Eagles with Shemar James and Demarvion Overshown at linebacker. The personnel elsewhere in the secondary is also better than when these teams met last season when Markquese Bell, Juanyeh Thomas, and Kaiir Elam all started. Now, the Cowboys have Joey Porter Jr., Malik Hooker, and Caleb Downs patrolling in the backend. Schematically, Dallas has the answers to taking away the middle of the field where McBride has been the catalyst for Arizona’s pass game. The tight end leads the Cardinals in targets in their last three games, was one away from doing so in the Giants loss, and still has double digit targets in every other game he wasn’t the team leader. The Cowboys clogging up the middle of the field passing lanes can’t come at the cost of either edge contain against the run or pass rush. Brissett is a hard quarterback to bring to the ground, so much so that it feels like it’ll take timely blitzes to finish sacks in this game as opposed to counting on an edge rusher group that’s been poor at finishing for the Cowboys. Any blitz opportunities stem from stopping the run, and the Cardinals had 116 rushing yards in their week one win and 120 to beat the Rams. They’ve only had one other game over 100 yards this season, again at the Giants. First-round pick Jeremiyah Love has a strong chance at rejoining Arizona’s offense out of the backfield for this game, and is also a load to tackle on inside runs while having home run ability outside the tackle. Zonovan “Bam” Knight led the Cardinals in rushing yards over their last two games with Love out, while veteran Tyler Allgeier has been listed as the starter. Which QBs are getting help from their supporting cast? Factors: — Pressure (%) — Drop (%) — Average Target Separation — YAC/Reception pic.twitter.com/AcGJMiryDx — Daniel Rotman (@daniel_rotman15) October 26, 2026 The Cowboys will be playing a more dangerous game against Brissett and this stable of running backs than they did against Tanner McKee, a hobbled Saquon Barkley, and Dameon Pierce last week. If they don’t maximize what Dak Prescott and the offense does in this game by getting stops, the losing streak against the Cardinals will be at risk of continuing. A third straight game with a defensive takeaway would be like a full size Twix bar in the Halloween basket. It all starts with setting a hard edge. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Arizona Cardinals if… …they aren’t a serious football team. In the spirit of trick-or-treating this weekend, this game needs to be a treat for the Cowboys at home if they want to avoid fans saying they fell for yet another trick of high expectations. In one of the two Cardinals’ wins, they didn’t score a touchdown, just six field goals. Of their five losses, only one is close, 36-30 to the 49ers. They gave up 45 points to the Lions and 31 to the Seahawks. The one deceiving score in their schedule was the 36-24 loss at the Giants, where the Cardinals had a chance to win it late but threw a pick six, but the Cowboys also have their own claim to having a chance to beat the Giants in New Jersey. The best teams in this league string together wins, something the Brian Schottenheimer Cowboys have had a ghoulishly hard time doing. If they miss out on this opportunity to do so at home against the Cardinals, they would need to beat the Colts in week nine and 49ers in week 10 to get back-to-back wins on November 8th and 15th. It was November 23rd when the Cowboys won a second straight game last season. This pattern is not sustainable, and the time is now for the Cowboys to put the losing streak to the Cardinals behind them and think about stacking wins. After a gauntlet of defensive-minded head coaches in the first five weeks of the season, where the Cowboys went 2-3, they didn’t come out with intensity at the Packers and lost to the offensive-minded Matt LaFleur. They bounced back by beating Nick Sirianni’s Eagles last Monday, and now get another offense-first head coach in his first season, Mike LaFleur. There really are no excuses and nowhere to hide for the Cowboys this weekend, if they want the win in Philly to be remembered for something and to be taken seriously going into November.

title: Cowboys news: Christian Parker may be making  adjustments this week
summary: The Cowboys are heading into their week eight matchup with a little bit of momentum after beating the Philadelphia Eagles on the road in a must-win game. Fortunately for the Cowboys, they host the Arizona Cardinals (2-5) at home in another must-win game. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, they have struggled mightily against the Cardinals in […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Cowboys are heading into their week eight matchup with a little bit of momentum after beating the Philadelphia Eagles on the road in a must-win game. Fortunately for the Cowboys, they host the Arizona Cardinals (2-5) at home in another must-win game. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, they have struggled mightily against the Cardinals in recent matchups. The Cowboys are 2-8 in their last 10 meetings with the Cardinals, but this is a new year, with a new team on both sides of the field. Dallas Cowboys DC Christian Parker hints at a defensive adjustment that fans have been waiting for since Week 1 – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports Despite pulling out a much-needed divisional win in Philadelphia on Monday night, the defense still has a lot of issues. Christian Parker spoke to the media today and hinted at some possible changes coming to the Cowboys defense soon. Two areas that show how static the Cowboys have been this season: Blitzing and rotating safeties post-snap. Through seven weeks, the Cowboys blitz rate is 28th in the NFL (22.8%) and their safety rotation rate sits at 19th, per Sumer Sports. Notably, they refused to turn up the pressure against the two backup quarterbacks they’ve faced over the last three games. That includes a 10.53% blitz rate versus Eagles backup Tanner McKee. Dak Prescott on Cowboys’ offensive identity, matchup vs. Cardinals – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com There has been a lot of identity talk with both the offense and the defense so far this season. While that’s not a great conversation to be having in week eight, it seems like both sides of the ball may be closer to leaning into one. “It was an attempt at re-identifying who we want to be,” Prescott said. “We obviously know we love our run actions and throwing the ball like that, but you’ve got to get the run going. We weren’t committed enough to it the last couple of weeks before last, and I think that obviously hurt us. We got us into more of a passing situation than we wanted to be earlier than we planned.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Cowboys injury updates: Jonathan Bullard window opens, Quinnen Williams, Caleb Downs limited – Calvin Watkins, The Dallas Morning News Jonathan Bullard returns to the practice field after missing the last four games due to an injured calf. Bullard is currently on IR, but could return in the next week, which will provide the Cowboys defensive line with more veteran depth as they look to catch the New York Giants. On Thursday, the Cowboys started the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. Bullard missed the last four games with a calf injury suffered in the loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 27 . Bullard is on injured reserve and has missed the required four games to become eligible to return. “I felt good, I’m good,” he said after Thursday’s practice. Ranking Dallas Cowboys’ Biggest NFL Trade Deadline Needs With Under 2 Weeks to Go – Mike Moraitis, Cowboys on SI Will the Cowboys be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline? It sure sounds like they will be buyers, but what position should we be looking into with two weeks until the NFL trade deadline? Despite the additions of Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence and Von Miller during the offseason, the Cowboys have gotten just 3.5 sacks from the group over seven games. Miller has zero and Gary and Lawrence have one apiece while Donovan Ezeiruaku leads the group with 1.5. One of the best ways to cover for the lackluster coverage the Cowboys have seen from is to improve the pass-rush off the edge. If there’s one position Jerry Jones should break the bank for, it’s this one. Cowboys can finally build momentum by beating Cardinals – Sean Martin, BTB The Cardinals have absolutely dominated recent matchups against the Cowboys. A win against the Cardinals (as silly as it sounds) could go a long ways to building momentum for the rest of the season. The Dallas Cowboys finally produced the performance they needed on Monday night, beating Philadelphia 38-21 to move to 3-4. Now Dallas comes home to face a 2-5 Arizona Cardinals team that has lost five of its last six games. This is a real opportunity for the Cowboys to finally put consecutive wins together. The biggest positive from Philadelphia was the way Dallas ran the football. Javonte Williams exploded for a career-high 155 rushing yards and a touchdown, while the Cowboys finished with 204 rushing yards at 5.4 yards per carry.

title: 2026 Week 8 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: How do you feel after the Cowboys’ pivotal win over the Eagles? For some, it’s infused hope back into this season. Others see it as fool’s gold: a cheap win against a broken Philly team that says little about Dallas’ prospects going forward. Wherever you fall in the optimism spectrum, the fact remains that the […]
full_text: Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images How do you feel after the Cowboys’ pivotal win over the Eagles? For some, it’s infused hope back into this season. Others see it as fool’s gold: a cheap win against a broken Philly team that says little about Dallas’ prospects going forward. Wherever you fall in the optimism spectrum, the fact remains that the victory kept Dallas in striking distance of the NFC East crown and even a wild card spot. As we near the midway point of 2026, let’s take a detailed look at the current NFC standings. These are all the teams with 3-4 records or better. Current 2026 NFC Playoff Standings 1. Minnesota Vikings 6-0 (4-0 vs NFC) 2. San Francisco 49ers 6-1 (4-1) 3. New York Giants 4-2-1 (2-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers 3-3 (3-2) 5. Chicago Bears 5-2 (3-2) 6. Detroit Lions 4-2 (3-1) 7. Green Bay Packers 4-3 (3-3) _______________________________ 8. Seattle Seahawks 4-3 (1-2) 9. Atlanta Falcons 3-4 (3-2) 10. Los Angeles Rams 3-4 (2-2) 11. Dallas Cowboys 3-4 (2-3) Clearly, Dallas’ best shot is to catch the Giants and enter the postseason as NFC East champions. But the wild card race is still there for them, especially once all those NFC North teams start cannibalizing each other as the season rolls along. One team that isn’t on that list is the Cowboys’ next opponent, Arizona. Dallas returns home with an important task: getting to .500 and handling business against the 2-5 Cardinals. While they’re hardly the cream of the crop this year, Arizona has an 8-2 record against the Cowboys over the last 20 years. No matter what the teams look like on paper, they always seem to give Dallas fits. For now, our rooting guides are staying playoff-focused. Beyond finally getting another win against the Cardinals, what can we hope for from the Week 8 schedule? NFC East teams Commanders d. Eagles Superficially, Philly (2-5) has a better record than Washington (1-4-1). While we don’t expect them to rally and contend without Jalen Hurts, they still have great talent on both sides of the ball. We want the Cowboys to be able to focus on catching up to the teams ahead of them, not looking over their shoulders. Taking it a little deeper: if both the Eagles and Commanders are going to have rough years, we’d rather Washington get the better draft asset. Philly is much more likely to contend next season if Hurts returns and they get an offseason to retool the roster. The Giants have their bye this week, so Dallas can at least inch a little closer to them in the standing with a win. NFC vs. NFC Panthers d. Packers Vikings d. Lions Falcons d. Buccaneers Seahawks d. Bears Tonight’s game between Carolina and Green Bay is an easy pick. Someone has to win the NFC South, so it might as well be the currently leading Panthers. They can help Dallas this week, as a Packers loss not only hinders them as a potential wild card team, but could improve the 2027 first-round pick that they owe the Cowboys. Minnesota’s 6-0 record means they’re probably well out of Dallas’ reach in any scenario. Given that, the best thing for the Cowboys is that they keep right on winning and improving their chances of catching other NFC contenders, like Detroit. Atlanta may be tied with Dallas in overall record right now, but it’s still just Week 8. Tampa has a head-to-head win over us and are only a game behind, plus they are about to get Baker Mayfield back. If they drop to 2-6 this week, it gives us a little more cushion with the Bucs and still plenty of time to get ahead of the Falcons. Nothing complicated about picking the Seahawks over the Bears: just trying to slow down Chicago in the wild card race. NFC vs. AFC Chargers d. Rams The Battle for Los Angeles is the only interconference game this week, and the rooting interest for Dallas is obvious. Unfortunately, the Chargers’ 0-6 record makes it hard to think this one’s going our way. AFC vs. AFC Jaguars d. Colts Browns d. Steelers Dolphins d. Patriots The Cowboys are headed to Indianapolis next week, so you might want to keep an eye on them this Sunday. Indy’s already thrown up the white flag on 2026, trading away key players this week in a classic fire sale. A home loss to the rival Jags would only further demoralize them ahead of Dallas’ arrival. The last two interest us solely for 2027 draft purposes, as we own picks from Pittsburgh (3rd round) and New England (7th round).

title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Time to build on success
summary: It certainly feels better to be celebrating a Cowboys win this week, but the time for that is over.  As was discussed extensively going into Monday night, it was already something of a make-or-break game for both teams. While Dallas kept hope alive to overtake the New York Giants for the division, it was absolutely […]
full_text: Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images | Getty Images It certainly feels better to be celebrating a Cowboys win this week, but the time for that is over. As was discussed extensively going into Monday night, it was already something of a make-or-break game for both teams. While Dallas kept hope alive to overtake the New York Giants for the division, it was absolutely against a badly wounded Eagles squad. And it will only mean something if the Cowboys continue their winning ways. So how to do that? Tom Ryle and Sean Martin have thoughts. Tom – I confess to having more a sense of relief than a feeling of triumph. Dallas finally put together a strong, balanced offensive showing with a defensive effort that was not totally incompetent. If you recall, that has pretty much always been seen as the formula for success this season. The challenge now is to duplicate it. They need to stack wins and build confidence to still have a shot at the playoffs. It would be ideal if they could face multiple teams having similar struggles to the Eagles. Win like four out of dive to set up for the stretch run. Well, the opportunity is there, as four of their next five opponents are 2-5 or worse. Sean – I agree with you Tom, beating the Eagles is always sweet no matter the circumstance, but I wouldn’t call this one triumphant. I’m actually weirdly proud of the fanbase as a whole, at least the sections of it I spend time with, for not doing the old “buy all the way back in as if nothing bad ever happened” after this win. The stage is now as clearly set as it could possibly be. For this team to prove that anything is different from year one to year two under Brian Schottenheimer, they must go to Seattle in the first week of December with seven wins. Anything short of this and there will be simply no place left to hide when this 2026 team gets compared back to the last one before it that also missed the playoffs. Injured opponent or not, I’m hopeful the Eagles film is one they can use in the building this week to really build off of. They put some great coverage reps on tape defensively, steamrolled the game with their offensive line and run game, saw Dak Prescott lead the league for week seven in average depth of target, and hopefully proved to themselves how good they can be. Now, we wait to see if they really are that good, with mild expectations still being wise. Tom – In order to get to seven wins, they have to string together victories for the first time this season. And of those next five games, the middle one is against the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers, one of the best and arguably the most resilient teams in the league. Which puts a lot of pressure on the other four games, starting with the Arizona Cardinals this week at AT&T Stadium. While the Cardinals are 2-5, they also have played one of the hardest schedules in the league, including losses to the Seahawks, Niners, Giants, Lions, and Broncos. Yes, QB Jacoby Brissett doesn’t exactly strike terror into your heart, and first-round pick RB Jeremiyah Love is listed as questionable, and has not been as impactful as they had hoped. TE Trey McBride is their best offensive weapon. They are not scoring much and have allowed more points per game than anyone else. Some would interpret all that as a very likely win for the Cowboys. I prefer to spin around in my admiral’s chair and scream “IT’S A TRAP!” OK, maybe that’s a bit extreme. But this is another game that could reveal a lot about Dallas, and it potentially could be very negative. If they struggle or, heaven forbid, lose, we can pretty much expect this year to be a failure. A win would at least show some character, and like against Philly, it really needs to be a double digit margin. Sean – Sometimes it feels like there aren’t many “firsts” for me left to write about as something of a seasoned Cowboys writer at this point, but yet here we are. I’m confident I’ve never called a Cowboys game against the Arizona Cardinals a prove-it game, but this really is. The Cowboys have lost four straight to these pesky red birds, going back to 2020. That season, the Cardinals loss was the first of four straight that doomed the season. The following season, it was a four-game winning streak the Cardinals snapped at JerryWorld in week 17, and even a 51-26 win at Philadelphia to conclude the regular season couldn’t bring back enough momentum for the Cowboys to avoid being one and done to the 49ers in the playoffs. The 2023 team that lost to the Cardinals in week three had plenty of time to recover from the loss, but missed out on a 3-0 start and also didn’t win a playoff game. Throw last year’s loss in primetime to the Cardinals in the “defense never gave us a chance” bucket, and we really are at a point where the fate of the season might rest on what happens in the early kickoff window this Sunday. Strange times. Tom – Thanks for reminding me of the curse of the desert birds. That just reinforces how important this game is. Not only are they trying to show some consistency on offense and shore up their defense, they are fighting this odd intangible. And if it isn’t clear already, this just needs to be the next win in a mini streak. Assuming they manage to get a victory against the Cardinals, they then travel to Indianapolis to face the Colts, another struggling team. And one thing their next two opponents have in common is a quarterback issue. I’ve already mentioned Brissett and his 53.6 QBR. Indy has Daniel Jones taking snaps, and he has almost twice as many interceptions as touchdowns. It is rather important for any future hopes that they reel off three wins in a row, and they certainly have the offensive weapons to do so. Maybe we are finally seeing the defense gel as well. If so, this season could be more fun than we thought a couple of weeks ago. Sean – Again can’t believe I’m saying this, but hopefully this isn’t getting greedy against the Cardinals – it would be nice to mark this as a game the Cowboys find out they can win a little more with both sides of the ball. If the offense lights it up, great. If the defense can get sacks and takeaways, great. If the return game can make a difference without being penalized, great. The Cardinals have pounced on opponents that didn’t capitalize in one phase or the other, and the Cowboys need to be complementary to make any of the pending wins we think they have ahead of them really count for something bigger. Enjoy Halloween weekend Tom, we have a Halloween home game here in Bozeman for the Bobcats, and personally I must say I’m looking forward to covering an early kickoff for the Cowboys as a nice changeup.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Eagles win, defensive improvement, Cardinals game
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  Who deserves the biggest credit on the offense this week for the victory? Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, or the offensive line? […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. Who deserves the biggest credit on the offense this week for the victory? Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, or the offensive line? Mike – The offensive line, and for me, it’s not even close and wrote about this in the Winners and Losers article here on BTB . Dallas rushed for 204 yards against a physical Eagles defensive front, averaging 5.4 yards per carry, while keeping Dak Prescott clean with zero sacks or quarterback hits allowed, as well as allowing zero tackles for loss all evening. That’s a remarkable turnaround for a unit that has faced plenty of criticism this season. They controlled the line of scrimmage to create running lanes and give Prescott the time to operate without constantly looking over his shoulder. Jorge – The O-line has rightfully gotten some flak this year for being middling, especially in the run game. They ranked 31st in the league in run-block win-rate before Monday’s game; even though the Eagles were banged up, the Cowboys offensive line still blasted them at the point of attack. Troy Aikman even pointed out that Tyler Smith had no one to block on one of Javonte Williams’ long runs. The O-line had a lot to answer for, Monday night they showed up and executed. Dyllan – The offensive line absolutely dominated the entire night. The Cowboys essentially ran the ball at will. When the big guys win the trenches, everything else is easier. And that was the case Monday night. Sean – I’m going to go with Dak Prescott, since Jorge and Dyllan already gave the offensive line their flowers. Off the loss to the Packers, Brian Schottenheimer made headlines talking about how the run/pass split isn’t completely in his control as play caller, due to Prescott having autonomy to audible at the line. It did feel like against the Eagles, the run-first approach was Schotty simply noticing his team was winning the line of scrimmage and sticking with what was working, but pair any impact Prescott had in getting the Cowboys into these right looks with his dominance as a passer on Monday. Tom – OK, I’m not afraid to show Javonte Williams some love. The line gets credit for opening holes, but he really maximized his opportunities. Keep that kind of running game going and Dallas’ offense won’t be a punchline anymore. And admit it, it felt soooo good to be on the other side of that “can’t stop the run” equation. Did the Cowboys defense show improvement against the Eagles? Mike – There were definitely signs of improvement, but let’s not start celebrating this defense with the way it’s gone this season. They showed more energy and better communication. They finally made some important plays, particularly DeMarvion Overshown’s fourth-quarter interception. Holding the Eagles scoreless in the final quarter was encouraging, but the same problems are still there. Philadelphia rushed for 121 yards at 4.8 yards per carry and converted five of 12 third downs. The run defense continues to struggle with gap discipline and tackling, while getting off the field on third down remains a major concern. The Eagles game was a step in the right direction, but this defense still have a long way to go before it gets my trust. Jorge – Still plenty of work to do, but very, very slowly, this defense is showing signs of life. The pressure still isn’t consistent enough, and for stretches, the third-down defense is still terrible, but the second half is where this defense is really starting to put it together. If they could apply that for the entire game, this team would obviously be in a very different situation, but back-to-back games with an INT is worth noting; there is life on that side of the ball. Dyllan – They allowed 24 points or less for the third straight week. They only let up seven points after the first two Eagles drives. That said, the night was still relatively disappointing in my eyes. This is a horrifically bad Eagles offense that made the Cowboys defense look silly at times. They need to continue to grow, mesh, and get healthy. Sean – Man, this was such a weird game for defenses on both sides. Fangio versus Parker is like the Spiderman point meme coming to life when it comes to two schemes resembling each other, and both were so bad against the run it feels like they just gave up and stopped trying. The Cowboys are going to see much tougher opponents down the line that will only stop running the ball if the Dallas defense actually makes stops. While I like some of the things they did in pass defense, mainly Joey Porter Jr. continuing to play well and DeMarvion Overshown’s interception, being stout against the run is still a big concern. Tom – We all know this would have been a vastly different game against a healthy Jalen Hurts. The defensive effort was perhaps best described as survivable, as in the errors and breakdowns didn’t overcome Dallas. Most of the credit for the win has to go to the offense. The D still needs to improve a ton. What’s is best way for Dallas to get back-to back wins and defeat the Cardinals this week? Mike – Change nothing from last week for a start. The offense finally found some offensive balance, with the offensive line dominating up front, Javonte Williams rushing for a career game, and Dak benefiting from a much cleaner pocket. The Cardinals have struggled to stop the run, so Brian Schottenheimer needs to establish Williams early and use that success to create opportunities for CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Dallas has the talent to do it, but the biggest challenge as far as I see it is proving Monday night’s performance wasn’t just a one-off. Jorge – Keep the run game going! The Cardinals rank 23rd in rush defense and are giving up 4.6 yards per carry this season. If the Cowboys want to maintain what everybody knows is a winning formula, that being offensive balance, they have to keep pounding the rock. If they can do that, they can also help their defense, which is continuing to grow, albeit slowly. Maybe we’ll see a complete game yet. Dyllan – Controlling the pace of the game will be imperative. This means once again dominating the trenches and staying balanced on offense. If Dallas can get out to an early lead, it’ll be interesting to see if the defense can capitalize again with turnovers and sacks like they did when Philadelphia finally got behind by two possessions. Sean – Build off the complementary football they played at the Eagles. The Cardinals have held the two opponents they’ve beaten this season under 17 points, a benchmark the Cowboys should easily expect to clear at home with momentum back on this side of the ball. Piling on points shouldn’t feel like a necessity though, if the defense gets pressure and they avoid special teams miscues. Tom – A repeat of the last game’s offensive pattern is a no-brainer for how best to get the W. But continuing to improve on defense, and in bigger increments, may be more important. We always thought the offense had it in them. The defense still has so much to prove. RAPID FIRE Who scores first for Dallas? Over Dyllan – Over. A blitz or two gets home Sean – Hopefully over Tom –…

title: Cowboys can finally build momentum by beating Cardinals
summary: The Dallas Cowboys finally produced the performance they needed on Monday night, beating Philadelphia 38-21 to move to 3-4. Now Dallas comes home to face a 2-5 Arizona Cardinals team that has lost five of its last six games. This is a real opportunity for the Cowboys to finally put consecutive wins together. The biggest […]
full_text: Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys finally produced the performance they needed on Monday night, beating Philadelphia 38-21 to move to 3-4. Now Dallas comes home to face a 2-5 Arizona Cardinals team that has lost five of its last six games. This is a real opportunity for the Cowboys to finally put consecutive wins together. The biggest positive from Philadelphia was the way Dallas ran the football. Javonte Williams exploded for a career-high 155 rushing yards and a touchdown, while the Cowboys finished with 204 rushing yards at 5.4 yards per carry. That balance made life much easier for Dak Prescott. If Dallas can carry that approach into Sunday, Arizona won’t be able to simply attack Prescott on every down. After two difficult weeks, Prescott responded exactly the way fans expected and gave Dallas the performance it needed thanks to a balanced offense. He threw for 212 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, finishing with a 118.1 passer rating. Dallas scored on seven of its nine offensive possessions and produced a season-high 416 yards. On the opposite side, Arizona has allowed 30 or more points in four of its last five games, including 45 against Detroit and 30 against Denver last weekend. What’s even more concerning for Arizona is they rank dead last in points allowed this season at 30 points per game allowed. When it comes to total yards allowed, they rank 29th. This means Prescott and the offense should have plenty of opportunities to take control of the game. For the Cowboys defense, this may be the biggest matchup for them to gather more confidence. Arizona has moved the football, which looks great on the stat sheet, but it hasn’t finished drives. They rank 10th in the league for total yards per drive on offense, yet rank 26th in points per game, and has scored only 16 and 18 points in its last two games. The Cardinals are also just 1-for-10 in the red zone over their last two games. Against Denver they reached the red zone four times and managed only one touchdown. That is exactly what this Dallas defense needs to get rolling. The Cowboys don’t have to completely shut Arizona down, but at least force field goals instead of touchdowns and let Prescott’s offense create the difference. If Dallas gets into the high 20s or 30s, the Cardinals will undoubtedly struggle to keep pace and become one-dimensional allowing them concentrate on constricting Arizona’s passing game. The Cowboys defense is getting healthier. DeMarvion Overshown finally returned against Philadelphia and immediately reminded everyone what Dallas had been missing. He tied for the team lead with six tackles, added a tackle for loss, broke up two passes and grabbed an interception. Cornerback Cobie Durant also returned from injury which only adds to the help this secondary needs. So what about the Cowboys defensive line? The Cardinals struggled to protect Jacoby Brissett against Denver. He was under pressure throughout their last game and was sacked three times. Arizona has allowed 15 sacks through seven games, which ranks middle of the league. As for running the ball, Arizona average 3.7 yards per carry, that ranks 27th in the league and their Run Block Win rate of 70% ranks 30th. That’s an offensive line struggling in pass protection and to get push in the run game. Dallas’ pass rush desperately needs more production. This gives Quinnen Williams and company a good opportunity to create some after registering two sacks against Philadelphia last week. Despite the sacks coming in slow, the Cowboys defensive line actually rank eighth in the league in Pressure Rate at 34%. Dallas should enter this game believing it is the better team, especially with the home field advantage added on top. There is every reason to believe Dallas can finally stack victories, move back to 4-4, and start building some genuine momentum.

title: “This one is important to us:” Broncos ready for another shot at KC
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! A good dose of revenge is always good for the soul. The Denver Broncos get their chance at a redo and to deliver a heaping portion to the Kansas City Chiefs this Sunday. But more than that is what a win does for the Broncos’ goal of winning the AFC West […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos scores a touchdown after being hit by Kei'Trel Clark #13 of the Arizona Cardinals during the second quarter of the game at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! A good dose of revenge is always good for the soul. The Denver Broncos get their chance at a redo and to deliver a heaping portion to the Kansas City Chiefs this Sunday. But more than that is what a win does for the Broncos’ goal of winning the AFC West again and, with it, a higher seed in the AFC playoffs. Denver’s odds of winning the AFC West shoot up with a victory. The revenge is nice, mainly for the fans, but it’s what comes with the win that matters for Denver this Sunday. As Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said to the media on Wednesday: “I think point blank, it’s important to our team. It’s important to us as players. They’ve been a really good team for a long stretch, and they continue to win games … It’s very challenging because they’re such a good football team all the way around. It starts with coaches, and then their players and their scheme. “They do a great job, and they just know how to win. They built a great culture of winning. For us, it’s about the next-game mentality. We know it’s a big one. That goes without being said. After falling to them already this year, this one is important to us. I expect a good game.” For Denver head coach Sean Payton, he doesn’t have to do much in terms of sending a message this week. The players know what this game brings. “I think teams in our league start with goal (No.) 1, win the division, goal (No.) 2 is best playoff seed, and goal (No.) 3 is win a championship,” Payton said to the media earlier this week. “So these division games work towards that first objective, and obviously, we’re playing a good team that has certainly been at the top of this division a long time.” As to whether Sunday’s game is a “must-win,” especially since it puts the Broncos in a great position to do that, Payton said there is still a path to the AFC West title even with a loss, just because of how much of the season remains. Though a win does make the path “easier.” “My message really afterwards was just that I said, ‘Look, don’t lose track of goal one, goal two, goal three,’” Payton said to the media. “We’re going to play in bigger games, but this is the next one, and I’m sure they’re looking at it the same way.” Broncos links

How the Denver Broncos can beat the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8 rematch Here are three things the Denver Broncos must accomplish to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs in their Week 8 rematch. Malcolm Roach is having a great season The seventh-year pro is really stepping up in an increased role in Denver’s defensive trenches. Potent quotables Sean Payton Opening statement “Pretty normal Wednesday relative to the schedule. Any questions?” On how the Chiefs have changed since their Week 1 matchup “I think the one change from the last couple of years is their ability and commitment to running the football the way they’re doing. They’re doing—obviously the addition of a runner, that’s the one thing that you see. Obviously it’s a divisional team. There haven’t been really any coaching changes. You have ample film. It does feel like it’s been a while, although relative to a season it hasn’t.” On what the Broncos can learn from Seattle’s performance against the Chiefs “I would say this, I think when you look at crossover film, you’re always like, ‘All right, who attacked him best? Who defended him?’ You’re more attentive to those games. So obviously it’s a real good defense, talking about Seattle. So there are certain things that carry over maybe structurally and then other things maybe that don’t relative to the scheme.” On ILB Alex Singleton’s importance to the defense “He’s playing well. He had a ton of production last week. It was the first time since 2017 where he had two weeks at Calgary as the defensive player of the week. Little trivia there. We had a picture for him. Listen, he’s playing well with good instincts and had some big plays last week in the run game.” On if RB Kenneth Walker ll contributed to the Broncos’ tackling struggles in their last matchup with the Chiefs “I think I probably said it after the game, there were a lot of things that we didn’t do well Week 1 that hopefully in this second time around we can be better in a number of areas.” On WR Marvin Mims Jr.’s success this season “I think to his credit, whenever we ask something of him—whether it’s intermediate, down the field—he’s been really effective. Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are… I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.” On the challenges of getting WR Marvin Mims Jr. more touches “Sometimes it’s coverage and then it’s trying to find those personnel groupings where we’ve got a number of guys that are healthy and playing well. So hopefully we can find those opportunities.” On the depth and production of the wide receiver group “I think we only have one receiver banged up. I think. It’s [WR] Jaylen [Waddle], relative to this game. We had good work today. We’ll continue to work the details of the plan, but I thought today’s practice was good.” On the signs of improvement in the run game “I think I’ve been a broken record just relative to a lot of things offensively and us improving. There was obviously a step last week. We have to continue to build on it, different type [of] defense in this game. I think it’s shifting the focus to the technique of where these ends play, the type of front we see. It’s different than the last couple of games.” On if he communicated with Head Coach Andy Reid while coaching in New York “No, I just saw a ton of… I was in charge in Philadelphia of looking at Green Bay where Andy was with [former Head Coach] Mike [Holmgren]. I was in charge of Denver, San Francisco, I think Kansas City. Those teams that maybe were in a similar type of offense. Then Andy got hired in 1999 and I was going to the Giants. Then over the years, obviously, he’s in Philly, I’m in New York, I’m in Dallas. Then I think it was just coincidence early in New Orleans. We played them a number of times and over the years. There’s a ton of respect for what he’s been able to do, but we didn’t overlap per se. There was some clip on the internet last night where he was, I think, playing the Jets, and this might have been his first or second year and [Pro Football Hall of Fame Head Coach] Bill [Parcells] was talking to him. He’s done a great job.” On how QB Bo Nix and C Luke Wattenberg share responsibilities when the Broncos face loaded pressure looks “Great question. It’s harder when you’re on the road because they can pay attention to the heel and the silent snap. It’s a loud stadium. The advantage at home is—you try your best to undress it as to, is it four weak, two strong? You’re trying to undress it a little bit with something that gets him into— that’s harder to do when you’re there than when you’re at home. So there’s a lot on Bo, this is tonight’s gameplan. There’s a lot on the center, the communication. Obviously it’s more challenging when you’re on a silent snap count.” On what he means by being aggressive “There are a ton of ways. It could be a motion, it could be a shift, it could be anything that maybe can help move them into it. Which is a little bit harder to do when you’re there.” On the impact of the fans in a game like this “I think just after that last question, the snap count. Our home games have been amazing. It’s hard to measure the end results, but it’s been significant. Our crowd noise, all of that just adds stress to the operation. A week ago, what was very unique was it felt like a home game. I think in a game like this, it’s significant.” On if he has coached a road game with a large turnout from his team’s fans “Man, that was something. I yelled at [QB] Bo [Nix] like, ‘What are you doing with the silent snap count?’ That’s their issue. No, that was impressive.” On what QB Bo Nix’s 62-yard run could mean for future games “I think structurally you have to look at the play. They’re playing a match coverage. So pattern read guys. If you didn’t know any better, you’d look at it and say they have man in the zone and the safety tricks in which he’s supposed to do. You would ask the question a week ago. It’s not something you head off the week with relative to the quarterback. He did a good job of just sensing a cavity. So I think it depends on… In that defense, the eyes are on the receivers more than the eyes are on the QB. So I think sometimes it’s the scheme and yes.” On DT Malcolm Roach’s development as a pass…

title: Broncos vs. Chiefs: 3 Things to Watch in Week 8
summary: The Denver Broncos have their rematch against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. This is the biggest game of the season for the Broncos, who have a shot to catapult into first place in the AFC West if they are able to find a way to defeat the Chiefs in Week 8. Here are three […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) hands off to running back Jonah Coleman (20) during the fourth quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos have their rematch against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. This is the biggest game of the season for the Broncos, who have a shot to catapult into first place in the AFC West if they are able to find a way to defeat the Chiefs in Week 8. Here are three storylines I’ll be watching closely as the game transpires. Will Jonah Coleman get the nod as the Broncos’ top back? One major key to victory this Sunday will be who has the best ground game. Last week, the Broncos had a season high 159 rushing yards. A good chunk of that was courtesy of quarterback Bo Nix’s 62-yard touchdown run. However, rookie running back Jonah Coleman flashed on his 9 carries and gained 54 yards on the ground. He was on the field for 50-percent of the team’s offensive snaps. It’s quite clear the offense is much better with him in the fold. It’s no surprise their top rushing efforts of the season came when he played and got meaning playing time. After their victory over the Cardinals, Head Coach Sean Payton emphasized finding a way to get Coelman more touches. That might not sit well with J.K. Dobbins, but Denver has to do what is best for the team. A healthy dose of Coleman on early downs to control the clock and dictate the pace of the game seems like a good plan. Let’s see if Payton gives him more touches. Which wide receiver steps up on offense to provide a big spark? Seven games into the season and the Broncos are 5-2. That’s the good news. The bad news? Their wide receiver corps isn’t producing at a high level. Nobody has stepped up to be ‘the guy’ in their offense. Truth be told, the Jaylen Waddle acquisition hasn’t been the impact move Broncos Country hoped it would be. It’s too early to know at this juncture, but it is quite possible Denver’s offense will be without both Waddle and Pat Bryant for Sunday’s matchup versus the Chiefs. I think that’s a big obstacle for the offense to overcome. The Broncos will need one of Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims Jr. or Troy Franklin to step up in a big way. Somebody has to be their go-to guy on Sunday. Sutton has had some big games against the Chiefs in the past and was clutch moving the chains last season. Mims Jr. hasn’t been featured much on offense, but Payton has dubbed him one of the team’s most explosive playmakers. Earlier in the week, he mentioned finding a way to get him the ball. Will the Nix-to-Mims connection revive this weekend? What’s Vance Joseph’s plan to shut down Kenneth Walker? Games are won in the trenches. It’s safe to say the Chiefs dominated in that respect in Week 1. They controlled the pace of the game and dictated everything by being dominant on the ground. Kenneth Walker was easily the biggest impact player for the Chiefs in Week 1. He absolutely demolished Denver’s defense and had 173 yards on 23 carries with 1 touchdown. Last year’s Super Bowl MVP has been a standout performer for them and quite frankly most of their entire offense through six games. However, he is coming off his worst outing of the season. In the Chiefs’ Week 6 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, Walker was held to just 36 yards on 14 carries. How Joseph switches up his defense to limit Walker and how the players execute will be something to watch as the game unfolds. All things considered, the Broncos’ defense wasn’t necessarily out of place on a lot of run fits in their first matchup. They just did a horrendous job tackling and finishing plays. I don’t Walker to be shut down entirely, but ensuring he doesn’t have a huge game is probably the most important mission for Denver’s defense on Sunday.

title: NFL predictions: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Vikings in Week 8
summary: The Detroit Lions (4-2) and Minnesota Vikings (6-0) will meet in Week 8 in an NFC North divisional clash. The Vikings are the last remaining undefeated team in the NFL, and while their defense is playing at an elite level, they’ve yet to face an offense like the Lions, making this a fantastic strength-on-strength showdown. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Detroit Lions (4-2) and Minnesota Vikings (6-0) will meet in Week 8 in an NFC North divisional clash. The Vikings are the last remaining undefeated team in the NFL, and while their defense is playing at an elite level, they’ve yet to face an offense like the Lions, making this a fantastic strength-on-strength showdown. “Minnesota is playing outstanding football,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said earlier in the week. “(Head coach) Kevin (O’Connell)‘s doing a hell of a job. (Defensive coordinator) Brian (Flores) is doing a hell of a job. This thing, they play very complementary football. […] I’ve got a lot of respect for this team, the way they play, but we’re looking forward to this; this will be good.” Let’s take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will earn a victory over the Vikings in this week’s Honolulu Blueprint. This week’s prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed at +1800 to win this year’s Super Bowl and are currently 3.5-point favorites in Week 8 . Viking s base scheme For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 8 preview: Breaking down the Vikings’ offensive and defensive schemes . Prediction 1: Counter creativity with creativity The Vikings enter this game undefeated, but outside of their NFC North games against the Packers and Bears, their opponents have been bottom-of-the-league teams, totaling seven wins and 20 losses combined. Now, they’re headed into the toughest part of their schedule, beginning with the Lions’ elite offense—the first top-10 DVOA offense they’ve faced this season. The Vikings’ success is built almost entirely on their defense, which ranks in the top 10 in virtually every meaningful defensive statistic and is top one or two in most of them. Over six games, they’ve suffocated teams with their aggressiveness (their 69% blitz rate is over 20% higher than the next-closest team), and with a veteran unit that returns most of its starters, they rarely make mistakes. I go into more detail in my breakdown of the Vikings defense in the article link above, but at their core, the Vikings are so problematic because of their creative blitzing and quarters zone coverage. On most traditional downs, the Vikings will deploy a base 3-4 defense and line up seven or eight defenders in the box and then “double mug” blitz them, meaning bring an overloaded pressure on a single side of the offensive line or straight up the middle (double A-gap). The goal is to disguise where the blitz will come from and gain an extra blitzer in one area, while unexpectedly dropping players into coverage in the opposite area. The Vikings are so efficient at disguising their intentions and getting to the quarterback quickly that they lead the NFL in pressures on 49% of pass-rushing attempts, 21 sacks, and a 10% sack rate. While the Vikings are operating at a scary level, it’s not a defense that is unfamiliar to the Lions and quarterback Jared Goff. In previous seasons, Goff has done well to manage the blitz, especially when he has a healthy offensive line. In games where Goff has succeeded, he’s found creative ways to offset the Vikings’ creativity, and his ability to stay calm under duress— he’s currently the best quarterback in the NFL vs. the blitz, with an EPA of 0.32 —has led to success in the six games this season. Here’s an excerpt from NextGenStats’ game insights: “Jared Goff has been sacked once and completed 15 of 19 passes for 162 yards and three touchdowns across 20 max blitzes faced this season (i.e., 6 or more pass rushers), resulting in a career-high 78.9% completion percentage. [….] Goff has faced a max blitz on at least six dropbacks in each of his past six meetings with the Vikings during the Brian Flores era dating back to 2023, a threshold he has reached in just three of 51 other games played over that span.” In recent weeks, purposefully or not, we’ve already seen the Lions testing some concepts to beat an overloaded blitz. Concepts like spreading out five wide, or shifting a tight end into the backfield in a fullback role, will help the Lions offense create quick outlets or adjust their protection. The Lions have also sprinkled in some 21 personnel (two running backs and one tight end), where Sione Vaki stays in to protect, allowing Jahmyr Gibbs to be an outlet for Goff’s passing game. While the Lions will need to be creative with their running backs and tight ends, their receivers will likely help Goff produce downfield. Last week, we saw the Lions deploy Amon-Ra St. Brown more on the outside, and he caught seven of his nine targets for 109 yards against the Packers. Expect more of that in this game, as the Lions will want to get St. Brown isolated vs. the Vikings’ zone, giving him more space to operate. Also, it wouldn’t be surprising to see them give St. Brown some choice routes, where he can adjust the depth based on who the Vikings blitz. As NextGenStats also pointed out, the Lions have also found a separation advantage by lining up St.Brown and Jameson Williams on the same side of the formation: “The Lions’ passing offense has been more explosive when they align to the same side through seven weeks, as they have averaged 8.0 yards per play with a 18.3% explosive-play rate on those snaps.” By pairing them, Williams can stretch the zone deep and force the defensive backs to adjust to his speed, opening things underneath for St. Brown. If the defense takes the underneath route, then they’ll have to try and stick with Williams one-on-one deep. With the Vikings’ philosophy of limiting explosive plays, look for the Lions to stress their zone and take what they have underneath. The Lions offense vs. the Vikings defense may be the NFL’s premier matchup this week. Prediction 2: Pin-and-pull The Lions won’t be able to rely only on their passing attack in this game; they’ll also need to get their rushing attack going. Detroit tends to lean on its outside zone blocking scheme, but it’ll also need to be creative and unpredictable by incorporating other concepts it’s had success with. The chart below (adapted from NFL writer Ray Carpenter ’s design) shows the EPA from the Lions rushing offense when running in specific directions vs. the Vikings’ EPA in defending those running plays. No surprise, the Lions are finding most of their rushing success behind left tackle Penei Sewell, and it lines up with where the Vikings have been weakest. But the Lions won’t simply want to run behind their All-Pro all game; they’ll need to get creative too. With the Vikings lining up so many defenders on the line of scrimmage, the Lions will want to attack those edges, and the pin-and-pull concept can cool off some of Minnesota’s aggressiveness. Let’s look at the final offensive play from the Packers game to see an ideal example of the Lions deploying a pin-and-pull concept to get outside leverage and open a massive rushing lane for Jahmyr Gibbs. On this third-and-6 play, the Lions run a toss-left to Gibbs with the tight end (Sam LaPorta) and wide receiver (Isaac TeSlaa) cracking down (“pin”) on the Packers’ two outside edge players. In concert with the “pin,” the Lions “pull” Sewell and left guard Christian Mahogany under and outside left to get out in front of Gibbs. Additionally, the Lions put St. Brown in motion, and he seals the opposite edge of the hole by blocking the corner. Here’s the pre-snap look with the blocking assignments in red: And now the results after the snap with the “pin” circled and the pull in solid red arrows: Prediction 3: Put Vikings offense behind the sticks While the Vikings defense has played lights out,…

title: Which NFL Week 8 game are you most looking forward to?
summary: I think this every year, but the 2026 NFL season feels like it is flying by. Despite October almost being over, it feels like everything just got underway a few weeks ago. With that said, I doubt many of the players feel that way. After all, the regular season is a grind that players and […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 26: Jarran Reed #90 of the Seattle Seahawks sacks Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears during the third quarter at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images I think this every year, but the 2026 NFL season feels like it is flying by. Despite October almost being over, it feels like everything just got underway a few weeks ago. With that said, I doubt many of the players feel that way. After all, the regular season is a grind that players and coaches often refer to as a marathon, as opposed to an all-out sprint. Filled with peaks and valleys, veteran teams learn not to ride the waves. Just try your best to keep stacking wins as you head into the holiday months. That is where we find the Detroit Lions in their Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings. After securing their first divisional win against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7, they will be looking to improve to 2-0 in the division, and 5-2 overall on the year. If you are looking for a fresh take on that game, be sure to check out Anthony Balaj’s three key matchups article. I know a lot of fans enjoy the Lions being in primetime windows, or even the 4 p.m. ET slot like they were against Green Bay. Still, there is something nice about the Lions’ game against Minnesota being at 1 p.m. ET. If you are at home, you can simply flip the channel to the next game. For me, I have about a 15-minute drive before I can be on my couch for the afternoon slate of games. That brings us to our question of the day—which game other than the Lions vs. Vikings are you most looking forward to in Week 8? My answer: I am going with the “Monday Night Football” game between the Chicago Bears and the defending Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks. The Bears are riding high right now, currently firmly in the mix for what is looking like it will be an ultra-competitive NFC North race. Seattle got out of the gates a bit slow, but with that defense, it’s tough to ever count them out. What about you? Which game other than the Lions are you most looking forward to in Week 8? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Detroit Lions vs. Minnesota Vikings preview, prediction: On Paper
summary: The Detroit Lions have a chance to take down the undefeated Minnesota Vikings and make a statement in a very competitive NFC North. But the Vikings and their historic defense won’t make it easy for Detroit. Let’s take a closer look at the matchup with our Lions vs. Vikings preview and prediction. It’s On Paper […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 02: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions directs his team in the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in the game at Ford Field on November 02, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions have a chance to take down the undefeated Minnesota Vikings and make a statement in a very competitive NFC North. But the Vikings and their historic defense won’t make it easy for Detroit. Let’s take a closer look at the matchup with our Lions vs. Vikings preview and prediction. It’s On Paper time. Lions pass offense (9th) vs. Vikings pass defense (1st) The Lions’ pass offense is coming off perhaps its most impressive performance. The Packers pass defense was the best they’ve played against so far, and they posted an impressive 119.7 passer rating and a really good 57.1% dropback success rate (sixth best of the week). For the season, they continue to establish themselves as a top-five unit in the NFL. They rank: First in passer rating (112.5) Fifth in yards per attempt (8.0) Second in dropback EPA (0.309) Fourth in dropback success rate (51.8%) The only reason they may be dragging behind in DVOA is strength (or lack of strength) of opponent. The Saints, Bills, Jets, and Cardinals all rank 20th or worse in pass defense DVOA. But last week’s performance against the Packers certainly helps Detroit’s case. In terms of pass protection, it’s been great news for Detroit. They rank second in PFF pass blocking grade (82.1), seventh in ESPN’s pass block win rate (55%), fifth in pressure percentage allowed (30.8%), and 11th in sack rate (5.1%). Obviously, this week, the key is how they manage the blitz. And they’ve been phenomenal thus far. Against the blitz, the Lions rank: Fifth in pressure percentage (35.1%) First in EPA/pass (+0.25) Eighth in sack percentage (5.4%) This will be a challenge for Minnesota. But, of course, the Vikings defense is their best unit on the team, particularly against the pass. Not a single quarterback has averaged a passer rating over 90 against the Vikings, and only Jordan Love managed over 200 net passing yards. Now, it’s worth clocking how bad the passing offenses the Vikings have faced off against. By DVOA, the best passing offense they’ve faced is Chicago (12th), but that game was played in a monsoon. Here’s where the rest of the teams rank: Packers (18), Bucs (25), Dolphins (26), Saints (24), Colts (31). Still, the Vikings aren’t just beating up bad teams, they’re destroying them. For the season, the Vikings rank: First in passer rating allowed (61.7) Fourth in yards per attempt (6.1) First in dropback EPA (-0.226) First in dropback success rate (35.5%) Obviously, their pass rush is what really kills teams. Their ridiculous 68.4% blitz rate is 26.1% higher than any other team, and it has resulted in the top pressure rate (48.8%) and sack rate (10%) in the NFL. Player to watch: LB Blake Cashman. I believe Cashman should be in the running for Defensive Player of the Year. Cashman does everything for the Vikings defense, including blitzing (4.5 sacks), coverage (five passes defended), and being a menace in the run game (six tackles for loss). He has PFF’s second-highest grade among linebackers (86.2) with ridiculous grades in pass rush (86.2, 3rd), coverage (75.1, 9th) and run defense (70.9, 25th). Advantage: Draw. This is a top-five unit vs. the top unit in the NFL. But the Vikings have yet to be tested like Detroit will test them, and the Lions are coming off a strong performance against what was the No. 2 pass defense in the NFL last week. This one can truly go either way. Lions run offense (14th) vs. Vikings run defense (9th) The Lions run game has been a statistical enigma this year. The inconsistencies are both hard to watch and tough to comprehend. On a play-by-play basis, the Lions remain a pretty damn good running game. They rank: 15th in yards per carry (4.2) 19th in rush EPA (-0.108) Third in success rate (46.9%) The high success rate and mediocre EPA/YPC usually suggests a lack of explosive plays, and that is true to some degree. The Lions are 10th in amount of 10-yard rushes (21), but they have just two rushes of 20+ yards (only two teams have fewer). But the bigger concern is the high percentage of negative plays. Detroit’s “stuffed” rate (0 or negative yardage runs) is 20.9%, the third highest in the league. To be producing the third-highest success rate but also the third-highest stuffed rate is literal insanity. It speaks to how good the run game is outside of these negative plays, but the lapses in blocking are frustrating and really throws the Lions’ offense off-balance. One answer to the problem could be rushing in lighter formations, as Detroit gets less and less efficient with the more tight ends they put out there: You're definitely onto something. Lions' EPA/rush by formation: 11 personnel: 0.06 (10th) 12 personnel: -0.07 (17th) 13 personnel: -0.48 (28th) (via @SumerSports ) https://t.co/rUOeIW00VF — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) October 29, 2026 Despite the inconsistencies, the Lions run blocking does seem to be very good. They rank fifth in PFF run blocking grade (73.2), fourth in adjusted line yards, and 20th in ESPN run block win rate. Minnesota has given up a few big days on the ground this year, but they’ve also faced some of the best rushing attacks in football (and two of the worst). Overall, they’re still among the best in the league: 21st in yards per carry allowed (4.2) Second in rush EPA (-0.212) First in rushing success rate (31.2%) Unfortunately for Detroit, they are also very good at creating negative plays in the run game. Their 19.1% stuffed rate ranks eighth in the NFL. They’re also stellar in another facet of the run game Detroit struggles at: short-yardage situation. The Lions are converting short-yardage situations just 60% of the time (21st), while the Vikings are allowing a power success rate of only 58% (ninth). Player to watch: Jalen Redmond. The Vikings’ 291-pound defensive tackle is currently PFF’s No. 1 graded interior defender against the run (90.5). He will give the Lions’ guards a handful on Sunday. Advantage: Vikings +1. There’s enough opportunity for the Lions to find some success here, but the inconsistencies are a huge concern right now, and if Detroit continues to allow negative plays in the run game, it will set up nightmare down-and-distances for Jared Goff. Vikings pass offense (27th) vs. Lions pass defense (24th) The Kyler Murray project is off to a slow start. It hasn’t been a disaster—as the Vikings are generally avoiding negative plays (18 sacks, 22nd; two interceptions, t-third)—but the efficiency is quite poor. 15th in passer rating (90.7) 22nd in yards per attempt (6.6) 25th in dropback EPA (-0.029) 30th in success rate (38.6%) It’s hard to pin down exactly where things are going wrong. Obviously, the Vikings have a strong set of receivers in Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson—Murray’s current favorite target. And while the offensive line isn’t great, the pass blocking statistics are fine: 11th in pressure rate allowed (32.7%), 10th in PFF pass blocking grade, but 30th in sack rate (9.9%). That suggests Murray has been holding onto the ball longer than normal and his 2.91 average seconds to throw (12th) does support that. And while he is certainly capable and willing to evade pressure with his feet, he hasn’t been consistent at it. Ultimately, I think this is just a relatively poor passing attack that doesn’t throw the ball deep often (Murray is 23rd in average depth of target and 15th in deep shot percentage), and hasn’t found its groove. Detroit is slowly climbing out of the basement with their pass defense. For the season they rank: 25th in passer rating (102.2) 17th in yards per attempt (7.3) 28th in dropback EPA (0.242) 28th in dropback success rate (50.0%) But over the last two games, the Lions rank: 15th in passer rating (87.8) 20th in dropback EPA (0.140)…
