title: Patriots unsuccessfully tried to claim ex-Raiders defensive tackle, per report
summary: The New England Patriots attempted to add to their defensive line this week, but ultimately failed to do so. One of six teams to put in a waiver claim on former Las Vegas Raiders defender Jonah Laulu, they were undone by their record being superior to that of the other five potential claimants. Besides the […]
full_text: The New England Patriots attempted to add to their defensive line this week, but ultimately failed to do so. One of six teams to put in a waiver claim on former Las Vegas Raiders defender Jonah Laulu, they were undone by their record being superior to that of the other five potential claimants. Besides the Patriots, the Tennessee Titans, Miami Dolphins, Houston Texans, Indianapolis Colts and New York Jets also tried to bring Laulu on board, according to a report by NFL insider Jordan Schultz. The 1-5 Titans were awarded the 26-year-old on Wednesday. Laulu entered the league as a seventh-round draft pick by the Colts in 2024 but was waived after his rookie training camp. He ended up with the Raiders as a waiver claim, and since then played 39 games with 22 starts for Las Vegas. Along the way, he registered 5.5 combined sacks — including 0.5 in five games this season. However, Las Vegas’ new coaching staff under Klint Kubiak did not view him as an integral part of the team’s defensive rotation. After playing 68% of defensive snaps in 2025, he was on the field for only 23% so far this year. His release earlier this week did not come as a particular surprise. For the Patriots, the move presented an opportunity to add another pass rusher to their interior defensive line. At the moment, the group consists of Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, Cory Durden, Joshua Farmer, DaQuan Jones and Leonard Taylor; Eric Gregory and Jeremiah Pharms Jr. offer additional depth on the practice squad. In total, New England has 52 players on its active roster, meaning that no follow-up move would have been necessary had Lautu been claimed. The Patriots are traveling to Miami this week to take on the Dolphins in a 4:25 p.m. ET matchup on Nov. 1.

summary: The New Orleans Saints lost another game, and sadly, it really didn’t change much in the draft order. full_text: WEST LAFAYETTE, IN - OCTOBER 10: Minnesota Golden Gophers offensive lineman Greg Johnson (65) warms up on the field during the college football game between the Purdue Boilermakers and Minnesota Golden Gophers on October 10, 2026, at Ross-Ade Stadium in West Lafayette, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints lost another game, and sadly, it really didn’t change much in the draft order. Like these past two seasons, the bad teams keep losing, and it’s keeping the Saints away from a single-digit pick, so in the bye week, the Saints are set to select at pick 10 in the NFL Draft. Here are some players the Saints could select at 10. OG Greg Johnson Looking at top guard options, Greg Johnson is the guy in the first round, although 10 may be a little bit of a reach, guard is becoming more and more important in today’s NFL, and the Saints need a starting RG. If they do not move on from Cesar Ruiz before the deadline, it’s going to happen in the offseason. Although I do like Jeremiah Wright, there’s no reason to believe he can start next season, and I don’t want the Saints to rely on that to happen. The other caveat to this selection is the coaching staff. If Kellen Moore, this coaching staff, and the front office are still in place, I don’t want the Saints to make this selection. They have good offensive linemen that are regressing under them already, so I wouldn’t expect a rookie offensive lineman to have much success. However, it’s the perfect selection for a new coaching staff and GM who hopefully knows the trenches, and a new head coach who can elevate this rookie. DL Xavier Gilliam The caveat put in place for the Johnson pick should be here as well. The Saints haven’t done well lately at drafting defensive linemen. Doesn’t matter if it’s a defensive tackle or edge rusher, it doesn’t work out. So, if a new staff is put in place, Xavier Gilliam would be a really good option. He is incredibly athletic, extremely quick off the snap, can win against offensive linemen with power and different pass-rush moves, and is equally dominant against the run. Gilliam is a player you will see throughout any game blowing up plays in the backfield, but he also makes the right decisions and has a consistent impact when he’s not creating incredible moments. The Saints do not have a DT anywhere close to the player Gilliam is on their roster, and putting him next to Chase Young could really elevate this entire defense.

title: Can the Saints still rise to the top of the NFL’s weakest division?
summary: Had any of us been told – off the back of the Saints’ Week 2 win in Baltimore that followed a refereeing injustice in Detroit – that New Orleans would sit 2-5 going into the bye week, it’s a safe assumption the reaction would be one of shock. But that’s indeed where we are, as […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons looks on from the field after an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Had any of us been told – off the back of the Saints’ Week 2 win in Baltimore that followed a refereeing injustice in Detroit – that New Orleans would sit 2-5 going into the bye week, it’s a safe assumption the reaction would be one of shock. But that’s indeed where we are, as we enter a week head coach Kellen Moore has branded a chance for evaluation. Some deficiencies are well-defined at this stage of the campaign: a failure to run the football matched by a failure to stop opponents from running at will. When Aaron Rodgers outruns your backs, it’s a bad sign. When Tyler Shough was also your leading rusher on the day in France with 7 yards, it emphasises the point. The offense still shows flashes in the passing game; Shough continues to throw the ball all over the field to a talented receiving room, one that will only become more potent as Jordyn Tyson nears his NFL debut. Even the defense has remained relatively able to keep teams out of the end zone, particularly if one exempts the fourth quarter in New York. The Raiders and Lions games were two that Kellen Moore’s team absolutely could’ve had. Either one of them would’ve been enough to see the black and gold currently tied for first in the win column in the NFC South. And that’s where the current debate lies: are the Saints headed for the league’s basement, or still in with a chance at hosting a playoff game? The optimist in me refuses to throw in the towel just yet. One has every right to feel despondent about this coaching staff and to deem another top pick, alongside large-scale organizational changes, to be the most desirable outcome as the season moves along. But there’s no part of me that’s convinced by any of Carolina, Tampa Bay, or Atlanta, even as the latter found a win over a depleted 49ers roster that was coming off a short week. Should Daniel Carlson have converted both field goal attempts or Shough not have thrown a key momentum-shifting interception in the third quarter against Pittsburgh, the Saints probably would have won a game in which the run game was a complete nonfactor. There are two ways to look at that, but the positive outlook says that New Orleans has the capacity to win games; they just need to find a way to start doing it. So, if you’ll excuse my short-termism, which I can explain away by my desperation to watch my team return to the playoffs for the first time post-Brees, I’ll continue to believe that the Saints can find their way to the NFC South crown. Do you share a level of optimism here in the bye week? Or did the black and gold’s dashing playoff hopes officially get left in Paris? Let us know how you’re feeling in the comments!

full_text: McBride the menace | Getty Images Welcome to Week 8, and happy Halloween! Halloween isn’t just spooky and scary – it ventures into the eerie and weird. Here’s something weird: The last undefeated team in the NFL is the Vikings, and the last winless team is the Chargers. If you told me in August that I’d be writing that sentence at the end of October, I’d ask you what you’re smoking. But that’s the reality as the NFL season enters November. The Vikings are 6-0 despite having one of the worst offenses in the league. In their five wins since Week 1, they failed to score a touchdown two different times, and only found the end zone five times, total. And that’s with a dominant, suffocating defense that keeps giving the offense the ball.1972 Dolphins, your champagne should be on ice right about now. The Chargers’ offense – which was supposed to be a juggernaut with the pairing of new O.C. Mike McDaniel and Justin Herbert – is even worse than Minnesota’s. They’re dead last in the NFL in scoring, at just 15 points per game. One of the most enjoyable things about Week 7 was that we didn’t have to see Jim Harbaugh’s team play. We did get to see his brother John’s team though, and that was glorious. The Giants went into Houston as 10.5 point underdogs and pulled off the second biggest upset of the season, so far, with a walk-off in OT. Maybe J.J. McCarthy could help that anemic offense up north. Hmm… Week 7 featured a lot of missed kicks, some horrible refereeing, and the defending Super Bowl champs making a statement by dominating the previously undefeated Chiefs in prime time. What does Week 8 have in store? Stats of the Week : Every team in the AFC North and NFC North is over .500. Meanwhile, no team in the NFC South is over .500. I feel like I’ve typed that last sentence at least a dozen times since I took this gig. The Bucs scored 43 points at Carolina, despite having just 64 passing yards. In one quarter, Tampa scored a TD four different ways: Run, pass, special teams, and defense, and they also kicked a field goal. A team did all of that within a single quarter only once before in NFL history. Speaking of things that haven’t happened in a while, the Ravens became the first team since 1950 to lose by 20+ points after leading by 13+ points at halftime. Baltimore has blown 17 double-digit leads in the 2020s. Baltimore’s point differential is +65 in the first half (1 st in the NFL) and -70 in the second half (last in the NFL). Aaron Glenn is 0-8 against the AFC East, and during his brief tenure, the Jets have been outscored 107-6 In the final two minutes of the first half. Aaron Rodgers threw his 540 th career TD pass, moving him past Peyton Manning and into third place all time. The Seahawks have not allowed a 100-yard rusher in 36 straight contests. The Dolphins did not hold the lead at any point in their first five games. In their sixth game (against the Jets on Sunday), they never trailed. On to Week 8. Note: There is no international game this week! Sleep in and move those clocks back an hour. Bye Weeks: HOU, NO, NYG, SF Week 8 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Trey McBride . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did very well, with more hits than misses. My wide receiver fades were especially strong. My Ride of the Week was Tucker Kraft, who scored a TD and put up 12.8 fantasy points, good for TE6 on the week. My Fade of the Week was Patrick Mahomes. The seven fantasy points he put up against Seattle was the single worst output of his nine-year career as Kansas City’s starter. That includes games he didn’t finish. My Sleeper of the Week Kyler Murray mostly stayed asleep and only produced 11 fantasy points. Because, you know, Minnesota can’t score touchdowns. You can check my work here . *** Ride of the Week: Zay Flowers (@BUF). I haven’t written enough about Flowers this season. He’s been a beast, and leads the NFL in some key metrics including catch percentage (76%), yards per route run (3.73), and yards after the catch (313). He’s fifth in receiving yards and is one of just six receivers with a team target share north of 30%. In other words, he’s been really, really good. This figures to be a high-scoring game (the Vegas total is 53.5, second biggest on the board), and the Bills’ porous secondary is a dream matchup. Buffalo has allowed the most touchdown catches (11) and fantasy points per game (FPPG) to opposing WRs. Flowers will come up smelling like a rose this week – book it. Fade of the Week: Bryce Young (@GB). Speaking of roses, the bloom is quickly coming off this one. Remember when Young stood tall as the QB2 after two weeks, and everyone was saying “ah, NOW we see why he was the first overall pick”? Well, it hasn’t been a disaster since then but there’s been a steady decline, culminating in a horrible performance at Tampa on Sunday (7.4 fantasy points) in a blowout loss. Now Young and his team must regroup on a short week and travel to Lambeau to play a Packers team that has to be chewing on nails after an incredibly frustrating loss at Detroit – one replete with some awful calls against them, more big drops, and two missed short field goals. The Panthers are down a couple of offensive linemen – not ideal. The Packers are allowing the fifth fewest FPPG to opposing QBs and have as many picks (9) as TD passes allowed. They lead the league in interceptions. Young is ranked right on the fringe of starter this week (QB12) but I think he’ll struggle again, and finish outside the Top-15. Sleeper of the Week: Geno Smith (vs. LV). Geno should start to cook now that he has a full complement of healthy weapons, including rookie WR Omar Cooper, Jr. As I’ve been saying in my waiver wire columns, Geno can get you fantasy points in the right matchup. This is one of those matchups. The Raiders are losers of four straight and their defense is the main culprit. They’re allowing the sixth most FPPG to opposing QBs, and the 16 TD passes they’ve allowed is tied for second most. Look for Geno to have plenty of success getting the ball to his young and talented receivers and tight ends. He put up 24.5 fantasy points against Miami and is a good bet to break 20 again. He’s ranked as the QB22 this week and that’s too low. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen , Lamar Jackson , Drake Maye, and Joe Burrow ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Three QBs ranked in the Top-10 this week who should smash: Dak Prescott (vs. ARI). This game has the highest total of the week (54.5), Dallas is flying high after trouncing the Eagles, and the Cardinals allow the fourth most FPPG to opposing QBs and have given up a league-worst 17 TD passes. Trevor Lawrence (vs. IND). The Colts handled Kyler Murray last week, but they just traded away DeForest Buckner as part of a fire sale, and now they get the rested Jaguars. Trevor should flourish at home against this middling (at best) defense. Jayden Daniels (vs. PHI). He’s positioned do well this week. It’s a decent matchup (10 th most FPPG allowed to opposing QBs), and Philly is reeling and on a…

title: NY Giants trade candidate: Indianapolis Colts’ DT Grover Stewart
summary: The New York Giants could use upgrades to the depth along their defensive line. The Indianapolis Colts have already traded away their best defensive lineman, sending DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. The Colts, though, still have veteran defense lineman Grover Stewart, and he could be a fit for what the Giants need to […]
full_text: Grover Stewart | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants could use upgrades to the depth along their defensive line. The Indianapolis Colts have already traded away their best defensive lineman, sending DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. The Colts, though, still have veteran defense lineman Grover Stewart, and he could be a fit for what the Giants need to solidify their run defense as they try to make a playoff push. Ralph Vacchiano of FOX Sports, in fact, is recommending Stewart as the one player the Giants should target before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. Vacchiano says: The Giants never really replaced Dexter Lawrence in the middle of their defensive line, and that’s easy to see from a run defense that’s giving up 128.1 yards per game. They have enough weapons on offense, as long as QB J.J. McCarthy keeps playing well. What they need to do is fortify a defense that has been battered by season-ending injuries to LBs Brian Burns and Tremaine Edmunds. Tennessee’s Jeffery Simmons is the DT star of the market, but he’ll likely cost a first-round pick. Grover Stewart, 33, should cost less than the fourth-rounder the 49ers dealt for Stewart’s old teammate, DeForest Buckner, though. And at 6-foot-4, 315 pounds, he could be a cheap way for the Giants to bulk up their defensive line and add a little interior push, too. Why it would work I am going to quibble a little bit with Vacchiano. D.J. Reader is not Lawrence, but Reader has been outstanding in the middle of the Giants’ defense. D.J. Reader deserves a lot more love. Through seven games: 15 run stops on 119 qualifying run plays. His 12.6% run-stop rate is SECOND among 44 interior defenders with at least 100 qualifying run plays, per PFF. Average tackle against the run: just 2.2 yards downfield. Love… pic.twitter.com/MNWMgHcheU — Alex Wilson (@AlexWilsonESM) October 27, 2026 Shelby Harris has been OK. The problem has been when those players rotate out. Rookie sixth-round pick Bobby Jamison-Travis played well against the Houston Texans, but he has only seen action in two games and the Giants can’t be sure what they will get from him. Darius Alexander’s run defense has been a bit better of late, but whether he can be trusted there is uncertain. C.J. Okoye has been disappointing, and barely plays. Stewart has historically been a plus run defender, and would provide an upgrade to the interior run defense. He has also shown some ability to push the pocket as a pass rusher. He is in the last year of a three-year, $39 million contract, so the Giants would be on the hook for the pro-rated portion of his $11.74 million base salary. The price to acquire Stewart would likely be a late-round draft selection. Why it wouldn’t work The Giants would have to do some salary cap juggling. The pro-rated portion of Stewart’s contract would, as of today, cost the Giants roughly $7.2 million. They currently have $7.6 million available under the cap, per Spotrac. The Giants would have to do some manuevering to have cap space to operate for the remainder of the season. Is this a trade you would like to see the team make, Giants fans?

title: NY Giants QB Jaxson Dart still eyeing a return for the playoffs
summary: When New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending knee injury in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams, head coach John Harbaugh held out hope that Dart would be able to return for the playoffs, should the Giants reach them. General manager Joe Schoen said on Tuesday that remains Dart’s aim. “He still […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co When New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending knee injury in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams, head coach John Harbaugh held out hope that Dart would be able to return for the playoffs, should the Giants reach them. General manager Joe Schoen said on Tuesday that remains Dart’s aim. “He still thinks if we make the playoffs that he’s going to be able to come back. That’s just his mindset,” Schoen said. “He’s in the locker room trying to do pass sets, dying to go back in the game. So, he’s one of those guys you appreciate his toughness and grit. And you’ve got to protect him from himself sometimes. “You guys saw the way he played his rookie season. You love the toughness in the competitor. And he’s going to come back stronger and better than ever.” Dart suffered damage to the MCL, PCL, and meniscus in his left knee. There was no damage to the ACL. According to orthopedic surgeon Dr. Kyle Flik, the extent of damage to the PCL will determine how quickly Dart can return. If it had to be reconstructed, which is unknown right now, a return for the playoffs would be out of the question. On ‘Up & Adams’ with Kay Adams, right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said Dart has willingly been helping replacement quarterback J.J. mcCarthy. Jaxson Dart has played a HUGE role in JJ McCarthy's success with the Giants says Jermaine Eluemunor 💪 @JEluemunor | @JaxsonDart | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/taQrUPOAGi — Up & Adams (@UpAndAdamsShow) October 28, 2026 Schoen said Dart is “doing the best he can.” “I know it’s tough for him. He’s coming to the team meetings. He’s back in the quarterback meetings. So he’s around. He’s not weight-bearing yet. So he’s on his crutches. But he’s staying as positive as he can,” Schoen said. “He’s around, which I think is good, mentally being around the guys, being around football still.” As indicated by our Dart-McCarthy post earlier Thursday, there is already much-too-early speculation about the future at quarterback for the Giants should McCarthy continue to play well.

summary: A year ago a struggling Jets team dealt a pair of high profile players, Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams, at the trade deadline for a pile of picks in the NFL Draft. With the 2026 Jets struggling, and star wide receiver Garrett Wilson looking visibly frustrated on the sidelines in Sunday’s loss to the Miami […]
full_text: Oct 25, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson (5) leaps to catch a pass against Miami Dolphins safety Zayne Anderson (23) during the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A year ago a struggling Jets team dealt a pair of high profile players, Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams, at the trade deadline for a pile of picks in the NFL Draft. With the 2026 Jets struggling, and star wide receiver Garrett Wilson looking visibly frustrated on the sidelines in Sunday’s loss to the Miami Dolphins, speculation has begun about whether the Jets could look to make a big trade this year involving the three-time 1,000 yard receiver. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest. Unlike Gardner and Williams, Garrett Wilson will play a big direct role in the development of any quarterback the team selects in next year’s NFL Draft. author: John B

title: Eagles at Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 8 enemy
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are riding a five-game losing streak entering Sunday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, a team they beat in the season opener. Can the Birds win a game for the first time since September 20? In order to preview this Week 8 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over […]
full_text: Nov 10, 2024; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn (L) congratulates Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) after a touchdown drive against the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Philadelphia Eagles are riding a five-game losing streak entering Sunday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, a team they beat in the season opener. Can the Birds win a game for the first time since September 20? In order to preview this Week 8 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven . The amicable Andrew Y kindly kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. 1 – In our Q&A exchange ahead of Week 1 , you said that the Commanders are “ one of the most boom-bust teams in the NFL.” There’s clearly been more bust than boom so far. What’s the biggest reason why? In short, I would say: injuries, two rookie coordinators figuring out how to call plays, and poor preparation and in-game decision making that I mostly blame on HC Dan Quinn. I should also throw in that GM Adam Peters deserves some blame for botching the Center situation in the offseason by starting week 1 with career backup IOL Nick Allegretti as our starting Center. On the plus side for Peters, he found a serviceable Center off the scrapheap in Lucas Patrick who has started at Center since week 3. In terms of injuries, the Commanders’ week 5 injury report had 23 players on it. I don’t remember seeing another injury report that long! Many of those players are on the mend and likely to play this week, but some key remaining absences are LT Laremy Tunsil (out for the year), RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (the best pure rusher on the roster), WR Terry McLaurin (torn patellar tendon, may never be the same player again), and DT Javon Kinlaw (one of our better penetrating IDL). In terms of the coordinators, we knew it was going to be risky having two coordinators who have never called plays in the NFL before and that is bearing out. On defense, DC Daronte Jones is trying to implement the complicated and almost unique Brian Flores defense from Minnesota. The defense is difficult to implement because it requires players to be very versatile, with even DTs occasionally dropping into coverage and CBs blitzing the QB. Even in Minnesota, the Flores defense was ranked 16th in yards allowed in its first two years before being ranked 3rd last year and 1st this year, and I think a lot of the improvement is due to players getting better at understanding their responsibilities. In addition, Daronte Jones is a first-time NFL playcaller and I think is showing a bit of slowness in adapting to mid-game changes by the opposing offense. On the other side of the ball, OC David Blough is a first-time playcaller with only two years of coaching experience and it’s occasionally showing. He has a good playbook, but plays are taking too long to get called, players are taking too long to get set, and Blough hasn’t been adapting well enough to blitzes by building hot routes into his plays. In terms of Dan Quinn, it’s a lot. Even though the Commanders are somewhat middle-of-the-road in terms of number of penalties, they are exceptional at getting penalties that erase big plays. The Commanders have the most yards erased by penalty in the NFL right now, and I think that comes down to coaching and ultimately, Dan Quinn. In addition, Quinn’s in-game decisions have cost this team games. If he had called for a field goal on the last play in overtime against the Giants, it’s almost certain the Commanders would have won that game. Most importantly though, he’s supposed to be a defensive head coach, yet the Commanders defense has been atrocious the entire time he’s been here. The defense is better under Jones, but it’s still the 9th worst defense in terms of points allowed. 2 – The Commanders decided not to fire Dan Quinn during their bye. How much longer do you think he has left? Reports have been pretty unanimous that owner Josh Harris would rather not fire a coach mid-season, so I think Dan Quinn should be safe until the end of the season unless it looks like the team has quit on him (which it hasn’t). For all his other faults, Quinn has traditionally been great at maintaining the locker room and keeping players motivated, so I don’t think they’re likely to quit on him. At the same time, I think the team would have to not only win the division, but also win a playoff game to keep Quinn around until next year. So I think the most likely outcome is that Quinn gets fired at the end of the season. 3 – Should Washington sign Jayden Daniels to a contract extension this offseason? Will they? Yes and yes. Although Jayden has made a few high-profile gaffes in situational awareness in recent games, he’s the biggest reason the Commanders are in those games to begin with. He’s adapted to a new (very different) offense really well and is playing from the pocket and even protecting himself better with his choices. He’s showing the passing ability you would want from a QB and is an amazing scrambler to boot. My only major concern with Jayden is whether or not he can stay healthy. However, he missed very few games in college and almost all of his games missed in the NFL (both last year and this year) have been due to his left elbow. I’m hoping he has just had a bit of a complicated left elbow problem that will ultimately get fixed. From what I understand, the ligaments in his left elbow may not have healed from last year, which is a low-probability, but very real risk whenever someone dislocates their elbow. It can be fixed with a replacement of damaged or torn ligaments with cadaver ligaments, which I expect Jayden to get after the season is over. 4 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Commanders’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? In terms of favorable matchups, WR Antonio Williams won his matchups against CB Cooper DeJean in week 1, so I expect that matchup to get exploited again. The Commanders also did a pretty good job in week 1 of limiting the Eagles run game outside of Jalen Hurts scrambles and I expect them to do it again. The Daronte Jones/Brian Flores scheme is particularly good at stopping the run. The biggest matchup against the Commanders is probably the Eagles DL against the Commanders run game. The Commanders have not been able to move the ball effectively on the ground outside of Jayden Daniels’ scrambles. I think the issue is partly run blocking, partly abandoning the run in playcalling, and partly that very little capital has been invested in the RB room. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Commanders currently listed as 5.5-point home favorites, what’s your score prediction? Maybe 23-17 in favor of the Commanders. In Week 1 when these teams played, the Eagles offense relied heavily on Jalen Hurts scrambles to move the ball in critical situations. Tanner McKee doesn’t seem to have the same scrambling ability. The Commanders also let in a lot of interior pressure in that matchup with Nick Allegretti playing at Center. With Lucas Patrick there now, the pass protection should be improved.

title: Eagles Film Preview: Philadelphia’s passing plan must punish the Commanders’ blitz
summary: Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite. I also record a video version for Patreon, where I break down […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 04: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks to pass during the third quarter of the game against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on January 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite . I also record a video version for Patreon , where I break down the plays in greater detail and where you can further support my work. I think the Commanders’ defense is a little better than its numbers suggest. The secondary has some talent, and Daronte Jones can create problems with his pressure packages. However, the lack of a reliable four-man pass rush is killing this defense. For the Eagles, this matchup comes down to whether they can handle the blitz. If they can, there should be opportunities to score. Pass Defense The Commanders are allowing around +0.15 EPA per dropback, ranking 26th, but I don’t think that tells the whole story of their secondary. Looking at the individuals, there is more talent here than those results suggest. The problem is getting everyone to play the same coverage correctly while asking them to hold up for too long. Moving to a new system has brought some predictable communication issues. Some plays each week show defenders with different understandings of how a route should be handled. The red-zone example below looks like Cover 4, but the two sides don’t seem to be operating with the same rules. The underneath defender carries a route on one side, while the cornerback on the other passes a receiver off to nobody. Those are the opportunities the Eagles need to create and exploit. Motion, changes in formation and route combinations that force defenders to exchange responsibilities should be part of the plan. There are capable coverage players here, but making them communicate and adjust gives you a chance to expose the mistakes. If you just line up and throw isolation routes, I’m not sure the Eagles are good enough to win. Washington Defense All22 Thread. 1) Moving to a new system, it's no surprise that they have had a few issues with communication in the secondary. I think they are a talented secondary individually, but they seem to make a few mistakes every week, like the one below, that cost… pic.twitter.com/6wpeMU7Lmu — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 Jones comes from the Brian Flores school of defensive football, and you can see the influence in the disguises and unusual pressure looks. Sometimes it’s fascinating. Sometimes I think they are asking their players to do too much. The Tampa 2 disguise below is a good example. A cornerback follows the receiver across the formation, suggesting man coverage, before the defense rotates into zone. I like that part! However, Frankie Luvu is lined up over the A gap and then has to become the deep middle defender. That is an enormous amount of ground to cover, especially for someone whose best work comes moving toward the quarterback. The disguise is supposed to make the quarterback hesitate, but it can also create a difficult assignment for your own defender. The Eagles need to read the movement after the snap and attack the space before that defender can get there. Tanner McKee will have to distinguish the initial picture from the coverage they actually play. 2) I think they are also guilty of trying to do too much at times. Daronte Jones comes from the Brian Flores school of thought, so expect to see some funky blitz looks. Sometimes, I think they try to do too much. This starts off pretty cool, with the CB following the WR across… pic.twitter.com/TUjRasUANd — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 The biggest issue, though, is the pass rush. They simply don’t generate enough pressure with four. The Commanders blitz on 47.4% of dropbacks, the second-highest rate in the league, yet their overall pressure rate is only 34.4%, ranked 18th. That is a lot of extra rushers for a fairly ordinary amount of disruption. The individual numbers reinforce the film. Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson are the main edge threats, but neither has consistently taken over games by winning his matchup. Daron Payne contributes pressure inside, but this isn’t a front that reliably wrecks the pocket without help. When the initial rush stalls, quarterbacks have time to wait for routes to develop and find the gaps between defenders. That is why I’m reluctant to blame all the passing production on the secondary. There are coverage mistakes, but there are also snaps when the coverage has done enough, and the quarterback is still standing comfortably in the pocket. I do think Quan Martin is a weak link when playing deep. His recognition of crossing routes needs to be better, and he can be slow to react and affect the throw. There are opportunities to manipulate his positioning and attack the space around him. Mike Sainristil has also had a terrible season, but his role has changed. With Trey Amos back, Sainristil played only seven defensive snaps in their last game. The Eagles shouldn’t expect the same opportunities to target him that they had in Week 1. Amos, Rasul Douglas, and Amik Robertson give this secondary a more credible group of corners, and Douglas and Robertson have both shown plenty of good individual coverage. 3) However, the biggest issue this defense has is the pass rush. That's why the defense isn't very good. They simply cannot get pressure with 4, which leads to more blitzes. They give up a lot of passing yards, but I do believe it's down to the pass rush rather than the… pic.twitter.com/lblsoD2Ext — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 The Commanders play a lot of two-high coverage, particularly Cover 2 and Cover 4. Their two-high rate is 69.6%, second highest in the league, and they are predominantly a zone defense. That doesn’t mean the Eagles should abandon the idea of throwing vertically. There are opportunities downfield. The classic Cover 2 hole shot, between the cornerback and the safety along the sideline, has been available. Posts and Go routes have also produced high-value plays against them. The Eagles need to recognize the coverage and take those chances when protection allows. Again, the pass rush is a huge part of the explanation. In the example below, the Commanders send five, and the quarterback still gets a beautiful pocket. You can debate the spacing in the secondary, but at some point somebody up front has to make the quarterback uncomfortable. 4) They play a lot of two-high coverages, especially Cover 2 and Cover 4. They give up the sideline on the classic 'hole' shot between the safety and cornerback a lot, but I still look at the pass rush here rather than the secondary. Washington sends 5, and you could not have a… pic.twitter.com/8z9j1o8Jfd — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 This defense is at its best when it blitzes. Extra pressure gives them a better chance to disrupt the play before the coverage is stretched. If I were in the Commanders’ defensive meeting this week, I would plan to blitz the hell out of the Eagles. I would make this offense prove it can identify the pressure and consistently get the ball to the right place. Given the Eagles’ problems answering pressure this season, I would be stunned if the Commanders didn’t lean heavily into that approach. I think we see a 50%+ blitz rate. This will not be like the Cowboys game. Expect overloads and defenders dropping from unexpected places. An edge defender showing rush can become an underneath coverage player, while a linebacker or defensive back replaces him. The offensive line, quarterback, and receivers need to understand the same answer. Getting the protection right is only part of the job if nobody is…

title: Eagles Film Preview: Commanders’ offense gives Philadelphia’s defense a chance to bounce back
summary: Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite. I also record a video version for Patreon, where I break down […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Zack Baun #53 of the Philadelphia Eagles tackles Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders in the second quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite . I also record a video version for Patreon , where I break down the plays in greater detail and where you can further support my work. The Commanders have a decent offense and a very good young quarterback, but I came away wondering how much more Jayden Daniels could do with better support. Injuries have depleted the talent around Daniels, so the Eagles aren’t facing Washington at their best. For this preview, I focused my film study on the four games Daniels played. Pass Game Remember all the offseason discussion about the Commanders becoming an under-center offense? Well, that hasn’t really happened. David Blough has introduced more of it than we saw under Kliff Kingsbury, but the Commanders still operate from under center on only around 27% of their plays. More importantly, they don’t look particularly good doing it. This offense looks far more comfortable in shotgun and empty, spreading the defense out and letting Daniels see what is happening in front of him. It sounds familiar, doesn’t it?! The lack of production from under center is pretty striking. Looking through their passing plays, I found no explosive completions of 20-plus yards from under center and only one under-center throw that generated at least +1 EPA. The intended relationship between the run game and the play-action passing game just hasn’t produced enough. They will show some interesting receiver insert action and crossing routes behind linebackers, but the under-center menu is heavily tilted toward runs and play action. They barely ever just drop back and throw. Defenses aren’t being asked to defend a particularly broad range of possibilities. Sound familiar?! (On a serious note, I want to write an offseason piece about young OC’s trying to force QB’s under center when it doesn’t suit them, because I think it’s a theme of this season). Washington' Offense All22 Thread. 1) After losing Terry McLaurin for the season, this is a team without a great deal of weapons. Stefon Diggs is their best weapon, and the Eagles already know how much of a threat he can be. They move Diggs around everywhere, and he's still an… pic.twitter.com/dV8oKkh9Wc — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 Stefon Diggs is the biggest remaining receiving threat. The Eagles already know how much trouble he can cause after the first meeting. He remains an outstanding route runner, and the Commanders move him around to find favorable matchups. He’s spent a lot of time in the slot, but I wouldn’t expect him to stay in one place all evening. His ability to change pace, manipulate leverage, and separate gives Daniels a dependable option in an offense that badly needs one. McLaurin’s absence makes the rest of the receiver rotation much more important. Antonio Williams should get more opportunities, and there are some encouraging examples of him working on choice routes and intermediate concepts. However, I would also keep an eye on Treylon Burks. He doesn’t get a huge number of targets, but I thought he looked pretty good in the games I watched. He can get downfield, threaten vertically, and make plays on crossing routes. I loved Burks coming out of college, so there is absolutely some bias here! Still, there is talent to work with, and this offense needs somebody to take on a bigger role. 2) Treylon Burks doesn't get a lot of targets, but he's actually looked pretty good in the games I've watched. He was a 1st-round pick for a reason, and he can get downfield and win vertically. They love these crossing routes, and Daniels normally excels at throwing them.… pic.twitter.com/9qrGA7ZSjs — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 The receivers benefit from playing with a quarterback who is much more advanced than the “one read and run” label that athletic quarterbacks inevitably get. Daniels wants to win from the pocket. He will stand in against pressure and release the ball before a receiver has finished his break. This opposite-hash comeback to Williams below is an excellent example. That throw requires anticipation, timing, and confidence in where the receiver will be. It’s a fantastic throw from a very good young quarterback. I do think there are stretches when Daniels is a little too conservative, particularly early in games. Kurt Warner has highlighted that, and I agree to an extent. However, watching the second half against the 49ers shows what he can do when he starts letting it rip. He also had a few accuracy misses in the games I watched, so I wouldn’t describe every aspect of his passing as consistently excellent. But the quality of his better plays is obvious. 3) Speaking of Williams! This is an outstanding throw from Daniels. Opposite-hash comeback with anticipation. Phew, He's an excellent young quarterback. Because of his running ability, many wrongly assume he's a 1-read, run-only QB. He can run, but he wants to win from the… pic.twitter.com/LLu3tOcxVG — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 The thing that impressed me most was how quickly Daniels eliminates what isn’t available. You regularly see him start on one side, recognize that the defense has taken it away, and work back across the field within the timing of the play. He isn’t automatically looking for an escape route when the first read is covered. He can get to his backside routes and deliver the ball with anticipation. That matters for the Eagles’ linebackers because the Commanders like attacking the middle of the field with crossing and dig routes. Daniels is comfortable finding those windows, and Chig Okonkwo gives him another receiving option inside. The linebackers can’t chase the first underneath route they see or get pulled too far forward by a run fake. 4) The thing that impressed me more than anything about Daniels was his ability to eliminate what isn't there quickly. He gets through his progressions very quickly for a young QB. He does this very frequently. He can eliminate what isn't there (you can see him start right here)… pic.twitter.com/cjiCMftDy9 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 However, the passing game has a significant weakness: its answers to pressure. There are too many plays when the protection is stressed, and the routes don’t give Daniels an accessible immediate answer. Overload pressures, particularly bringing four defenders from one side, have caused repeated problems. The offense can end up asking the quarterback to survive while receivers are still working downfield. This is something I want Vic Fangio to attack. We haven’t seen enough of those aggressive overload looks from the Eagles, and this matchup makes sense to mix them in. The Commanders have taken 14 sacks as a team, with eight coming against blitzes and eight coming on third down. Obvious passing situations and pressure have caused real problems. 5) However, Daniels and the whole offense have a massive problem. They are struggling against the blitz big time, as many offenses are this year. They just don't seem to have answers built in against pressure. Even when they do, Daniels doesn't always take them. Here's the… pic.twitter.com/3RvBFmpyOT — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 29, 2026 Daniels has to take some responsibility too. It would be too generous to blame every pressure failure on Blough. There are snaps when a quick throw is available, and Daniels doesn’t get to it quickly enough. In the example below, he spends too long considering the vertical route…

title: Eagles News: Philadelphia has reportedly told teams that Moro Ojomo is not available for trade
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I don’t buy that the Eagles won’t trade Moro Ojomo and actually plan to re-sign him instead. This reporting reads to me like Howie Roseman outwardly maintaining that stance in hopes that other teams will increase their offers for the impending […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Moro Ojomo #97 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I don’t buy that the Eagles won’t trade Moro Ojomo and actually plan to re-sign him instead. This reporting reads to me like Howie Roseman outwardly maintaining that stance in hopes that other teams will increase their offers for the impending free agent defensive tackle. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Albert Breer: How Two Former Roommates Put the Jeffery Simmons Trade Together – SI Philadelphia Eagles — The Eagles have gotten calls on DT Moro Ojomo, a rising star in a contract year. And that makes sense, given that the team has already paid Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis at his position. Still, the team has told others that Ojomo is not available, and has at least given off the vibe that it’ll try to re-sign him, despite having Carter and Davis already on big deals. That said, other contract-year players like Hollywood Brown, Tariq Woolen and Dallas Goedert could be had. A Saquon Barkley trade seems less likely, especially with Barkley banged up. Eagles Injury Report: Saquon Barkley among key players missing from practice again – BGN Barkley is tracking to miss Sunday’s game. If he can’t play, the Eagles are left with one healthy running back on the active roster: Jaydon Blue. Blue was called up from the practice squad on Wednesday. Playing for the Dallas Cowboys as a rookie last season, Blue logged 38 carries for 129 rushing yards (3.4 average) in addition to one reception for five receiving yards. The Eagles also have Elijah Mitchell, whom the team temporarily elevated to be available to play in Week 7, on the practice squad. Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell. Not exactly the most inspiring backfield for the Eagles to work with! Fantasy football start/sit advice for Week 8 at QB, RB, WR, TE – SB Nation Start — Dallas Goedert, Eagles vs. Commanders — The Eagles are hard to trust, but Goedert gets an excellent matchup here against the Commanders. On the season they’ve allowed the second-most touchdowns, the fifth-most yards and the second-most fantasy points to the position. In Week 1 Goedert caught 4-of-5 targets for 77 yards and two touchdowns against this same team. That was with Jalen Hurts of course, but Tanner McKee is targeting Goedert, as he has 17 receptions over their last three games. Unfortunately those receptions haven’t led to a lot of fantasy scoring, but this week I like his chances to find the end zone. Eagles-Commanders preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice At center, the Commanders cut Tyler Biadasz this summer. Biadasz certainly wasn’t a world-beater but was a solid enough starting center. They then moved Nick Allegretti to center, full-time. Allegretti wasn’t really even a good guard (or a starting one at that), and yet the Commanders opted to put more responsibility on his plate. That was ill-advised. Allegretti missed time during training camp, played poorly during the regular season, and has since been replaced by 33-year-old Lucas Patrick. At RT, 2025 first-round pick Josh Conerly has cut down significantly on his sacks allowed. He has been an improved player. Sam Cosmi is a good RG. This is a bad offensive line, but it might not matter since the Eagles have failed to pressure opposing quarterbacks. As noted above, they have just 8 sacks as a team. Only one team has fewer. Game Review – DAL 38, PHI 21 – Iggles Blitz Tanner McKee seemed more confident and aggressive. The coaches had a better gameplan for him and it gave McKee a better chance of being successful. He should continue to improve as he gets more experience. If he plays the rest of the season we should have a good idea of whether he’s worth bringing back to be the backup QB. I know the current version of him isn’t a guy you’d want, but I do think he’ll get better. As far as him ever developing into a future starter, I think that ship has sailed. My biggest frustration with him on Monday night was decision-making and accuracy. There were times when he had good opportunities available and went elsewhere. Worse was him missing some open guys. McKee must get better with his footwork and mechanics to improve his accuracy. He also needs to be smarter about situational football. McKee did draw defenders offside on two plays. NFL Week 8 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips – ESPN Betting insight: Since 2000, home favorites off a bye are 1-9-1 ATS against teams on short rest after Monday night. Washington’s defense gives Philadelphia a chance despite the injuries. McKee keeps finding Dallas Goedert, and the Commanders struggle against TEs. They also allow touchdowns on 81.8% of red zone trips. I don’t trust Washington to pull away from this depleted Eagles offense. Saquon Barkley on the trade block? What an Eagles sell-off could look like – The Athletic Buyer’s perspective: A running back who is approaching 30 is risky, even one as good as Barkley, who has dealt with injuries this season. His production may have peaked in 2024, during his 2,000-yard season. Still, Barkley’s contract mitigates some of the risk for a potential buyer. He only has $2.5 million guaranteed in 2027. A buyer could view Barkley as a rental for the rest of this year, then cut him in the offseason before his option bonus is due Sept. 1. If Barkley is healthy, he could be a difference-maker for a contender that needs backfield help. The Vikings are one possible team. […] Seller’s perspective: Trading Barkley guts the locker room of its most (available) influential voice on offense. That’s worth considering for a team trying to identify its next generation of leaders. However, Barkley is battling the health challenges he wanted to defy at age 29. Barkley’s stinger, hamstring and back injuries raise red flags. If the Eagles trade Barkley, they can avoid $52.4 million tied up in future option bonuses. Do the Eagles think Barkley’s production in 2027 and 2028 will be more valuable than the investments they could make otherwise? After Dreadful Cowboys Loss, Where Do Eagles Go From Here? Answering Philly’s Biggest Qs – FOX Sports So the idea that Sirianni is safe just because of his stellar record doesn’t hold up to scrutiny, especially since two of those years felt like wasted chances in Philadelphia. And don’t forget, there was some thought he might have been in danger after the Eagles’ first-round exit last year. “They don’t tolerate failure there,” the NFL executive told me. “It feels like every year they don’t win a title, they’re at least thinking about firing their coach. And if you’re about to start over anyway, this might be the perfect time to change it all.” “I never got the impression that they loved him there anyway,” the scout added. “You can’t argue with winning, though. But once that’s gone, all bets are off.” NFL Week 8 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com Why Dan picked the Commanders: Things are getting worse at a troubling clip for Nick Sirianni’s Eagles, who were once 2-0. They have the league’s second-longest active losing streak (five games) and a -745 differential in total yards (second-worst in the NFL and worst by the Eagles through seven games since 1999). Yes, they have entered worst of the century levels of bad, at least by their standards. The Commanders didn’t win in October, either, but they enjoy a significant rest advantage entering Week 8. Washington is coming off a bye, while Philadelphia is playing on a short week after being blown out by the Cowboys on Monday night. Dan Quinn should have ample time to get his players ready to kick a division rival when it’s down. Then again, the following from NFL Research makes me wonder if the Commanders can…

title: Eagles Injury Report: Saquon Barkley among key players missing from practice again
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 8 game against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Barkley is tracking to miss Sunday’s game. If […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 26: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley #26 looks on during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 8 game against the Washington Commanders. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Barkley is tracking to miss Sunday’s game. If he can’t play, the Eagles are left with one healthy running back on the active roster: Jaydon Blue. Blue was called up from the practice squad on Wednesday. Playing for the Dallas Cowboys as a rookie last season, Blue logged 38 carries for 129 rushing yards (3.4 average) in addition to one reception for five receiving yards. The Eagles also have Elijah Mitchell, whom the team temporarily elevated to be available to play in Week 7, on the practice squad. Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell. Not exactly the most inspiring backfield for the Eagles to work with! Smitty and Wicks are tracking to miss another game after also being unavailable in Week 7. With these two potentially out and Covey unlikely to play, the Eagles are down to the following wide receivers: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. They also have three practice squad receivers: Erik Ezukanma, Xavier Gipson, and the newly signed Quentin Skinner. Campbell is track to miss Sunday’s game after getting banged up in Week 7. Look for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to start next to Zack Baun. Jones is also set to miss Sunday’s game, leaving the Eagles without their top backup cornerback on the outside. The Eagles listed six players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Michael Carter II, Nolan Smith, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Moro Ojomo, and Marcus Epps. Smith was listed as limited for the second day in a row. He has a chance to return after missing Week 7 due to a concussion. Carter II also has a chance to play for the first time since getting injured in Week 5. Greenard, Hunt, and Ojomo were also listed as limited for the second day in a row. Guessing they’ll be able to play, albeit at less than 100%. Epps is a new addition to the report with his injury description listed as “jaw/concussion evaluation.” He apparently got banged up during Thursday’s practice. Epps began the season as the safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel packages but was then relegated to special teams duty only after struggling on defense. The Eagles listed eight players under FULL PARTICIPATION: Zack Baun, Landon Dickerson, Dallas Goedert, Drew Kendall, Tyler Steen, Arnold Ebiketie, Smael Mondon, and Jakorian Bennett. Baun, Dickerson, Goedert, Kendall, Steen, and Ebiketie were all listed as full participants for the second day in a row. They’ll play on Sunday. Bennett was also full go again but he’s still on injured reserve. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to activate him to the roster if they want him to suit up against Washington. If not, he’ll remain on IR in his 21-day practice window that will soon be closing. Mondon was upgraded from limited on Wednesday to full on Thursday. Treylon Burks, who is now WR3 with Terry McLaurin out for the season, was downgraded from limited to DNP. The Commanders are already weak at the pivot, so, that’s not an ideal development for them. title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 8 Edition
summary: Now that Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys scores a touchdown against Cooper DeJean #33 of the Philadelphia Eagles during a game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 8 NFL POWER RANKINGS 1 – Kansas City Chiefs (Last Week: 1) – The Chiefs got dominated; they didn’t even enter the red zone once. Seems like more of an anomalous loss than it is a sign of more struggles to come, though. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 2) – As KC can attest to, it’s hard to remain undefeated. The 49ers’ injuries caught up to them in a loss to Atlanta. 3 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 3) – The Bills return from their bye to host the Ravens. Big chance for Buffalo to put a potential playoff threat in a bigger hole. 4 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 4) – The Vikings are undefeated … and they deserve credit for reaching the point of being the league’s only lossless team. But, let’s be real, they’re just not as scary as some of the other top teams. Will be very interesting to see how Minny fares against Detroit this weekend. If they win that one, they’ll have to be taken a bit more seriously. 5 – Chicago Bears (LW: 5) – The Bears are a real threat to be the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoff picture. Even more so after trading for Jeffery Simmons. That’s a much-needed boost for Chicago’s defensive line. 6 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 6) – Mike Macdonald outcoached Andy Reid in Seattle’s dominant defensive effort. Funny enough, the reigning Super Bowl champions wouldn’t qualify for the playoffs if the season ended today, which it doesn’t. But there’s reason to believe they’re going to be in the dance. 7 – Detroit Lions (LW: 8) – The Lions can’t claim to be the team to beat in the NFC North if they don’t beat the Vikings in Detroit on Sunday. 8 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 10) – The Bengals have the NFL’s fifth-best point differential as Joe Burrow is completing 71.7% (!) of his passes this season for a 110.4 passer rating. Cincy also ranks second overall in DVOA. They shouldn’t be slept on. 9 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 9) – The Jags are returning from their bye to host the Colts, who traded away some of their best players this week. Failing to win this game would be pretty unserious behavior. 10 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 7) – Lamar Jackson’s return comes at a crucial time with the Ravens set to take on the Bills. They can’t really afford a loss here in an ultra-competitive AFC North. 11 – New England Patriots (LW: 11) – A.J. Brown is now expected to miss more time due to injury. He just hasn’t looked right. 12 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 12) – After beating the Raiders, the Rams have a chance to go on a winning streak with the Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals up next ahead of their bye. We’ll see if they can actually stabilize or not. 13 – Denver Broncos (LW: 15) – The Broncos are a middling team and there isn’t much interesting to say about them. 14 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 17) – The good news for the Cowboys is that they avoided a season-ending loss to the Eagles. The bad news for the Cowboys is that a lot of their underlying issues were still on display in Philly. 15 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 13) – The Raiders’ 3-0 start feels like a long time ago now after four straight losses. Going to be time to see Fernando Mendoza sooner than later. They should absolutely be looking to trade Kirk Cousins ahead of the deadline. 16 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 16) – Green Bay is an average team. They fit perfectly here in the middle. 17 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 18) – The Browns continue to defy expectations while leading the AFC North. Todd Monken is doing what good coaches do by maximizing the talent he’s been given to work with. 18 – New York Giants (LW: 20) – This Giants team deserves major credit; they were 10.5-point road underdogs to a Texans team that looked to be on the upswing after a rough start. And they went out and beat Houston. Regardless of what happens moving forward, the J.J. McCarthy trade is already a win for New York. 19 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 14) – Baker Mayfield only had 64 passing yards against a Panthers team that lost by 30 points. That’s not a very good sign for Carolina’s outlook. 20 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 21) – The Steelers have won three in a row, albeit some of the league’s least threatening teams. Will be interesting to see how they fare in a rematch against the Browns after previously losing to Cleveland. 21 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 23) – The Falcons are the NFL’s weirdest team. Not really sure what to expect from them on a weekly basis. High highs and low lows. 22 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 26) – It previously looked like the Bucs were left for dead but they’re still alive in a weak NFC South. Tampa has yet to lose a division game this season. 23 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 19) – The Saints are 2-5 entering their bye. Kellen Moore is 8-16 since being hired last year. 24 – Houston Texans (LW: 22) – The Texans are 2-5 overall … but they’re 2-1 in division games, which is important. They’re on life support but it’s too soon to bury them entirely. 25 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 24) – Stick a fork in the Eagles; they’re cooked. This team has lost five straight games and no one will be surprised if the losses continue to pile up. Things have been trending in the wrong direction since last year; Nick Sirianni’s club is 5-10 in their last 15 games. 26 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 25) – Kudos to the Colts for being honest about themselves (unlike they were around this time last year when they traded for Sauce Gardner) and realizing they need to be sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline. 27 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 28) – The Cardinals have oddly owned the Cowboys for some time now. We’ll see if they can keep it up with a win over Dallas this weekend. 28 – Washington Commanders (LW: 29) – The Commanders return from their bye to host the reeling Eagles, who are coming off a Monday night game. If Washington can’t capitalize on this rest advantage and deliver on Amik Robertson’s guarantee that the Commanders will beat the Eagles , they’ll be 1-5-1 ahead of games against the Rams, Giants, and Bengals. In other words, Sunday night is a must-win for Washington. 29 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 32) – The Dolphins are on the board with a win! 30 – New York Jets (LW: 27) – Aaron Glenn is giving the Jets a coaching disadvantage. 31 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 30) – Cam Ward has thrown more interceptions (5) than touchdown passes (4) this season. I think it’s safe to say he’s probably not the long-term answer. 32 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 31) – The Bolts stand alone as the NFL’s only winless team. Their first victory might not come until … Week 11 against the Jets?

title: Eagles News: Jalen Carter says he’s not playing “to what the fans want, even though it don’t really matter what they want”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Carter spoke to reporters on Wednesday after previously declining to answer questions after Monday night’s loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Wasn’t a great look for him to dodge the media after a no-show performance by the defense. Carter clearly isn’t […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts against the Carolina Panthers during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jalen Carter spoke to reporters on Wednesday after previously declining to answer questions after Monday night’s loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Wasn’t a great look for him to dodge the media after a no-show performance by the defense. Carter clearly isn’t a “trash” player but he’s certainly not living up to the expectations that come with being the highest-paid interior defensive lineman in the NFL. It’s not hard to understand how he could be frustrated, especially while playing through a hairline fracture in his wrist. But I’m not sure including this line about fan expectations is very productive. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … What will it take for Jalen Carter to dominate more consistently? – NBCSP How does Carter think he’s playing? “I think ya’ll ask me this every year and I say trash,” Carter said. “So trash. I think you asked me this last year and the year before and I gave you the same answer. So trash. Not to my expectations and I guess not to what the fans want, even though it don’t really matter what they want.” Carter isn’t trash, obviously. No one thinks that. He’s a great young talent who needs to turn into a consistently great player. The Eagles’ lousy season has been full of what-ifs. Let’s answer some of them. – Inquirer What if the Eagles hadn’t extended Jalen Carter’s contract before this season? In July, the Eagles made Carter the highest-paid defensive tackle in the NFL, handing him a four-year deal worth as much as $160 million. Much was made of how long it took the two sides to reach this agreement — it was announced within 24 hours of the start of training camp — but in reality, the Eagles signed Carter as soon as they could. He was eligible for a new contract after his third NFL season, and he had finished his third NFL season. Now, Carter is so talented — and the Eagles invested so much in him, trading up to draft him with the No. 9 overall pick in 2023 — that one could make a good case that they had no choice but to sign him. They weren’t going to let him walk away in free agency in a couple of years, and if he had an outstanding 2026, it would have been only more expensive to sign him. But aside from one game, that 19-17 loss to Jacksonville in London on Oct. 11, he has not been outstanding, and through his first three seasons, he has been genuinely great for, what, a season-and-a-half? For the first nine weeks of 2023 and all of 2024? What’s more, from his spitting incident last season to his refusal to take public accountability for his and the defense’s subpar performances this season, he has shown few signs if any that he’s maturing into the on-field game-wrecker and off-field leader the Eagles need him to be. Had the Eagles waited to give him the extension, if he were still playing now on his rookie contract, would they be getting a better, more motivated Carter? If they had been more patient, might they have reconsidered letting Milton Williams — who in New England has been every bit as good as Carter, if not better — sign elsewhere? Commanders cornerback guarantees Washington will beat the Eagles in Week 8 – BGN Well, if it’s bulletin-board material that will help the Philadelphia Eagles win a football game to snap their five-game losing streak, the Washington Commanders just gave them some. Speaking after practice on Wednesday, Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson guaranteed that his team will beat the Eagles. Ten hypothetical NFL trade deadline deals that could swing the Super Bowl race – The Athletic 4) DT Moro Ojomo to the Bills. Compensation: Third-round pick. After missing out on Buckner, the Bills could make a splash for a young defensive tackle with loads of potential. Last season, when Ojomo started nine games, he finished with six sacks. He’s just 25, and he could be even more effective in a system like Jim Leonhard’s that gives him freedom to get upfield more often. The Eagles already gave Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter big extensions, so they likely would let Ojomo walk after the season. With their season falling apart, the wise move would be to trade Ojomo, who could be a game-changer for the Bills as a run stuffer and interior pass rusher. He also fits into Buffalo’s 3-4 scheme. Pairing Ojomo with budding star Deone Walker would be a move for this season and the future. NFL QB rankings, Week 8: Joe Burrow, Caleb Williams hit season high; Patrick Mahomes slides – NFL.com 25) Tanner McKee found some success early against the Cowboys’ leaky defense on Monday night, but he couldn’t sustain the production long enough to keep up with the Dallas offense. It’s still clear he’s an inexperienced backup, but he’s playing with an injury-ravaged cast that lowers the ceiling for the entire offense. The Longest Autumn – PHLY Eagles I know Howie Roseman understands what needs to happen to this roster. This is an organization facing difficult decisions, and those decisions have to be made. But the fascinating question now isn’t simply who stays and who goes. It’s how we find meaning in the rest of this season? How do we remain invested when the stakes that once consumed our Sundays are suddenly gone? Because I don’t want to give up football in October. I don’t want to spend the next three months pretending to care about the gutters. I want to care about the Birds. And today, that’s what we’re going to figure out. How do you survive the longest autumn? NFL Told Saquon Barkley to Divest Polymarket Stake – Front Office Sports Saquon Barkley was forced to divest his equity stake in Polymarket because NFL players are not allowed to invest in or endorse gambling or prediction-market companies under league rules, the Eagles running back told Front Office Sports. A profile of Barkley revealed last September that Polymarket was among his start-up investments. But at some point between then and this past summer, the league told players they are not allowed to have financial interests in prediction-market platforms. “I am not in that right now,” Barkley told FOS. “I am not allowed to be in that.” How will the Giants resolve their quarterback ‘problem’ if J.J. McCarthy continues to play well? – Big Blue View The question is: Which quarterback is better, and what should the Giants do with the one who is not the answer to that question? Originally I thought there was a chance the Giants might flip McCarthy to a contending team in the other conference before the trade deadline (which is two days after the Giants’ next game, in Philadelphia). Now I can’t imagine that happening unless McCarthy and the Giants lay such a big egg in Philly that it changes the team’s view of him. Flaws and flash carry the Cowboys past the Eagles – Blogging The Boys The Dallas Cowboys delivered a performance against the Philadelphia Eagles that was both encouraging and concerning, showcasing their offensive potential and their lingering bad habits on defense. While a 17-point win over a bitter divisional rival is always pleasing, a closer look at the film shows a team still trying to completely put it all together. Let’s highlight some specific elements that jumped out at us after further review. While Philadelphia’s defense ranks 31st with a 28.7% pressure rate, the Commanders’ offensive line is allowing pressure 39.9% of the time. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Wednesday in advance of their Week 8 game against the Washington Commanders. Note that this report is an estimation because the team held a walkthrough in lieu of a normal practice. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Barkley is listed with hamstring and back injuries. He was clearly in discomfort while trying to gut it out and play on Monday night. Perhaps the Eagles are just managing him to try to get him to Sunday. But it seems like he might be in danger of missing the game. We’ll learn more about his outlook on Thursday, when the Eagles will hold their first real practice of the week. Smitty and Wicks might be in danger missing their second straight game. The Eagles could be without their top two wide receivers once again. Speaking on Wednesday, Vic Fangio noted that Campbell “came up a little bit lame” during Monday night’s game. If he has to miss time, it’ll be Jeremiah Trotter Jr. starting next to Zack Baun. Trot Jr. had already been eating into Campbell’s playing time anyway. Covey got banged up on the first play of the game in Week 7. Seems like he might miss some time due to a knee injury. Look for Makai Lemon to return punts. Jones apparently got hurt on Monday night. If he can’t play, the Eagles will be without their top backup cornerback option on the outside. The Eagles listed six players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, Jonathan Greenard, Moro Ojomo, Michael Carter II, and Smael Mondon. Nolan Smith might be able to return to the field in Week 8 after missing Week 7 due to a concussion. With the Eagles banged up at edge rusher, the team could really use him out there. Hunt and Greenard clearly played at less than 100% in Week 7 based on their relatively low snap counts . Guessing they might be similarly limited again in Week 8. Ojomo was previously listed on the report with an abdomen injury. Now he’s listed with a neck injury. Guessing he’ll be able to play this weekend but his snaps might be more limited than usual. Carter II hasn’t played since getting banged up in Week 5. Prior to getting hurt, he had overtaken Marcus Epps as the safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel packages. We’ll see if he reclaims that role or if the Eagles will stick with Kenny Moore II there. (MC2 vs. KM2.) Mondon is a new addition to the report with a knee injury. If Campbell can’t play, Mondon will be the top backup behind Baun and Trot Jr. The Eagles listed seven players under FULL PARTICIPATION: Zack Baun, Landon Dickerson, Dallas Goedert, Drew Kendall, Tyler Steen, Arnold Ebiketie, and Jakorian Bennett. Baun, Dickerson, Goedert, Kendall, Steen, and Ebiketie should all be good to go against the Commanders. Bennett is still in his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. We’ll see if the Eagles activate him from IR or not. He’s out for the season. Quinyon Mitchell won’t get the chance to erase him like he usually does. Coming off their bye, Washington was without three players on Wednesday: No. 2 receiver Stefon Diggs, starting defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw, and No. 2 tight end John Bates.
